vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes ksupa sparshane as an unaccented final-stem root belonging to Tudadi that behaves regularly without vowel guna before Sarvadhatuka affixes: ksupati, akshupat. It is semantically equivalent to sprisha but classified distinctly within Tudadi.

meanings.English: to touch, to come into contact with

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sphuṭ' expresses the action of bursting, breaking open, or blooming. In simple active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes something opening up or splitting on its own (like a flower blooming or an egg breaking open). In the causative form (sphoṭayati), an external agent causes an object to crack, split, or blow up.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Present indicative, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: In the morning, the flower blooms.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Ṇic pratyaya, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to burst or breaks something open
scenarios.example_english: The boy bursts the balloon.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'sphuṭir' in Tudadi is listed with the sense 'bhedane' (breaking, bursting, opening). Since it is marked with an 'ir' anubandha (ir-it), it optionally takes the 'aṅ' substitute for 'cli' in the aorist (luṅ), yielding forms such as 'asphuṭat' alongside standard formations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'sphuṭir bhedane' as denoting fracture, splitting, or expanding manifestation. When taking the regular Tudadi vikarana 'śa', the root vowel does not undergo guṇa in srvadhātuka affixes (sphuṭati), but undergoes guṇa in causative and certain ārdhadhātuka contexts (sphoṭayati, sphoṭaḥ).

meanings.English: to burst, split open, expand, or bloom

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sic' means to sprinkle, pour, moisten, or irrigate. As a member of the Tudadi class, it inserts a nasal sound (num-agama) yielding 'siñc' in the present tense. It can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (siñcati) and Atmanepada (siñcate). When used with the causative affix, it becomes 'secayati' (causes to water or irrigate).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), Parasmaipada, 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The gardener waters the plants with water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (causative), Lat lakara, Parasmaipada, 3rd person singular
scenarios.meaning: Causes to irrigate / gets someone to water
scenarios.example_english: The farmer causes his son to irrigate the farm.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'ṣica kṣaraṇe' belongs to Tudadi-gana and is characterized as Ubhayapadi and Anit. By the sutra 'śe mucādīnām' (7.1.59), it receives the intermediate num-agama before the sarvadhatuka affix 'śa', resulting in forms such as siñcati and siñcate. In lit-lakara and other ardhadhatuka contexts, gunation applies optionally based on general phonetic rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'ṣica' in the sense of emission or moistening (kṣaraṇaṃ sravaṇam sekaśca). Combined with upasargas such as 'abhi', it conveys ritual consecration (abhiṣiñcati - to crown/anoint), while with 'ni' or 'pra' it designates continuous showering or pouring.

meanings.English: To sprinkle, water, pour out, moisten, irrigate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chup' means 'to touch' or 'to feel by physical contact'. In the standard active voice (Parasmaipada), the subject performs the act of touching an object. When modified into the causative form (ṇijanta), it conveys making or allowing someone to touch something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (present active indicative, lat lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The child touches the delicate flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇijanta (causative present indicative)
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother has the child touch the water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'chupa saṁsparśane' belongs to Tudadi gana. It takes the unaccented 'śa' vikarana without guna of the penultimate short vowel in sarvadhatuka affixes, yielding the present form 'chupati'. It is categorized primarily as anit and parasmaipadi.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines the root in the sense of tactile contact (saṁsparśana). It conjugates regularly in Tudadi as chupati, forming the perfect cuccopa, noting traditional accents and anit phonological behavior.

meanings.English: to touch, to feel, to contact

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'muc' means to release, let go, discharge, or set free. Since it is Tudadi-gana and takes the 'num' augment before the consonant endings in the present stem, it forms 'muñcati' in Parasmaipada and 'muñcate' in Atmanepada. When used in the causative form (nic), it becomes 'mocayati', meaning 'causes someone to release' or 'liberates/frees'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active voice (Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The archer shoots (releases) an arrow.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative active (Nic pratyaya, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The king frees (releases) the prisoner from bondage.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mucḷ' is designated in the sense of 'mocane' (freeing, discharging, untying). Being marked with irit/l-it characteristics in traditional parsing, it takes the 'num' agama by 'she mucadinām' giving the base 'muñc-'. It is Ubhayapadi and Anit.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'mucḷ mocane' within the group of Tudadi roots receiving the intermediate nasal augment (num). It operates transitively in shedding, discharging, untying, and liberating.

meanings.English: to release, liberate, loosen, discharge
meanings.Bengali: mukto kora, chere dewa, mukti dewa

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vid' in the 6th class (Tudadi-gana) signifies three main actions: experiencing consciousness/perceiving, communicating or narrating, and dwelling or residing. Because it belongs to the Tudadi class, it takes the thematic affix 'śa' without vowel strengthening (guna), yielding 'vidati'. When used with causative or communicative affixes, it strengthens to 'vedayati' to mean 'making known' or 'informing'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Active Voice), Lat lakara (Present Tense), Tudadi vikarana 'sa'
scenarios.example_english: The sage resides in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative / Prayojaka (Nic pratyaya), Lat lakara
scenarios.example_english: The student informs the teacher of the entire incident.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Under 'vida cetanākhyānanivāseṣu', Madhava explains that this root operates in three specific semantic spheres: cetana (feeling, consciousness, or perception), ākhyāna (speaking, declaring, or narrating), and nivāsa (dwelling or staying). Belonging to the Tudadi group, it takes the 'śa' pratyaya in sarvadhatuka contexts and avoids guna modification in the basic present stem, forming 'vidati'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin highlights the distinction between this Tudadi root and other homophonous roots such as 'vida jñāne' (Adadi) and 'vidḹ lābhe' (Tudadi with num-agama). He confirms the three distinct applications—cetana, ākhyāna, and nivāsa—and illustrates the basic thematic conjugation 'vidati'.

meanings.English: to perceive, to experience consciousness, to narrate or inform, to dwell
meanings.Hindi: anubhav karna, batana ya soochit karna, nivas karna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root snih belongs to the Tudadi class and means to feel love, care, or affection for someone. Because it takes the class marker 'sa' (a) without vowel strengthening in the present tense, it forms 'snihati'. When used causatively with the nic affix, it means 'to make affectionate' or 'to lubricate/smoothen', forming 'snehayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi gana (sa-pratyaya), Lat lakara, prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The mother feels deep affection for her son.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (nic-pratyaya), Lat lakara, prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: He softens and endears the heart with love.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root snih is categorized under Tudadi in the sense of priti (affection/fondness). By the application of the vikarna sa, the stem does not undergo guna in sarvadhatuka, yielding snihati. In ardhadhatuka environments, forms vary according to vet/it options.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes shniha pritau as a Tudadi parasmaipadi root signifying attachment or love. It undergoes standard sa-vikarna in the present system yielding snihati, distinguishing it morphologically from the Divadi class snihyati.

meanings.English: to feel affection, to love, to be fond of, to be moist/smooth
meanings.Hindi: sneh karna, prem karna, lagav hona
meanings.French: aimer, eprouver de l affection, cherir

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣup' expresses the action of trembling, shaking, or slight movement. Beloging to the Tudadi group (6th class), it takes the thematic conjugational marker 'śa' (which remains as 'a' and prevents guna strengthening of the root vowel 'u'). Thus, 'kṣup + a + ti' forms 'kṣupati'. In causative constructions with 'ṇic', guna occurs to give 'kṣopayati' meaning 'causes to tremble' or 'shakes something'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The tender leaf of the tree trembles due to the force of the wind.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya), Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to shake, agitates, or stirs up
scenarios.example_english: The fierce storm-wind causes the branches of the tree to shake.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṣupa sañcalane' is enumerated among the Parasmaipada roots of Tudadi gana. Being followed by the Sarvadhatuka class affix 'śa' which is marked with 'ś' (and hence acts as 'ṅit' per standard rules), it does not undergo guna of the penultimate short vowel 'u' in the four sarvadhatuka tenses/moods, yielding forms like kṣupati, akṣupat, kṣupet, and kṣupatu. In ardhadhatuka forms like Lit, it produces cukṣopa, cukṣupatuḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'kṣupa sañcalane' as denoting movement and trembling (calana-artha). Following sphura and sphula in the classical listing, it remains Parasmaipadi and Anit in standard primary tenses, producing simple thematic conjugations without internal vowel modification in the present stem.

meanings.English: to shake, to tremble, to vibrate, to move slightly

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root sphut means to bloom, blossom, burst open, or become clearly visible. In its simple present form (sphutati), it describes a flower opening or something bursting naturally on its own. When used with a causative affix (sphoṭayati), it means someone actively breaks, pops, bursts, or reveals something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi gana vikaranashabda (śa-pratyaya)
scenarios.example_english: The lotus blossoms in the garden.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Preshana / Hetuman (Causative ṇic-pratyaya)
scenarios.meaning: causes to burst / pops / breaks open
scenarios.example_english: The boy pops the balloon.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root sphutir is defined under Tudadi-gana in the sense of vikasana (blooming, expanding, opening). It takes the vikarana pratyaya sha without guna of the stem vowel in the sarvadhatuka environment, generating the primary finite form sphutati. In the causative operation with nic, guna applies to yield sphoṭayati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin categorizes sphutir as vikasane (to expand, break open, or manifest). He notes the formation of nominal derivatives such as sphuta (clear, evident) and sphota (bursting, explosion, or manifest sound concept in grammar), and records standard lakara inflections like pusphuta in liti and sphutitaha in kta-pratyaya.

meanings.English: To blossom, to bloom, to burst open, to become clear

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root pracch means to ask, question, or inquire. In the present tense, the root undergoes samprasarana along with the Tudadi class marker -sa-, transforming into 'prcchati'. Because it is a dvikarmaka (two-object) verb, you can mention both the person being asked and the question/topic being asked as direct accusative objects.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The student asks the teacher a question.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Karmani prayoga (passive voice), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The student is asked the way by the teacher.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: praccha jnipsayam. Tudadi-gana. Jnanecchayam vartate. Samprasaranena 'prcchati' iti rupam sidhyati. Akathitanca iti sutrena dvikarmakatvam bhavati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: praccha jnipsayam. Jnipsa jnaptum iccha praśna ityarthah. Sa-pratyaye ca grahi-jyadi-sutrena samprasaranam.

meanings.English: to ask, inquire, interrogate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root bhrasj means to fry, roast, or parch. Falling in the Tudadi gana with the vikaranapratyaya sa, its consonant cluster undergoes samprasarana and dental-palatal shifts to yield forms like bhrijjati and bhrijjate. Being an Ubhayapadi root, it can take Parasmaipada endings when the action is general, or Atmanepada endings when the action directly benefits the performer.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Tudadi (sa) Parasmaipada kartari prayoga (3rd person singular present)
scenarios.meaning: He or she roasts / fries (grains or food).
scenarios.example_english: The cook roasts the chickpeas.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Tudadi (sa) Atmanepada kartari prayoga (3rd person singular present)
scenarios.meaning: He or she roasts / fries for oneself.
scenarios.example_english: The farmer roasts grains for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: bhrasja pake. Tudadih ubhayapadah anit. Grahijyavayavyadhivasi-vicascravasprcchibhrasjatinamiti samprasaranam bhavati. Rlasya ca dvitvam. Bhrijjati bhrijjate ityadi rupani sidhyanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: bhrasja pake. Tudatvat sa-pratyaye bhrasjo rasanayositi bhrijjadesah samprasarananca vidhiyate. Bhrijjati bhrijjate.

meanings.English: to roast, fry, parch

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'viṣ' means to pervade, spread throughout, or encompass. Belongs to the Tudadi group where it forms active forms like 'viṣati'. In the causative (Nic) form, it means to cause to spread or wrap around.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Active, Lat Lakara, Tudadi Sa-vikarana)
scenarios.example_english: The fragrance pervades the entire house.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic Pratyaya (Causative, Lat Lakara)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to encompass, wraps, or surrounds
scenarios.example_english: The mother wraps the child with a cloth.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root viṣḷ is listed in Tudadi gana in the sense of vyapti (all-pervasion and extension). Because of the marker 'ḷ', it is Anit and conjugated as viṣati in the present tense.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes viṣḷ vyāptau as belonging to the sixth class taking the Sa-vikarana without Guna in the Sarvadhatuka affixes, forming viṣati to denote encompassing or pervading.

meanings.English: to pervade, encompass, extend throughout

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'spṛś' means to touch, feel, or contact. It belongs to the 6th verb class (Tudadi), which adds an unaccented 'a' (śa-pratyaya) without strengthening the vowel 'ṛ' into 'ar' in the present tense (giving 'spṛśati' instead of 'sparśati'). In the causative form, it means to make someone touch or to apply/smear, conjugated with -ayati as 'sparśayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice, present tense, simple base)
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the soft flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic-pratyaya (causative voice, present tense)
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother makes the child touch the moon (symbolically reaches out).

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that spṛś takes the śa-vikarana of Tudadi without guna in Sarvadhatuka affixes, forming spṛśati. In Ardhadhatuka forms, guna occurs optionally or obligatorily per standard rules, yielding sparṣṭum or spraṣṭum, and in the lṛt (future) it yields sprakṣyati or sparkṣyati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains spṛśá saṃsparśane as physical contact or touching. He details the specific sandhi and phonological permutations involving vocalic 'ṛ' and the final palatal sibilant 'ś' when followed by Ardhadhatuka consonants (such as ta-pratyaya giving spṛṣṭa).

meanings.English: to touch, to feel, to perceive by touch

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'truh' means to hurt, injure, or destroy. In the present tense, it takes the standard Tudadi conjugation suffix 'śa' (a) without vowel strengthening, forming 'truhati'. When used causatively with 'ṇic', it becomes 'trohayati' meaning 'causes to hurt' or 'destroys'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, laṭ lakāra (present active)
scenarios.example_english: The tiger injures the deer.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic pratyaya (causative active)
scenarios.example_english: The king causes the enemy to be crushed by the troops.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root truha belongs to the tudādi-gaṇa and denotes hiṃsā (harm, injury, or killing). It is parasmaipadi and aniṭ, taking the vikarana 'śa' in sārvadhātuka environments without guṇa to the penultimate vowel, producing truhati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines truha in the sense of hiṃsā (violence or destruction). It operates as a transitive verb taking an accusative object, following standard class 6 parasmaipada paradigms.

meanings.English: to injure, harm, hurt, kill
meanings.Bengali: hingsā karā, āghāta karā, badha karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kuc' means to contract, shrink, bend, or curl up. In simple active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes something shrinking or curling inward naturally. When used with a causative affix (Nic), it means to cause something to contract or bend.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: Due to cold, the leaf curls up.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic pratyaya, kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to shrink / makes something contract
scenarios.example_english: The heat causes the leaf to shrink.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kuca sankocane - Tudadi parasmaipadi set. The root conveys the sense of shrinking or contraction. It takes the shat-pratyaya (sha) in sarvadhatuka contexts, yielding kucati without guna due to the nit-vat nature of sha.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kuca sankoce - Listed among the tudadi class denoting inward bending or shrinkage. Forms kucati, cukoca, kucita.

meanings.English: to shrink, to contract, to curl, to bend

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛt' means 'to cut' or 'to divide'. In the Tudadi class, it receives a nasal augment (num-agama) before the present tense marker 'sa', forming 'kṛntati' (cuts). When used in the causative form with the affix 'nic', it changes to 'kartayati' meaning 'causes to cut' or 'gets something cut'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (present tense, 3rd person singular with num-agama)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer cuts the grass.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇijanta prayoga (causative present tense, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: causes to cut / has someone cut
scenarios.example_english: The master gets the tree cut.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṛtī cchedane. tudādir aniṭ parasmaibhāṣī. mucāditvāt śa-pratyaye pare num-āgamaḥ bhavati, tena 'kṛntati' iti rūpaṃ sidhyati. liṭi 'cakarta', luṭi 'kartā', lṛṭi 'kartsyati' ityādīni rūpāṇi bhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṛtī cchedane. mucādipāṭhāt num. kṛntati. cakarta, cecṛtatuḥ. chedanaṃ dvidhākaranam ityarthaḥ.

meanings.English: to cut, sever, divide, split

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lī' means to cling to, embrace, adhere, hide, or melt/dissolve into something. In the Tudadi class with Atmanepada endings, it expresses clinging or merging intimately into a base or disappearing into a hiding place. In causative forms, it conveys making someone or something melt, dissolve, or attach.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana (Atmanepada)
scenarios.example_english: The honeybee clings to the flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: Heat causes the clarified butter to melt.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'līṅ' is placed in Tudadi gana with the semantic marker 'shleshane' (clinging, adhering, embracing, dissolving). Being anudatta-it, it takes Atmanepada affixes. With the vikarana 'sha', the penultimate long vowel remains intact, yielding 'līyate'. In lit lakara, it forms 'lile' and 'lilyate'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'līṅ shleshane' as an intransitive root denoting close adhesion or dissolution into a substrate. It is anit in primary conjugations, taking s-aorist with Atmanepada endings like 'alishta'.

meanings.English: to cling, adhere, melt, dissolve, hide
meanings.Bengali: lege thaka, gole jaoya, lukiye thaka
meanings.German: haften, schmelzen, sich auflosen, sich verstecken
meanings.French: adherer, fondre, se dissoudre, se cacher

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sphul' belongs to the 6th group of verbs (Tudadi-gana) and means to blossom, open up, burst forth, or expand. In its basic form (Parasmaipada), it describes a subject expanding or blooming by itself. When turned into a causative verb using the 'nic' suffix, it means to cause something to expand or to open up forcefully.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), present tense (lat-lakara), third person singular
scenarios.example_english: The flower blooms in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (causative), present tense (lat-lakara), third person singular
scenarios.meaning: causes to open / causes to burst / reveals
scenarios.example_english: The sun causes the lotus to blossom.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti states 'sphula vikasane'. It belongs to the Tudadi class and takes the 'sha' vikaranapratyaya without guna change in the sarvadhatuka stems, yielding 'sphulati'. In the ardhadhatuka forms, guna occurs as applicable, taking the intermediate 'i' augment (set), producing forms like pusphola and spholita.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'sphula vikasane bhedane cha', meaning to expand, bloom, or break forth. Like sphur, it indicates sudden manifestation or unfolding. It is grouped in the Tudadi series with Parasmaipada inflection.

meanings.English: to blossom, to expand, to burst open

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣur' belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi group) and means to scrape, scratch, cut, or shave. In the basic present tense, it takes the class marker 'śa' without initial vowel strengthening, yielding 'kṣurati' (scrapes or cuts). When converted to causative using the 'ṇic' suffix, the vowel undergoes guṇa strengthening, forming 'kṣorayati' (causes to cut or shave).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi class marker 'śa' (lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The barber shaves the hair with a sharp tool.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇijanta) form with guṇa vowel grade (lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The king has his hair shaved by the attendant.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti categorizes 'kṣura' in the Tudadi gana with the semantic attribute 'vilekhane' (in the sense of scratching, shaving, or cutting). Being an unaccented vowel-consonant base in this class, it takes the 'śa' vikarana and retains simple thematic endings (kṣurati). It is marked as seṭ (taking the augment iṭ in non-thematic forms such as kṣoritā and cakṣora).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under the Tudadi section that 'kṣura vilekhane' denotes scraping, furrowing, or cutting off surfaces. The derived noun 'kṣura' specifically signifies an instrument for cutting or shaving (a razor), directly manifesting the root meaning of superficial incision and scraping.

meanings.English: to scrape, shave, cut, or scratch

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'guh' means to hide, conceal, or cover. Being an Ubhayapada root in the Tudadi class, its short 'u' lengthens to 'u' (guh -> guh-) before vowel affixes. In Parasmaipada, it denotes the act of hiding something externally, while in Atmanepada, it often emphasizes self-concealment or keeping a secret within oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana (Kartari)
scenarios.example_english: The boy hides the money in the chest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana (Kartari)
scenarios.example_english: The deer hides itself in the dense forest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: guhū samvarane. svaritetvat ubhayapaditvam. tudadyantargatah 'udano dhatoh' ityadina dirghatvam apadyate. gūhati, gūhate, jugūha, juguhire.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: guhū samvarane chadane ityarthah. guhati guhate. niguhanartham prayujyate.

meanings.English: to conceal, hide, cover

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛt' means 'to cut' or 'to sever'. In the 6th class (Tudādi), it belongs to the 'mucādi' sub-group, which means it receives an extra nasal sound 'n' inside the root before the present tense marker 'śa', turning the base into 'kṛnta-'. In the basic active voice, it expresses the direct act of cutting. When the causative suffix (ṇic) is applied, the vowel undergoes guṇa strengthening to 'ar' without the nasal insert, meaning 'to cause someone to cut' or 'to have something cut'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Tense, Parasmaipada, Lat Lakāra with śa-vikaraṇa and num-āgama)
scenarios.example_english: The boy cuts the paper with a thread.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative Form (Ṇijanta, Parasmaipada, Lat Lakāra)
scenarios.example_english: The gardener causes the branches of the tree to be cut.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṛtī' is listed in the sense of 'chedane' (cutting/division). The final vowel 'ī' is an it-marker. Belongs to the mucādi class within Tudādi, hence by the rule 'śe mucādīnām' (Panini 7.1.59), the root receives the augment 'num' (nasal insert) when followed by the sarvadhātuka affix 'śa', producing the present stem 'kṛnta-'. In non-sarvadhātuka contexts where guṇa is applicable, it becomes 'kart-' (e.g., cakarta, kartitā, kartsyati).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kṛtī chedane' as indicating the physical act of cleaving, cutting, or dividing. He highlights the operation of num-āgama strictly under the śa-pratyaya environment (kṛntati), distinguishing it from 7th class roots and clarifying the absence of the nasal in perfect (cakarta) and desiderative (cikṛtsati/cikartati) formations.

meanings.English: to cut, to divide, to sever, to slice

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'trut' means to break, split, cut, or snap into pieces. In active voice (Kartari Prayoga), it takes Tudadi 'sha' vikarana without guna in Sarvadhatuka tenses (trutati). In the causative (Nic), it means to cause something to break or to snap deliberately (trotayati).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga, Tudadi Gana (sha vikarana), Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The dry tree branch snaps.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic (Causative affix), Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy breaks the thread.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'truta cchedane' belongs to Tudadi gana and is Parasmaipadi. By 'tudantibhyah shah' (3.1.77), the vikaranapratyaya 'sha' is added. Because 'sha' is an apit Nit-vat pratyaya, guna of the penultimate ik-varna does not occur in Sarvadhatuka forms, producing 'trutati'. In Ardhadhatuka environments, guna operates yielding 'atrotit' and 'trotita'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'truta cchedane' signifies dividing, cutting into parts, or snapping. It is set and inflects in Parasmaipada (trutati, tutrota, trotisyati). It is classified alongside roots denoting partition and structural breaking.

meanings.English: to break, to snap, to cut, to split

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'riṣ' belongs to the 6th group (Tudadi gana) and means to harm, hurt, or injure. Because it is in the 6th class, the root vowel 'i' does not undergo guna strengthening before the present tense marker 'a', forming 'riṣati' (he/she harms). When used with the causative suffix Nic, it undergoes guna to become 'reṣayati' (causes to harm or destroy).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Active, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Harms or causes injury to someone
scenarios.example_english: The enemy harms the citizens.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic Pratyaya (Causative, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Causes harm or destruction to someone
scenarios.example_english: The wicked ruler causes harm to all.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Under the Tudadi section, Sayana analyzes 'riṣa hiṃsāyām'. The root takes the standard Tudadi śa-pratyaya where no guna occurs in Sarvadhatuka environments, producing the simple present form 'riṣati'. In Ardhadhatuka forms, it exhibits anit characteristics with regular guna changes, yielding forms like 'rekṣyati' or 'ariṣat'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'riṣa hiṃsāyām' within the group of roots signifying injury and violence. He points out that the base vowel remains light in the present tense (riṣati) and details its application in classical semantic contexts of causing physical harm or affliction.

meanings.English: to harm, to hurt, to injure
meanings.Hindi: himsa karna, chot pahunchana, hani pahunchana
meanings.Bengali: himsa kora, aghat kora, khoti kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chup' means 'to touch'. In its simple present form (Kartari Prayoga), it takes standard 6th-conjugation endings to denote someone touching an object. When modified with the causative suffix (Nic), it shifts meaning to causing someone or something to touch.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Tense, Lat Lakara, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the delicate flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic Pratyaya, Lat Lakara, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_sanskrit: mātā bālasya hastaṃ dīpena chopayati na tu kadācit.
scenarios.example_english: The mother never lets the child's hand touch the flame.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: chupa sparśane | tudādigaṇasthaḥ parasmaipadī anit ca | chupati, cucopa, chopitā/coptā | sparśanam saṃyoga-viśeṣaḥ |
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: chupa sparśane | chupati, chopitaḥ | anit parasmaibhāṣāḥ saṃsparśe vartate |

meanings.English: to touch, to feel

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bhuj' in the 6th class (Tudadi-gana) means to bend, curve, or make crooked. Unlike the 7th-class 'bhuj' which means to eat or protect, this Tudadi root forms 'bhujati' in the basic active voice. When causative affix Nic is added, it becomes 'bhojayati', meaning to cause to bend or crook.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Active Voice), Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The worker bends the iron rod.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (Causative), Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The artisan causes the bow to bend.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: bhuja kautilye. tudadi-parasmaipada-anit. kautilyam vakribhavanam vakriकरणam ca. bhujati, bhugoja, bhoksyati, abhoksit. kta-pratyaye bhugnah iti rupam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: bhuja kautilye. kautilyam kutilabhavo vakribhavanam. bhujati. rug-bhujau tu parasmaipadinau anitau ca.

meanings.English: to bend, to curve, to make crooked

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'riṣ' belongs to the Tudadi class (6th conjugation). Because it takes the Tudadi-specific conjugational sign 'śa', the vowel 'i' is preserved without changing into 'e' (guna) in the present tense, producing 'riṣati'. It denotes the action of injuring, hurting, or harming.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: A righteous person does not harm anyone.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (causative), Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to harm or causes injury to
scenarios.example_english: The demon causes harm to the children.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: riṣa hiṃsāyām. tudādiraniṭ parasmaipadī. śap-apavādaḥ śaḥ, tasmād guṇābhāvaḥ. riṣati, areṣīt ityādi rūpāṇi bhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: riṣa hiṃsāyām. śap-viṣaye śa-pratyayaḥ. aguṇatvāt riṣati iti sidhyati.

meanings.English: to injure, harm, hurt

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'truṭ' belongs to the Tudadi class (6th Gana) and primarily means to snap, break, or be torn apart. In its basic active form (Parasmaipada), it describes something breaking or tearing. When used with the causative affix (ṇic), it shifts the meaning to actively causing something to break or cutting something into pieces.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat-lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The worn-out rope suddenly breaks.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (causative), Kartari prayoga, Lat-lakara, 3rd person singular
scenarios.meaning: causes to break / cuts / snaps something
scenarios.example_english: The monkey breaks the branch of the tree.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti places 'truṭa chedane' within the kuṭādi subgroup of the Tudadi gana. Being in kuṭādi, it undergoes standard Tudadi vikarana (śa) without medial guna in sarvadhatuka affixes (truṭati). In ardhadhatuka affixes with it-agama, guna takes place optionally or per general rules (troṭiṣyati, atroṭīt).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'truṭa' conveys division, separation, or cutting (chedana / bhedana). It is classified under Parasmaipada and is treated as a seṭ root in general conjugational environments outside the basic present stem.

meanings.English: to break, to snap, to be cut or torn

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sic' primarily means to sprinkle, pour, or water plants. When conjugated in Parasmaipada (siñcati), it refers generally to the act of pouring or sprinkling liquid onto an object. In Atmanepada (siñcate), it is used when the fruit of sprinkling directly pertains to oneself or in reflexive/intransitive-like nuances. When the causative affix 'ṇic' is added (secayati), it means causing another person or system to sprinkle or irrigate.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active voice (Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The gardener waters the trees with water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative form (Nic pratyaya, Lat lakara)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to sprinkle or causes to be irrigated
scenarios.example_english: The farmer gets the field irrigated.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: ṣicṛ kṣaraṇe. Tudādi-gaṇa-paṭhitaḥ ubhayapadī anit ca. num-āgamaḥ sarvadhātuke bhavati yena siñcati siñcate iti rūpe sidhyataḥ. kṣaraṇam atra jalādinā secanam abhipretam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: ṣicṛ kṣaraṇe. kṣaraṇaṃ sravaṇaṃ secanaṃ vā. śap-vikaraṇasya apavādaḥ śā-pratyayaḥ, num-āgamaśca. siñcati siñcate, asecat asikta.

meanings.English: to sprinkle, to water, to pour out

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mṛś' belongs to the Tudadi group (Class 6), where the stem vowel 'ṛ' does not get strengthened to 'ar' before the present tense marker 'a', yielding 'mṛśati'. It primarily means to touch or feel physically, but when used with prefixes or in intellectual contexts, it shifts to mean deliberating, examining, or reflecting upon something carefully.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the soft flower with his hand.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga with upasarga 'pari', Lat lakara
scenarios.example_english: The scholar carefully considers the result of the action with logic.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Under 'mṛśa āmarśane' (Tudadi), Sayana explains that āmarśana entails both tactile perception (sparśana) and cognitive deliberation (parāmarśa / vicāra). Because it belongs to Tudadi, the present stem is formed with 'śa' without guna ('mṛśati'). In ardhadhatuka formations, it exhibits forms like mamarśa / mamṛkṣatuḥ in Lit, marṣṭā / mraṣṭā in Lut, and amārṣīt / amrākṣīt in Lun.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'mṛśa āmarśane' as 'āmarśanaṃ saṃsparśo vicāro vā', highlighting its dual scope in physical touch and mental reflection. He details the optional replacement rules and sandhi alternations for sibilant-final roots before jhal affixes.

meanings.English: to touch, to stroke, to reflect, to deliberate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛṣ' means to furrow, plow, or drag. Because it belongs to the Tudadi class and is Ubhayapada, it takes both Parasmaipada (kṛṣati) and Atmanepada (kṛṣate) terminations in the active voice without changing its basic meaning, though Atmanepada can emphasize that the outcome of plowing/pulling directly affects the subject.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Parasmaipada, Lat, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer plows the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (Atmanepada, Lat, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Plows or pulls (for one's own benefit)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer plows the field for his own harvest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṛṣa vilekhane. vilekhanaṁ bhūmeḥ phalādinā dāraṇam. tudāditvāt śaḥ. svariteto 'bhāve 'pi kecidubhayapadatvam icchanti, anye tu parasmaipadinam eva pathanti. aniṭ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṛṣa vilekhane. vilekhanaṁ sīrādinā kṣetradāraṇam. kṛṣati, kṛṣate. halantatvād aniṭ.

meanings.English: to plow, to furrow, to drag, to till

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chid' (chidā~) belonging to the Tudadi class means to kindle, ignite, stimulate, or blaze up. When used in active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes an agent setting something on fire, kindling, or stirring up energy and illumination.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga), Present Tense (Lat Lakara), 3rd Person Singular
scenarios.example_english: The sage kindles the fire of spiritual wisdom.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Past Tense (Lun Lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The sacrificer ignited the sacred fire.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya notes that 'chidā sandīpane' in the Tudadi class indicates illumination, blazing, or stirring up (dīptau, prakāşane). It receives the Tudadi vikarana and retains parasmaipada endings in regular active forms.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'chidā sandīpane' as excitation, inflammation, or the act of lighting/kindling a fire or energy (jvalane, ujjvalīkaraṇe).

meanings.English: to kindle, to ignite, to illuminate, to excite
meanings.Hindi: jalana, sulagana, prakashit karna, uddipta karna

canonical_dhatvartha: hiṁsāyām (to hurt, harm, tear, or injure)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'riś' belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi-gana) and means 'to injure' or 'to tear/harm'. Because it belongs to Tudadi-gana, the stem-marker '-śa-' is added without causing the vowel 'i' to strengthen into 'e' (no guna in the simple present), forming 'riśati'. In the causative form, it takes '-ṇic-' to mean 'causes someone to injure' (reśayati).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat-lakara (Simple Present), Prathama-purusha (3rd person), Ekavacana (singular), Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The tiger tears the body of the deer.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (Causative), Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: Causes to harm / inflicts injury through someone
scenarios.example_english: The enemy causes harm to the friend through others.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'risa himsayam' as an anit, talavya-shantam root within the Tudadi group. By the pratyaya 'sa', the root vowel does not undergo guna in sarvadhatuka affixes, giving the forms risati, risatah, risanti. In lit-lakara it forms riresa, ririsatuh, ririsuh. The krdanta participle is ristah.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'risa himsayam' as conveying violent injury, wounding, or cutting apart. It is parsed identically to rusa himsayam with anit status and parasmaipada endings, giving forms like risati, aresit, and resayati.

meanings.English: to injure, harm, tear, wound
meanings.Bengali: hingsa kora, aghat kora, chire phela

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dṛnph' belongs to the Tudadi class (6th Gana) and means to vex, agitate, or torment someone. It operates in Parasmaipada, taking the sixth gana vikaraṇa 'śa' (which triggers the nasalized stem in present tense forms like 'dṛnphati'). When converted into the causative form (nic), it signifies causing someone to agitate, distress, or disturb another person.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The wicked person distresses the virtuous man.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya), Kartari prayoga, Lat-lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The enemy causes agitation and torment among the citizens.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'dṛnphi utkleshe' is categorized under Tudadi. Being idit (possessing short 'i' as an it marker), the root retains an internal nasal consonant (num-agama), yielding present tense forms such as 'dṛnphati'. Madhava notes its semantic focus specifically on emotional and physical agitation or causing acute distress (utklesha).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin states that 'dṛnphi' is read in the semantic spectrum of causing disturbance and harassment ('utkleshe'). It undergoes standard Tudadi conjugation with 'śa' pratyaya, and retains the nasal infix throughout sarvadhatuka formations.

meanings.English: To torment, to agitate, to distress, to vex
meanings.Bengali: klesha deya, byakul kara, jantrana deya
meanings.French: tourmenter, agiter, causer de la detresse
meanings.Chinese: zhemo, shi ku nao, fan rao

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root dṛt belongs to the Tudadi group and means to respect, honor, or pay regard to someone. When conjugating in the present tense, it receives a special nasal insert (num-agama), transforming the stem into dṛnt-, giving the present-tense form dṛntati (he/she respects). When used with prefixes or causatives, the voice and meaning shift towards honoring or causing someone to regard with care.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The well-behaved student respects the word of the teacher.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Upasarga 'ā' + Atmanepada substitution in the sense of reverence
scenarios.meaning: shows deep reverence / holds in high regard
scenarios.example_english: A noble person honors all virtuous people.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: dṛtī ādare. As part of the five roots starting with kṛt (kṛtādi pañcaka) in Tudadi gana, this root takes the 'num' augment before the Sarvadhatuka affix 'śa', resulting in the operational base dṛnt- and producing the finite active form dṛntati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'dṛtī ādare' as signifying pūjā (worship/honor) and sammāna (respectful regard). It undergoes regular num-agama insertion under the Tudadi class rules, yielding dṛntati in the Parasmaipada active voice.

meanings.English: To respect, to honor, to regard, to care for

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root kṣip means 'to throw', 'to fling', or 'to dispatch'. In the standard active voice (Parasmaipada), it forms kṣipati (he/she throws). When adding the causative suffix (ṇic), it changes to kṣepayati, meaning 'causes to throw' or 'makes someone cast'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Active, Parasmaipada, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy throws a stone into the water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (Causative, Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to throw / makes someone fling
scenarios.example_english: The teacher causes the student to shoot (fling) the arrow.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṣipa preraṇe. tudādi-gaṇasthaḥ, parasmaipadī, anit-kāraḥ. preraṇaṃ preṣaṇam utpādanaṃ kṣepaṇaṃ ca. kṣipati, cikṣepa, kṣepsyati, akṣaipsīt/akṣipat. niraḥ kuṣa-kṣipa-śriyāṃ niṣedho vācyaḥ iti kṣiptvā, kṣiptaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṣipa preraṇe. kṣipati, cikṣepa. kṣepakaḥ, kṣepaṇam. preraṇa-bhāve vartamānaḥ sakarmakaḥ aniṭ ca.

meanings.English: To throw, to cast, to fling, to direct

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root ṛṣ means 'to go', 'to move', or 'to flow'. As a Tudadi class (6th Gana) root, it takes the class marker 'śa' (a), where the root vowel does not undergo guna in the simple present tense, giving the form 'ṛṣati' (he/she goes or flows). In causative forms (Nic), it conveys making someone move, push, or flow.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Simple Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The wind moves along the forest path.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: causes to move / pushes forward / directs
scenarios.example_english: The boatman propels the boat.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes under 'ṛṣa gatau' in Tudadigana that this root is primarily used in the sense of motion (gamana) and approaching (prāpti). Being in Tudadi, 'tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ' applies without guna in Sarvadhatuka environments, producing 'ṛṣati', while Ardhadhatuka forms show standard vriddhi/guna (arṣiṣyati, arṣitum).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini confirms 'ṛṣa' as a Tudadi root denoting 'gatau' (moving, flowing, or reaching). He notes its connection to words denoting flow, sage-like insight (rishi as seer of paths/mantras), and steady progressive movement.

meanings.English: to go, to move, to flow, to push

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛṣ' means to plough, scratch, or pull. In the active voice (Parasmaipada), the agent performs the action of ploughing or pulling directly. When used in the Atmanepada, the action can emphasize a reflexive benefit or involvement. When made causative (Nic pratyaya: karṣayati), it means 'to make someone plough' or 'to cause to drag/attract'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The farmer ploughs the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (Causative), Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The master causes the field to be ploughed by the servant.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that 'krsa vilekhane' belongs to the Tudadi class taking the vikarana 'sa'. It carries the primary sense of furrowing the soil (vilekhana) and pulling/dragging (akarsana). Being anit, it forms past participles such as 'krsta' without intermediate 'i'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'vilekhana' as the action of furrowing or tearing open the earth as with a ploughshare. He also highlights its overlap with the Bhvadi root krs (to draw/attract), where Tudadi krsa takes anudatta/svarita markers permitting ubhayapada usage in particular contexts.

meanings.English: to plough, to furrow, to drag, to draw

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'jri' belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi gana) and expresses the natural process of growing old, wasting away, or decaying over time. In its simple present tense, the root takes the Tudadi vikarna 'sha' and forms 'jriyati' (he/she/it grows old). When used in the causative sense (nic-pratyaya), it becomes 'jrayayati' or 'jarayati', meaning 'to cause to age' or 'to wear down'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara (Present Indicative), Kartari prayoga (Active Voice), Prathama purusha, Eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: With time, the human body grows old and frail.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lan lakara (Past Imperfect), Kartari prayoga (Active Voice), Prathama purusha, Eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The tree dried up and decayed.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti classifies 'jri' under Tudadi gana with the canonical arthapatha 'vayohanau' (loss of vitality or advancing of old age). Due to the Tudadi vikarana 'sha', which is treated as Nit (sarvadhatukam apit), guna of the radical vowel 'i' is blocked by 'kniti cha'. The root undergoes iyam-adesha by 'achi shnushudhrubhrvam yvoriyamuvau', yielding the present form 'jriyati'. It is anit in standard morphological operations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in the Kshiratarangini explains that 'jri' denotes the progressive deterioration of the physical frame and decline of youthful vigor ('vayaso hanih'). He highlights the standard Tudadi formation without radical strengthening in the sarvadhatuka paradigm, confirming the base 'jriyati' as an intransitive verb of state transition.

meanings.English: to grow old, to age, to decay, to waste away
meanings.Hindi: buddha hona, jirna hona, kshina hona
meanings.Bengali: briddha haoya, jirna haoya, khoy paoya

transitivity: Intransitive (Akarmaka) / Transitive (Sakarmaka in certain contexts of movement)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sṛp' means to crawl, creep, or glide smoothly. In the standard present tense (Kartari Prayoga), it takes the Parasmaipada endings to form 'sarpati' (he/she crawls or creeps). When transformed into the causative form (Nic-pratyaya), it becomes 'sarpayati' (causes to crawl or glide).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Present Tense, 3rd Person Singular, Parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The snake glides slowly in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic Pratyaya (Causative, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy slides the toy cart along the ground.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'sṛpḹ' belongs to Tudadi-gana and denotes movement (gati). The vowel 'ḹ' is an it-marker indicating the inclusion of specific aorist alternatives. By regular laghupadha-guna before the Tudadi vikarana 'sa', the base becomes 'sarpa-', producing 'sarpati'. It is anit (devoid of i-agama in non-sarvadhatuka affixes).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'sṛpḹ gatau' under Tudadi-gana. The it-letter ḹ leads to optional forms in the aorist (asṛpat / asrākṣīt). The root fundamentally signifies creeping or gliding motion.

meanings.English: to crawl, to creep, to glide

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rish' means to go, move, or flow. It belongs to the 6th verb class (Tudadi), where the present-tense marker '-a-' (sha-pratyaya) is added to the root without strengthening the vowel into guna, yielding forms like 'rishati'. When used in the causative, it means to cause to go or direct.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, lat-lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The river flows swiftly down from the mountains.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), kartari prayoga, lat-lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The charioteer drives the horse forward.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti confirms that 'risha gatau' belongs to the Tudadi class. Because it receives the sha-vikarana which is anit-nit, guna substitution does not apply to the penultimate ik-vowel in sarvadhatuka contexts, maintaining the vowel 'ri' to form 'rishati'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin analyzes 'risha gatau' as an intransitive root denoting continuous movement or flowing motion, pointing out its anit status in ardhadhatuka operations and parallel semantic behaviors across Vedic and classical usage.

meanings.English: to go, move, flow, or glide

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'diś' primarily signifies granting, bestowing, giving away, or pointing out. In the basic active form (Parasmaipada), it conveys the general act of pointing or giving (e.g., diśati). In the middle voice (Atmanepada), it indicates that the action or its direct outcome is undertaken by or for oneself (diśate). When combined with prefixes like 'upa-' (upadiśati) it shifts to instructing or advising, and with 'ā-' (ādiśati) it means commanding.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: He/she gives, bestows, or points out
scenarios.example_english: The wealthy person bestows charity upon the beggar.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Upasarga 'upa' + Kartari Prayoga (Parasmaipada, Lat lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The teacher instructs the disciple in righteousness.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'diśa atisarjane' belongs to the Tudadi class. The term 'atisarjana' indicates giving (dāna), granting, or showing/pointing out. Being anit and having both Padas (Ubhayapada), it forms 'diśati' and 'diśate' in the present tense with the 'śa' (a) vikaraṇa.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'diśa atisarjane' as signifying surrender, abandonment, or generous granting (atisarjanaṃ dānaṃ visarjanaṃ vā). With varied preverbs like upa, ā, nir, and sam, it yields diverse specialized meanings such as instruction, command, and direction.

meanings.English: to bestow, grant, give away, point out, show
meanings.Hindi: dena, daan dena, nirdesh karna, dikhana

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tur' belongs to the Tudadi class and signifies moving with great haste, rushing, or speeding forward. In simple active sentences (Kartari prayoga), it expresses that the subject is hurrying or running fast toward a destination.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara (present tense), Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The horse rushes swiftly towards the village.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lun lakara (aorist tense), Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The traveler hastened home quickly.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'turi' is listed under the Tudadi group in the semantic sense of 'tvarana' (swiftness, speeding). The final 'i' serves as an it-marker (it-samjna). Being a member of Tudadi-gana, it takes the class sign 'sha' (a) before Sarvadhatuka affixes without initial guna in present forms, producing 'turati'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin analyzes 'turi tvarane' as denoting rapid displacement and exertion in speed. He highlights its presence in early Vedic and classical registers to describe quick motion, contrasting it with roots of ordinary walking.

meanings.English: to hasten, to rush, to make speed, to run quickly
meanings.Hindi: jaldi karna, tvarit gati se chalna, begapoorvak aage badhna
meanings.Bengali: druta gati kora, taratari kora, begavan howa
meanings.German: eilen, sich beeilen, hasten, schnell laufen
meanings.French: se hater, se depecher, courir avec precipitation

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rup' belongs to the 6th class (tudādi-gaṇa) and takes the 'śa' suffix (yielding 'a' without guṇa strengthening in the basic present tense), conjugated in the Parasmaipada voice. It expresses the action of bewildering, confounding, or perturbing the mind.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, laṭ-lakāra, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The illusionist confounds the minds of the people.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic-pratyaya (causative), laṭ-lakāra, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to be confounded / throws into bewilderment
scenarios.example_english: The deceitful speaker causes the audience to be bewildered.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: rupa vimohane - tudādirudāttaḥ parasmaibhāṣaḥ. vimohanaṃ cetaso vyākulatāpādanam. 'tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ' iti śa-vikaraṇe guṇābhāve 'rupati' iti rūpaṃ sidhyati. liṭi ruropa.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: rupa vimohane. vimoho vyākulatvaṃ saṃśayo vā. rupati, ruropa, ropitā. śa-pratyaye guṇābhāvaḥ.

meanings.English: to confound, bewilder, perplex, or disturb the mind
meanings.Russian: sbivat s tolku, privodit v zameshatelstvo, obolshchat

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'piñj' primarily expresses the actions of coloring/painting, joining or connecting elements together, marking/drawing lines, and moving. In simple active voice (Kartari Prayoga), it describes a subject coloring an object or making distinct marks on a surface.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, lat lakara, prathama purusha, eka-vacana (Simple Active Present)
scenarios.example_english: The painter colors the canvas.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (Causative), lat lakara, prathama purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The teacher makes the student color the leaf.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: piñji varṇasaṃdhānavilekhanagatyartheṣu. idittvān num. piñjati. varṇane, saṃyojane, vilekhane, gamane ca asya prayogo bhavati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: piñji varṇasaṃdhānavilekhanagateṣu. idittvān nityannum. piñjati paṭam (varṇayati, lepayati ityarthaḥ).

meanings.English: to color, to paint, to join, to mark or trace

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root pṛc means to join, mix, touch, or come into intimate contact with something. In the 6th class (Tudadi), it conjugates in Parasmaipada to describe an entity coming into contact with or uniting with another object. When used with prefixes like sam (sampṛc), it conveys thorough mingling or association.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The wind contacts and carries the fragrance.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Sam-upasarga with Lat-lakara, bahu-vacana
scenarios.example_english: People mix water thoroughly with milk.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: pṛcī samparke. pṛcītyanidit. aniditāmiti nalopaprāptāvapi iditvānna bhavati. samparkaḥ saṃśleṣaḥ ekībhāvo vā. ayam anit parasmaipadī ca bhavati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: pṛcī samparke. samparko mishrībhāvaḥ saṃbandhaśca. pṛcati ityādi rūpāṇi bhavanti.

meanings.English: to touch, to mix, to join, to come into contact with
meanings.Hindi: sparsha karna, milana, samparka me lana

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root sphur means to throb, twitch, quiver, or flash. When used in normal active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes something pulsing, shining, or twitching on its own. When the causative affix (nic) is added, it means to cause something to throb or to make something flash/manifest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi shashtha-gana (sap replaced by sa)
scenarios.example_english: The eye twitches, indicating good fortune.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (causative) in Kartari prayoga
scenarios.example_english: The poet awakens the emotion in the heart.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: sphura sphurane. tudadi-gane parivrittau sa-pratyaye sphuratiti bhavati. lit-lakare pusphora ityadi rupani sidhyanti. akarmakah ayam dhatu spandane vartate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: sphura sphurane calane spandane ca. sa-pratyaye gunabhavat sphurati. pusphora, sphurita, asphorit iti rupani bhavanti.

meanings.English: To throb, quiver, twitch, or flash

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root ghūrn means to whirl, spin, reel, or stagger. In normal active usage (kartari), it describes someone or something revolving or staggering on its own. When the causative suffix (nic) is added, it means making someone or something spin or whirl.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (simple present, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: When the wind blows, the tree sways and reels.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic-pratyaya (causative present, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: causes to spin or whirls something
scenarios.example_english: The boy whirls the stick around.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains ghūrṇa in the meaning of bhramaṇa (wandering, revolving, or staggering). As a Tudadi root, it takes the vikaraṇa śa (a), forming ghūrṇati and optionally ghūrṇate in ubhayapada contexts with set characteristics in non-conjugational tenses.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines ghūrṇa as denoting circular movement, dizzy reeling, or unsteady agitation (bhramaṇe). It highlights the root's usage in expressing both continuous spinning and wandering motion.

meanings.English: to whirl, roll, stagger, reel, rotate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root spṛś belongs to the Tudadi class and means to touch or make physical contact. In basic active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes an agent directly touching an object. When the causative affix (ṇic) is added, it forms sparśayati, meaning to make someone or something touch or bring two things into contact.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, eka vacana
scenarios.meaning: touches or makes physical contact with
scenarios.example_english: The boy affectionately touches his mother.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇijanta (causative), kartari prayoga, laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, eka vacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch or brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The physician causes the medicine to touch the patient's body part.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that spṛśa belongs to the Tudadi gana, takes the śa-vikaraṇa, and operates in parasmaipada. It is classified as aniṭ. In forms like sṛṣṭa, the vowel does not undergo guṇa before kkit affixes, but in sṛta or future tense sprakṣyati, phonological adaptations with ṣ/kṣ apply systematically.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains spṛśa in the sense of tactile perception and physical reaching. With prefixes such as upa (upaspṛś), it takes specialized ceremonial meanings like ritual ablution or sipping water (ācamana).

meanings.English: to touch, to feel, to perceive by touch

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhu' belongs to the Tudadi class and means to shake, agitate, or cause to tremble. Because it is marked with an indicator 'ñ' (dhuñ), it takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada terminations. In the present tense, the Tudadi vikaraṇa 'a' (sa) triggers the 'uvaṅ' substitute, yielding 'dhuvati' and 'dhuvate'. In causative forms, it takes 'nic' to mean causing someone or something to shake or blow.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The wind shakes the tree.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat lakara (3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: shakes / trembles (often when the fruit of action stays with agent)
scenarios.example_english: The horse shakes its own body.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: dhuñ kampane tudadih ubhayapadi anit. tudatvad a-pratyaye 'aci shnudhatubhruvam yvor iyanuvanau' ity uvanadeshe dhuvati dhuvate iti rupa-siddhih.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: dhuñ kampane. uvaṅadesha-vishaye dhuvati dhuvate. kampanam calanam preranam va.

meanings.English: to shake, agitate, tremble, fan

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣup' belongs to the 6th group of verbs (Tudadi class). In simple present active sentences, it adds the suffix 'a' (śa-vikaraṇa) without strengthening its inner vowel 'u', producing 'kṣupati' (he/she touches). When we make it causative (making someone else touch), the vowel strengthens to 'o' and uses 'ayati', giving 'kṣopayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Simple Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga, Lat Lakara, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy touches the delicate flower.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative Form (Prena / Nic-pratyaya, Lat Lakara, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.meaning: causes to touch / brings into contact
scenarios.example_english: The mother makes the baby touch the leaf.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṣupa sparśane. tudādiḥ parasmaibhāṣaḥ anit. śa-pratyaye upadhāguṇābhāve kṣupati iti rūpam siddhyati. liṭi cukṣopa, luṭi kṣoptā, lṛṭi kṣepsyati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṣupa sparśane. kṣupati, cukṣopa. sparśanam nāma saṁśleṣaḥ sambandho vā. ktvāyām anitvāt kṣuptvā iti bhavati.

meanings.English: to touch, to feel, to come into contact with

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sphul' belongs to the 6th group (Tudadi-gana) and takes Parasmaipada endings. It fundamentally denotes blooming, bursting open, flashing, or flaring up. When used in the simple present tense with the vikaranapratyaya 'sha' (a), it forms 'sphulati' without guna modification of the radical vowel. When converted into a causative (nic) form, the vowel undergoes guna to form 'spholayati', shifting the meaning from 'it blooms/bursts' to 'makes something bloom/burst'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Tudadi-gana vikarana (sha / a), Lat-lakara (Present Tense), Prathama-purusha, Eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The flower blossoms in the garden.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (Causative), Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to blossom, bursts open, or expands
scenarios.example_english: The sunrise causes the lotus to bloom.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'sphula vikasane' within Tudadi-gana. It notes that being an udattopadesha root ending in a consonant, it takes the 'sha' vikarana in sarvadhatuka affixes, remaining without guna in the stem ('sphulati'). In ardhadhatuka forms, it admits the intermediate 'it' augment (set-tva), yielding forms like 'spholita' and 'aspholit'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'sphula vikasane' as conveying unfolding, expansion, and sudden manifestation (sphutikaranam). He highlights the phonetic and semantic kinship between the roots 'sphur' (trembling/flashing), 'sphut' (bursting/cleaving), and 'sphul' (flowering/expanding).

meanings.English: to blossom, expand, burst open, flash, or radiate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rish' belongs to the 6th group (Tudadi gana) and means to flow, go, move, or reach. In standard active voice (Parasmaipada), it describes the natural flowing or moving of something like water or a person going forth. When used in the causative (Nic), it changes to mean causing someone to move or propelling something forward.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga, Lat Lakara, Tudadi-vikarana 'sha')
scenarios.example_english: The river flows swiftly.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya, Lat Lakara)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to move, propels forward, or directs
scenarios.example_english: The wind directs the path.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'rish' with the canonical sense of 'gatau' (movement, flowing). Being in the Tudadi class, it takes the 'sha' vikarana yielding 'rishati' without guna in Sarvadhatuka forms. The root denotes straightforward or rapid motion.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'rishi gatirau' that the root conveys physical moving, gliding, or flowing. It retains the anit characteristics in specific ardhadhatuka operations and follows standard Tudadi morphological rules.

meanings.English: To go, flow, move, glide, or reach

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mruñc' belongs to the 6th class (Tudadi Gana) and conveys the fundamental action of moving, going, or slithering. In basic active usage (Parasmaipada), it describes the subject moving by themselves. When converted into the causative (Nic), the meaning shifts to causing or directing someone or something else to move.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana (Basic Active Kartari)
scenarios.example_english: The deer moves in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic Pratyaya, Lat lakara (Causative Active)
scenarios.example_english: The cowherd causes the cow to move.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mruñcu' is listed under the Tudadi group having the primary semantic designation 'gatyām' (in the sense of movement or going). It forms Parasmaipada finite verbs with the Tudadi vikaraṇa 'śa', yielding standard forms like 'mruñcati' in the present tense, and taking the set augment pattern in relevant non-conjugational tenses.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin categorizes 'mruñcu' among the cluster of movement roots (gatyarthaka dhatus) following 'añcu', 'vañcu', and 'srañcu'. He confirms its morphological behavior as taking unaccented 'śa' affix without penultimate vowel modification in the universal four lakaras.

meanings.English: To go, to move, to glide

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root dṛphi means to string together, arrange, or compose (such as flowers into a garland or words into literature). Because it has an 'i' marker (idit), it receives a nasal 'm' insertion in its stem, conjugating in the 6th class (Tudadi) as dṛmphati.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (present indicative, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The poet composes a text.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic-pratyaya (causative, present indicative, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: causes to string together / gets composed
scenarios.example_english: The teacher makes the students compose verses.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: dṛphi saṃdarbhe. saṃdarbho nāma granthanam. idittvāt sarvatra num bhavati. dṛmphati, dadṛmpha, dṛmphitā, dṛmphiṣyati. seṭ-paratvāt kṛdanteṣu dṛmphitaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: dṛphi saṃdarbhe. saṃdarbhaḥ saṃgrahaṇam granthanam ca. dṛmphati. idittvān num, tena m-kāra-yutam rūpam jāyate.

meanings.English: to string together, to weave, to compose

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root tubh belongs to the 6th verb group (Tudadi gana) and carries the primary meaning 'to hurt, strike, or kill' (himsayam). In standard present tense (kartari prayoga), it takes the 'sa' (a) vikaranapratyaya and Parasmaipada endings without strengthening the root vowel, forming 'tubhati'. When converted to causative (nic), it forms 'tobhayati' ('causes someone to hurt or strike').

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The hunter hurts the deer in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative voice), lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The master causes the servant to strike the enemy.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root tubha~ is taught under the Tudadi gana in the sense of violence and injury (himsarthaka). As it belongs to the tudadi class, the pratyaya 'sa' applies in sarvadhatuka contexts, giving the un-lengthened radical form 'tubhati'. In it-lopa operations, the terminal vowel markers are dropped.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin categorizes tubha~ among the roots denoting himsana (injury/hurting). The inflection maintains non-guna stem behavior in standard four sarvadhatuka tenses under Tudadi rules, deriving tubhati, atubhat, and tubhet.

meanings.English: to hurt, injure, strike, or kill
meanings.Bengali: aghat kara, himsa kara, badh kara

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'ksip' means to throw, cast, or send forth. Because it belongs to the Tudadi class, it takes the class infix 'sa' (a), producing the base 'ksipa-' rather than strengthening the internal vowel 'i' in simple present forms (yielding 'ksipati'). When used with causative affixes (Nic), it signifies causing someone to throw or dispatching an object through an agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The boy throws the ball.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (causative voice), Lat lakara, 3rd person singular
scenarios.meaning: Causes to throw / makes someone cast
scenarios.example_english: The king causes the archer to shoot the arrow.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'ksipa prerane' is listed under the Tudadi gana with anudatta it-marker. It is anit and functions as Parasmaipadi. Being in Tudadi, it takes the 'sa' vikarana without guna of the laghupadha vowel in sarvadhatuka affixes, forming 'ksipati', 'ksipatah', 'ksipanti'. In lit, it becomes 'ciksepa'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'ksip prerane' signifies the act of propelling, throwing, or directing something outward with force. It forms anit participles like 'ksiptah' in kta pratyaya and 'ksiptva' in ktva pratyaya.

meanings.English: to throw, cast, propel, send forth

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛṣ' means to furrow, plough, pull, or drag. Because it belongs to the Tudadi gana, it adds the intermediate 'śa' vikaraṇa without guṇa strengthening of the root vowel in the present tense (forming kṛṣati or kṛṣate). As an Ubhayapadi root, it can take Parasmaipada endings when the action is directed outwardly or generally, and Atmanepada endings when the fruit of the action is intended for oneself. When used with the causative affix (Nic), it changes to 'karṣayati', meaning to cause to pull or to drag.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The farmer ploughs the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic-pratyaya), Kartari prayoga, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/She causes to drag, attracts, or torments.
scenarios.example_english: The moon attracts the ocean.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṛṣa vilekhane. Tudadir anudatta it ubhayapadavidhiḥ. Vilekhanam atra bhūmyādeḥ phālādinā dāraṇam, ākarṣaṇaṃ ca. 'tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ' iti śa-pratyayaḥ. Sārvadhātuke na guṇaḥ, kṛṣati kṛṣate. Liti cakāra cakṛṣe. Luni akrākṣīt akṛkṣata.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṛṣa vilekhane. Tudādir anit ubhayato-bhāṣā. Vilekhanaṃ vidāraṇam ākarṣaṇaṃ ca. Krṣati, kṛṣate. Kṛṣṭaḥ, kṛṣiḥ iti rūpāṇi sidhyanti.

meanings.English: to plough, to furrow, to drag, to pull, to draw

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rish' means to flow, glide, move steadily, or reach a destination. In the 6th class (Tudadi), it adds 'a' (sha-pratyaya) directly to the root to form 'rishati'. When turned into a causative (nic), it changes vowel quality to 'arshayati', meaning 'causes to flow' or 'directs forward'. From this root comes the word 'rishi' (the seer who approaches or perceives truth).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The river flows towards the ocean.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Prena (causative/nic), Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: Causes to move, directs, or channels
scenarios.example_english: The farmer directs the water into the farm.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti classifies 'rishi' under Tudadi gana denoting 'gati' (movement) and 'prapana' (attainment/reaching). Being marked with 'i', it forms 'rishati' in sarvadhatuka tenses and exhibits standard guna transformations in ardhadhatuka environments.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'rishi gatiprapanayo' indicating dynamic forward motion and obtaining. He emphasizes the etymological link between this root and nominal derivatives representing guided motion, celestial bodies, and Vedic seers (rishis) who reach beyond ordinary perception.

meanings.English: to move, to flow, to glide, to reach
meanings.Tamil: paayndhu sel, payanam sei, sendru aday
meanings.Chinese: liu dong, qian jin, dao da

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mas' belongs to the 6th class (Tudādi gaṇa) and signifies undergoing change, transformation, or ripening into a new state. Because it is used in Parasmaipada, it directly expresses the subject undergoing a transformation over time or maturing naturally.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ-lakāra (Present Tense, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: With time, the fruit transforms into sweet.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Ṇic-pratyaya (Causative Present Tense)
scenarios.example_english: Warmth transforms milk into curd.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'masī' has an anubandha 'ī' indicating it belongs to the aniṭ group. It is read in the sense of 'pariṇāma' (transformation or natural evolution of form and state). In Tudādi, it takes the vikaraṇa 'őa' yielding 'masati' without guṇa.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'masī pariṇāme' as indicating mutation, development, or maturing of an entity into an altered condition (avasthāntarāpatti).

meanings.English: to transform, to change state, to mature

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'riś' belongs to the Tudadi group and inherently means to injure, tear, or hurt. Because it takes the Tudadi class affix 'śa' (which does not cause guna strengthening of the root vowel), the basic present tense form is 'riśati'. In causative (Nic) formations, it gains the sense of causing someone to injure or tear, yielding 'reśayati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular with Tudadi 'śa' pratyaya
scenarios.example_english: The tiger injures (or tears) the deer.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic pratyaya), Lat lakara, 3rd person singular with guna strengthening
scenarios.example_english: The enemy causes the brothers to hurt each other.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti identifies 'riśa hiṁsāyām' under the Tudadi class.
