vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṝñ hiṃsāyām - kryādiḥ, ubhayapadī, aniṭ. kṛṇāti, kṛṇīte. śnā-pratyaye kṛte 'ṛta id dhātoḥ' ityadīnāṃ viśeṣavidhīnām aprasaṅge 'hrasvasya guṇaḥ' ityādividhiḥ prayujyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṝñ hiṃsāyām. hiṃsanaṃ pīḍanaṃ vadho vā. kṛṇāti kṛṇīte. kīrṇaḥ. kryādāvayam ubhayatobhāṣaḥ.

meanings.English: to injure, to hurt, to harm, to kill
meanings.Bengali: aghat kara, himsa kara, badh kara
meanings.French: blesser, faire du mal, endommager, tuer

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'gṝ' belongs to the Kryadi (9th) class and means 'to swallow', 'to ingest', or 'to devour'. When conjugated in the active voice (Parasmaipada) with the 9th class marker 'sna', it expresses the act of taking in or consuming food or substances. In the causative form, it signifies making someone swallow or feed.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Active Voice), Present Tense (Lat lakara), 3rd Person Singular
scenarios.example_english: The python swallows the small deer.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (Nic), Active Voice, Present Tense (Lat lakara), 3rd Person Singular
scenarios.example_english: The mother makes the child swallow the medicine.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'gṝ' is listed in the Kryadi gana in the sense of 'nigaraṇa' (swallowing or ingesting). In the Sarvadhatuka conjugations with the affix 'sna', the radical vowel undergoes characteristic transformations yielding forms such as gṛṇāti or girati/gilati across cross-references.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'gṝ nigaraṇe' as the physical act of swallowing or devouring into the throat and stomach, noting its regular Parasmaipada terminations in the 9th conjugation.

meanings.English: to swallow, ingest, devour

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root vrīñ belongs to the 9th class (Kryadi) and means to choose, select, or cover. Being an Ubhayapada verb ending in the marker ñ, it takes Parasmaipada endings when the fruit of the action is general or directed elsewhere, and Atmanepada endings when the action directly benefits or reflects back upon the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada active voice (prathama puruṣa ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The teacher selects the student based on merit.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada middle voice (prathama puruṣa ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The king selects the finest gem for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: vrīñ varaṇe kryādiḥ ubhayapadī aniṭ. vrīṇāti vrīṇīte iti rūpe bhavataḥ. liti vivrāya vivriye. luti vretā. lṛti vreṣyati vreṣyate. varaṇa-kriyāyām āvaraṇārthe api ayam prayujyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: vrīñ varaṇe. vrīṇāti vrīṇīte. vrīti kryādipāṭhād aniṭtvam. vivrāya vivriye. ihāvaraṇam api grahītavyam.

meanings.English: to choose, to select, to cover

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pṝñ' belongs to the 9th class (kryādi gaṇa) and takes the infix 'nā' (śnā-pratyaya), shortening its vowel to form 'pṛṇāti' in Parasmaipada and 'pṛṇīte' in Ātmanepada. When an action of nourishing or filling is performed, Parasmaipada is generally used when the primary benefit goes outward, whereas Ātmanepada is used when the result directly relates to oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, 3rd Person Singular (laṭ-lakāra), kryādi-śnā pratyaya
scenarios.example_english: The father nourishes the needy person with charity.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Ātmanepada, 3rd Person Singular (laṭ-lakāra), ñit-ubhayapada
scenarios.example_english: The sage satisfies his own self with wisdom.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'pṝñ' is defined as 'pālanapūraṇayoḥ' (in the sense of nourishing/protecting and filling). Being marked with anubandha 'ñ', it is an Ubhayapada root. In the present tense (laṭ) and other sarvadhātuka environments of kryādi gaṇa, it takes the śnā affix, shortening the long vowel by relevant sūtras to yield pṛṇāti and pṛṇīte.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'pṝñ pālanapūraṇayoḥ' as a dual-meaning root of the 9th class denoting both preservation/maintenance (pālana) and filling/completing (pūraṇa). In non-conjugational tenses and with standard ardhadhātuka affixes, it behaves with seṭ characteristics according to the standard rules of kryādi.

meanings.English: to nourish, to protect, to fill
meanings.Bengali: palon kora, poshon kora, purno kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root stambh means to stop, block, support, or make something rigid and motionless. In active voice, it describes the act of restraining or propping up an object. With causative affixes, it conveys causing something or someone to become paralyzed, arrested, or firmly held in place.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat (Present Indicative), Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana via Kryadi affix sna
scenarios.example_english: The dam stops the massive flow of water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic (Causative), Lat, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: Causes to become paralyzed or completely halted
scenarios.example_english: The sorcerer paralyzes the enemy with a spell.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root stambhu is listed in the Kryadi gana in the sense of pratibandha (obstruction, arrest, or propping up). By the special sutra 'stambhu-stumbhu-skambhu-skumbhu-dhrubhyah snusca', this root optionally takes the vikaranapratyaya snu in addition to standard sna, resulting in alternate forms like stabhnati and stabhnoti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains stambhu as holding fast or fixing firmly. The root undergoes loss of the medial nasal in specific non-sarvadhatuka environments and combines with upasargas like vi, sam, and prati to express stupefaction, thorough obstruction, or stiffening.

meanings.English: To block, to arrest, to prop up, to stiffen, to paralyze
meanings.Hindi: Rokna, thamna, stambhita karna, sahara dena

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bandh' belongs to the 9th class (Kryadi) and means 'to tie', 'to bind', or 'to fasten'. In its basic active form, it takes the class marker 'sna', where the root loses its nasal and becomes 'badhnati'. When a causative suffix (Nic) is added, it forms 'bandhayati', shifting the meaning from performing the action directly to causing or ordering someone else to tie something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The cowherd ties the calf to the tree with a rope.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic-pratyaya (causative), Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, 3rd person singular
scenarios.meaning: Causes to tie / makes someone bind
scenarios.example_english: The king causes the guard to bind the thief.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti classifies 'bandha' under Kryadi with the meaning 'bandhane' (fastening, tying). It details the phonological reduction of the root nasal resulting in 'badhnati' before the Kryadi vikarna 'sna', the loss of the root penultimate nasal in specific weak environments, and the phonetic transformations leading to forms such as 'babandha' in Lit, 'bhantsyati' in Lrt, and 'baddhah' in the Kta-pratyaya.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini glosses 'bandha bandhane' highlighting its anit status and transitive nature. He notes the contraction of the stem in strong and weak conjugational forms ('badhnati', 'badhnitah', 'badhnanti') and the phonological changes in Ardhadhatuka forms, showing the shift of the aspirate and dental sounds into 'banddhum' and 'baddham'.

meanings.English: To bind, to tie, to fasten, to fetter

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root pṝ means to fill, nourish, or protect. As a ninth-class (kryādi) root, it takes the marker 'nā' or 'nī' (śnā-pratyaya) between the root and endings. It can be used in both Parasmaipada (pṛṇāti) when the action is directed outward and Atmanepada (pṛṇīte) when the result reflects on oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice, parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The devotee fills the vessel with water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice, ātmanepada)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer fills his own storehouse with grain.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: pṝñ pālanapūraṇayoḥ. kryādiḥ, ubhayapadī, aniṭ. śnā-pratyaye kṛte 'hrasvo hyākhyātam' ityādinā hrasvatve 'pṛṇāti', 'pṛṇīte' iti rūpe sidhyataḥ. pūraṇe poṣaṇe ca vartate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: pṝñ pālane pūraṇe ca. svaritetvād ubhayapadī. pṛṇāti, pṛṇīte. pālanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ, pūraṇaṃ sampādanam.

meanings.English: to protect, to nourish, to fill, to satisfy

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root jṝ belongs to the 9th class (Kryadi) and signifies the natural process of aging, wearing down, or decaying over time. In its primary active conjugation (Parasmaipada with the class affix śnā), it expresses that a subject itself grows old or deteriorates. When used in causative constructions (Nic), it shifts meaning to causing something to digest, wear out, or consume.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kryadi-gana active present indicative (laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana with śnā pratyaya)
scenarios.example_english: With the passage of time, the human body grows old.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative present indicative (ṇijanta, laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The digestive fire properly digests consumed food.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root jṝ is listed in the Kryadi gana with the meaning vayohānau (loss of youth / aging). Being an ṝ-ending root in this gana, it takes the vikaraṇa śnā. By specific morphophonemic operations (such as substitution of īr/ur by 'ṛtaśca saṃyogādeḥ' and related sutras), forms like jīrṇāti and jīryati (in Divadi) are derived. It is inherently anit in primary conjugations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes jṝ vayohānau in the Kryadi group. It denotes the decay of bodily strength and youth. In non-conjugational past participial formations, the affix kta yields jīrṇaḥ through the regular vocalic change and na-tva transformations.

meanings.English: to grow old, to age, to decay, to wear out
meanings.Hindi: vriddha hona, jīrna hona, kshin hona
meanings.Bengali: briddha haoya, jirna haoya, khoy prapta haoya
meanings.French: vieillir, s user, se decomposer, digerer

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'jyā' means to age, decay, or lose bodily vigor and youth. In the present tense (Kryādi-gaṇa), the root undergoes a special phonological change called saṃprasāraṇa where 'jyā' changes to 'ji-' before taking the class marker '-nā-', forming 'jināti'. In the causative (ṇijanta), it takes the form 'jyāpayati', meaning 'causes to decay or waste away'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara (Present tense, active voice, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: With the passage of time, every body decays and grows old.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇijanta), Lat lakara (Active voice, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: causes to waste away / weakens / deteriorates
scenarios.example_english: The disease weakens his strength and vitality.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: jyā vayohānau. jināti, jinītaḥ, jinanti. jñājanyoriti vā saṃprasāraṇam, halśnaśānoriti dīrghatvam. vayaso hāniḥ vṛddhabhāvaḥ kṣayaḥ vā.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: jyā vayohānau. jināti. vayasaḥ paripākaḥ hāniḥ. 'jyāvayohānau' ityatra saṃprasāraṇena jināti iti rūpam.

meanings.English: to grow old, decay, waste away, lose vigor
meanings.Kannada: vṛddhatva hondu, kṣīṇavāgu, vayassu kaḷedu hōgu
meanings.Hindi: būḍhā honā, kṣīṇa honā, vṛddhāvasthā ko prāpta honā
meanings.Bengali: vṛddha haoyā, kṣaya prāpta haoyā, jīrṇa haoyā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kun' belongs to the Kryadi class (9th conjugation) and takes the vikaraṇa 'śnā', forming 'kunāti' in the present tense. It carries the primary meaning of connecting, binding together, or making a relationship.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present tense (Lat lakara), Third person singular, Active voice (Kartari prayoga)
scenarios.example_english: The weaver connects the threads.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present tense (Lat lakara), Third person plural, Active voice (Kartari prayoga)
scenarios.example_english: The friends connect with one another.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kuna' is listed in Kryadigaṇa with the sense of 'sambandhana' (connection, association, binding). Being parasmaipadi, it receives the class-affix 'śnā' yielding the forms kunāti, kunītaḥ, kunanti in the present tense.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kuna sambandhane' denoting the act of linking or union. The root inflects with the standard Kryadi characteristics, showing lengthening and vowel modifications in appropriate conjugational markers.

meanings.English: to connect, to link, to bind together

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'prī' means to please, to satisfy, or to love. In the 9th class (kryādi), it takes the marker 'nā/nī' (śnā). Being Ubhayapada, you can use Parasmaipada endings (prīṇāti) when the action pleases someone else, or Atmanepada endings (prīṇīte) when the fruit or feeling is mutual or centered on oneself. Adding the causative suffix gives 'prīṇayati' (causes someone to be pleased).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), parasmaipada, 3rd person singular, present tense (laṭ)
scenarios.example_english: Good behavior pleases all people.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), ātmanepada, 3rd person singular, present tense (laṭ)
scenarios.meaning: takes delight in / loves for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The mother affectionately cherishes her own child.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'prīñ' belongs to the kryādi gaṇa, carries an indicatory 'ñ' marking Ubhayapada status, and is classified as aniṭ. It operates in the senses of tarpaṇa (gratification/pleasing) and kānti (affection/love/desire). In the present tense, it receives the śnā vikaraṇa, yielding prīṇāti and prīṇīte, with reduplicated perfect forms piprāya and pipriye.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin analyzes 'prīñ' as expressive of both emotional satisfaction and affection (tṛptau premni ca). It undergoes standard kryādi lengthening and vocalic operations, contrasting with roots of mere eating or physical delight by denoting an inner sense of joy and love.

meanings.English: to please, to gratify, to delight, to love
meanings.Hindi: prasanna karna, tripta karna, prem karna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dabh' belongs to the 9th group (Kryadi Gana) and means 'to deceive, injure, or overpower'. In the basic present tense, it takes the Kryadi marker 'sna' to form 'dabhnāti' in the active voice (Parasmaipada). When used causatively with the suffix 'ṇic', it becomes 'dambhayati' / 'dābhayati', meaning 'causes someone to deceive or harm'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active voice (Kartari Prayoga), Present tense (Lat Lakara, Prathama Purusha Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The deceitful person cheats or injures the enemy.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative form (Nic Pratyaya), Present tense (Lat Lakara)
scenarios.example_english: The king causes his foes to be deceived through an envoy.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes 'dabhā hiṃsāyāṃ dambhe ca'. Being in Kryadi Gana, it receives the vikaraṇa 'śnā' (Pānini 3.1.81). The root is anit, undergoes standard Pāṇinian operations for roots in this class yielding forms such as dabhnāti, dadābha, dabdhum, and dabita / dabdha depending on the context of Vedic and classical usages.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin classifies 'dabhā' among the roots denoting harm, injury, and deception ('hiṃsāyām'). He highlights the morphological alternation between 'dabh-' and nasalized 'dambh-' across various primary derivations and confirms its Parasmaipada and Kryadi-specific conjugation.

meanings.English: To deceive, harm, injure, overpower
meanings.Hindi: Dhokha dena, hinsa karna, kshati pahunchana
meanings.Bengali: Protarona kora, himsha kora, khoti kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lū' means to cut, sever, or reap crops. Since it is marked with a nasalized anudātta-svarita marker (ñ), it is Ubhayapadī: it takes Parasmaipada endings when the fruit of the cutting action benefits someone else, and Ātmanepada endings when it directly benefits the agent. In the 9th class (Kryādi), it takes the marker 'nā' (śnā), forming 'lunāti' and 'lunīte'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, parasmaipada (action done for others)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer cuts the grain in the field (for sale/others).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, ātmanepada (action done for self)
scenarios.example_english: The farmer harvests the grain for his own use.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: lūñ chedane. svaritetvād ubhayatobhāṣā. kryāditvāt śnā-pratyayaḥ. 'svādistrayāṇām' iti hrasvaḥ - lunāti, lunīte. lavitā, lavitum, lūnadhānyaḥ ityādīni rūpāṇi bhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: lūñ chedane. kryādigaṇasthaḥ. chedanam dvidhākaraṇam kṛntanam vā. hrasvatve 'lunāti', 'lunīte'. lavitā, lavatīti prayogāḥ.

meanings.English: to cut, lop, sever, harvest, reap

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṝ' belongs to the 9th conjugation group (Kryadi gana) and means to harm, hurt, or injure. It has an indicator marker 'ñ' (ñit), which allows it to be conjugated in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada depending on whether the fruit of the action is intended for another person or the agent itself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Parasmaipada, 3rd Person Singular, Present Tense)
scenarios.example_english: The hunter harms the deer in the forest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari Prayoga (Atmanepada, 3rd Person Singular, Present Tense)
scenarios.example_english: The wicked person harms himself through anger.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṝñ hiṃsāyām. kryādiḥ ubhayapadī aniṭ. kṛṇāti, kṛṇīte. svāṅgakarme ātmanepadavidhiḥ, paratra parasmaipadam. kīrṇaḥ, kārayati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṝñ hiṃsāyām. śnā-pratyayaḥ. kṛṇāti kṛṇīte ityādi. hiṃsā-viśaraṇārtheṣu pravartate.

meanings.English: To injure, harm, hurt, or kill
meanings.Bengali: Hingsa kora, aghat kora, hotya kora
meanings.French: Blesser, nuire, faire du mal, tuer

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root kṣubh belongs to the 9th class (Kryadi) and expresses the action of shaking, churning, or agitating. By Paninian rule, it optionally takes the class affix snu alongside the regular Kryadi affix sna, yielding distinct forms in the present tense to describe agitating liquids or causing emotional agitation.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kryadi class affix sna (Paninian standard Kryadi present active)
scenarios.example_english: He stirs the milk with a churning rod.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative suffix nic (Prerana / driving agitation)
scenarios.example_english: The powerful wind violently agitates the ocean.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that under the sutra stambhustumbhuskambhuskumbhuksubhyah snusca (3.1.82), the root ksubhu optionally takes the vikarna snu in addition to sna in Kryadi, highlighting its core semantic domain of sancalana (physical or emotional perturbation and stirring).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin analyzes ksubhu as denoting churning or moving forcefully (manthana-sancalana), identifying its phonological stability across the non-conjugational tenses and contrasting it with its intransitive usage in other ganas.

meanings.English: to shake, agitate, churn, or perturb
meanings.Bengali: khubdha kara, noda deoya, manthan kara

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vri' (vrin) means to choose, select, prefer, or solicit. As an Ubhayapada root in the 9th conjugation (Kryadi), it takes the 'sna' (na/ni) class infix. When taking Parasmaipada endings, the action is directed outward or neutrally performed. When taking Atmanepada endings, the choice or selection yields fruit primarily for the subject himself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Lat Lakara
scenarios.example_english: The king selects a qualified minister.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Lat Lakara
scenarios.example_english: The maiden chooses the best groom for herself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'vrin varane' in Kryadiah. The ikara is long and takes the anudatta-it marker indicating Ubhayapada. In the Sarvadhatuka tenses, the affix 'sna' applies, yielding vrinati and vrinite. It undergoes standard gunation in Ardhadhatuka forms without it-agama due to being anit.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'vrin varane' shares semantic space with choose or elect. In Kryadigana, with the application of 'kriyadibhyah sna', the stem becomes vri-na/vri-ni before strong and weak endings respectively, demonstrating both parasmaipada and atmanepada inflectional series.

meanings.English: to choose, select, opt for, screen, or woo
meanings.Bengali: bachhai kara, baran kara, pachhanda kara

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'knu' belongs to the Kryadi class (9th conjugation) and means 'to make a sound' or 'to groan/creak'. Because it has an anubandha 'n' (nit), it can take either Parasmaipada endings (knunati) when the action is general, or Atmanepada endings (knunite) when the fruit of the action relates back to the subject.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana, parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The patient groans in pain.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana, atmanepada (kartrabhipraya)
scenarios.meaning: makes a sound for oneself / hums softly
scenarios.example_english: The singer softly hums to himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: knun sabde. kryadih ubhayapadi anit. sna-pratyaye krite knunati knunite ityadini rupani bhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: knun sabdarthah. nitvad ubhayatobhasah. kshirasvami notes its placement in the non-vocalized sound roots of the ninth gana.

meanings.English: to make a sound, to groan, to hum softly
meanings.Hindi: aawaz karna, karahana, dhimisvar me bolna
meanings.German: einen Laut von sich geben, stohnen, summen

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root pᤱ belongs to the 9th class (Kryādi-gaṇa) and takes the class affix 'nā/nī' (knā), conjugated in Parasmaipada to mean 'to protect', 'to foster', or 'to fill'. When used in its regular active form (pᥑṇāti), the subject directly fills or nourishes something. In causative forms (pūrayati), it commonly conveys causing something to become completely full.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṭ (present tense), prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana, kartari prayoga
scenarios.example_english: He fills the pot with milk.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic-pratyaya (causative present), prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she causes to fill / completely fills
scenarios.example_english: The cloud fills the lake with water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: pᤱ pālanapūraṇayoḥ. kryādiḥ parasmaipadī. pᥑṇāti pᥑṇītaḥ pᥑṇanti. pālane poṣaṇe pūratāyāṃ ca vartate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: pᤱ pālanapūraṇayoḥ. pᥑṇāti. pālayati poṣayati pūrayati ca ityarthaḥ.

meanings.English: to protect, nurture, foster, fill, satisfy
meanings.Bengali: pālan karā, poṣaṇ karā, pūrti karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mṝñ' belongs to the 9th class (kryādi gaṇa) and means 'to injure, harm, or kill'. Since it has the marker 'ñ', it is conjugated in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada. In the present tense, it takes the class sign 'nā/nī' yielding forms like mṛṇāti and mṛṇīte.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Kartari prayoga (active voice), 3rd person singular present
scenarios.example_english: The warrior slays the enemy.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Kartari prayoga (middle voice), 3rd person singular present
scenarios.example_english: The tiger kills the deer for itself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root mṝñ is placed in the kryādi gaṇa with the meaning hiṃsā (injuring or killing). Being anubandha-ñ-it, it takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada affixes. In sārvadhātuka contexts, it takes the śnā pratyaya, resulting in forms like mṛṇāti and mṛṇīte.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes mṝñ in the sense of hiṃsana (harming/slaying). It forms aniṭ derivatives and follows the rkāra lengthening and reduction rules typical of the kryādi r-ending roots.

meanings.English: to kill, to injure, to destroy

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'aś' belongs to the 9th group (Kryadi Gana) and means 'to eat' or 'to consume'. In the active voice (Parasmaipada), it inserts the special Kryadi conjugational infix 'nā/nī' (śnā), turning the base into 'aśnā-' or 'aśnī-', producing forms like 'aśnāti' (he/she eats). When transformed into the causative (ṇijanta) form with the suffix 'ṇic', the base takes a vṛddhi vowel change to become 'āśayati', meaning 'causes to eat' or 'feeds'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-puruṣa eka-vacana (3rd person singular) with śnā vikaraṇa
scenarios.meaning: He/she eats or partakes of food
scenarios.example_english: The boy eats a sweet fruit.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative (ṇijanta) form in Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-puruṣa eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she feeds or causes someone to eat
scenarios.example_english: The mother feeds milk to the child.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'aśa bhojane' is classified in Kryadi Gana with the canonical sense of eating. It takes the conjugational affix śnā in the sarvadhatuka tenses. Madhava details the standard weak/strong gradations where śnā becomes nī before consonant-initial weak affixes (e.g., aśnītaḥ) and retains nā before vowel-initial endings with loss of ā (e.g., aśnanti), along with imperative 'aśāna' by the rule 'śnāsorallopaḥ'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'aśa bhojane' as an exclusively Parasmaipada transitive verb of the ninth class denoting the act of consuming meals or nutrition. He distinguishes this verb from the fifth-class homograph 'aśū̃ vyāptau' (which is Atmanepadi and means pervading), noting the derivation of principal forms including aśnāti, āśa, aśitā, and aśiṣyati.

meanings.English: to eat, consume, partake of food

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pli' means to go or move. Belonging to the ninth group of verbs (Kryadigana), it takes the marker 'na/ni' in present tense forms. Being an Ubhayapada root, it can be conjugated in Parasmaipada (when the action is directed outward) or in Atmanepada (when the action directly affects oneself).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Kartari prayoga, Present tense (Lat), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The traveler goes to the city.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Kartari prayoga, Present tense (Lat), 3rd person singular
scenarios.example_english: The boy journeys toward his own home.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'plīñ' has the intrinsic meaning of 'gatau' (movement, going). Marked with an indicatory 'ñ', it is an Ubhayapada root. In Sarvadhatuka conjugations, it accepts the Kryadi class affix 'śnā' with appropriate lengthening and vocalic operations producing 'plīnāti' and 'plīnīte'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Under 'plīñ gatau', Kshirasvamin notes that this root signifies motion. As an anit root, it takes typical reduplicated perfect forms like 'piplāya' and 'pipliñye' and forms standard past participles such as 'plīnaḥ'.

meanings.English: to go, to move, to proceed

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root dhṝ belongs to the 9th class (Kryadi) and means to slip down, fall, drop, or become loose. Because it is in the 9th class, it takes the marker 'nā' (Śnā) in the present tense, producing forms like 'dhṛṇāti'. In the causative (Nic), it expresses causing something to drop or loosen.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present tense (Lat), 3rd person singular, active voice (Kartari Prayoga)
scenarios.example_english: The leaf slips down from the tree.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative suffix (Nic), 3rd person singular
scenarios.meaning: causes to slip down or drop
scenarios.example_english: The wind causes the fruit to drop from the tree.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root dhṝ is listed in Kryadi in the meaning of avasraṃsana (slipping, falling, declining). It takes the Śnā pratyaya yielding dhṛṇāti, dhṛṇītaḥ, dhṛṇanti. In lit-lakar it forms dadhāra.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines avasraṃsana as cyutiḥ (dropping, falling, separating from a position). It belongs to the Anit group of roots terminating in long ṝ in the Kryadi gana.

meanings.English: to slip down, to fall off, to drop, to loosen
meanings.Bengali: khoṣe poṛā, jhore poṛā, śithila howā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bandh' means to bind, tie, or fasten. In the basic active form (Parasmaipada), it describes an agent directly tying an object. When modified with the causative suffix (Nic), it signifies making or causing someone else to perform the act of tying.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama Purusa, Ekavacana (Simple Active Voice)
scenarios.example_english: The cowherd ties the cow with a rope.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Nic pratyaya (Causative Active Voice)
scenarios.meaning: Causes to tie or gets bound
scenarios.example_english: The master makes the servant tie the horse.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'bandha' belongs to the Kryadi class and carries the sense of fastening or binding (bandhane). It is anit and Parasmaipadi. It takes the class conjugational affix sna (Kryadibhyah sna), resulting in the present-tense third-person singular form 'badhnati'. When followed by kit/nit suffixes, the penultimate nasal is dropped by standard Paninian morphophonemic operations, yielding past participle forms such as 'baddhah' and gerund 'baddhva'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'bandha bandhane' as an Anit root belonging to the 9th conjugation. It signifies the physical or figurative act of chaining, confining, or connecting objects together. In non-conjugational stems with Kit affixes, elision of the internal nasal takes place, whereas in the present tense it forms 'badhnati' through the regular application of sna-vikarana.

meanings.English: to bind, to tie, to fasten, to fetter

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'math' belongs to the 9th class (kryadi gana) and means to churn, agitate, shake, or crush. In standard active voice (Parasmaipada), the subject performs the action of churning or stirring substances like milk, curds, or oceans. When used with a causative affix (Nic), it signifies causing someone else to churn or agitate.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha (third person), ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The cowherd woman churns the curd.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic-pratyaya (causative), kartari prayoga, lat-lakara, prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to churn / causes to stir
scenarios.example_english: The mother has the girl churn the curd.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti designates 'matha vilolane' within the Kryadi class. The characteristic class marker 'sna' (shna) is applied, yielding forms such as mathnati, mathnitaḥ, mathnanti. It emphasizes the semantic aspect of vigorous agitation, stirring, and extraction through churning.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin analyzes 'matha' under the meaning of 'vilolana' (churning or shaking intensely). It highlights phonological behaviors across tenses and participles, noting regular formation in forms like mathita and mamatha.

meanings.English: to churn, agitate, shake, stir, destroy

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhṛ' belonging to the Kryādi class means to slip down, loosen, or droop. Because it has the marker 'ñ', it can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada. It takes the Kryādi class sign 'śnā' (-nā-/-nī-), resulting in forms like 'dhṛṇāti' and 'dhṛṇīte'. When used in causative (ṇic), it means to cause to drop or loosen.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), parasmaipada, prathama purusha, eka-vacana, lat lakara
scenarios.example_english: The leaf slips down / drops from the tree.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nijanta (causative), kartari prayoga, parasmaipada, lat lakara
scenarios.meaning: causes to slip down or loosens
scenarios.example_english: The strong wind causes the blossoms to drop down.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: dhṛñ avasrambane. 'avasrambanaṃ' nāma galanam avadhvaṃsanaṃ vā. ñittvād ubhayapadī. kryādau śnā-pratyayaḥ. dhṛṇāti, dhṛṇīte.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: dhṛñ avasrambane. sraṃsane ityarthaḥ. anit, ubhayatobhāṣaḥ. dhṛṇāti, dhṛṇīte.

meanings.English: to droop, slip down, loosen, or fall down
meanings.Bengali: shithil howa, jhule pora, khoshe pora
meanings.French: glisser vers le bas, se détendre, tomber

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vṝ' means to choose, honor, or share. Because it has an indicatory marker 'ñ' (ñit), it takes both active (Parasmaipada) and middle (Atmanepada) endings. In the present tense, it takes the Kryadi infix 'nā/nī', forming 'vṛṇāti' when doing the action generally and 'vṛṇīte' when choosing or accepting something specifically for oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense)
scenarios.example_english: The king chooses truth and virtue.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense)
scenarios.example_english: The maiden chooses a groom for herself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'vṝñ sambhaktau' as denoting mutual division, selection, and affectionate service or honoring (sambhajana). Being ñit, it operates in both padas (ubhayato bhasha). In the sarvadhatuka Kryadi class, it takes the affix 'snam' (nā/nī) yielding forms like vṛṇāti and vṛṇīte.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'vṝñ' expresses sambhakti (sharing, choosing, serving). The vowel 'ṝ' undergoes substitution according to canonical sandhi and phonological rules under the Kryadi vikaraṇa.

meanings.English: to choose, select, serve, honor, or share
meanings.Hindi: chuna, varan karna, seva karna, bantna
meanings.Bengali: bachhai kora, boron kora, seva kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'skumbh' means to stop, block, support, or hold back an object or person. Belonging to the 9th class (kryadigaṇa), it takes the 'nā' affix (śnā) in the present tense, producing forms like 'skubhnāti' or 'skumbhnāti'. It directly conveys obstructing movement or providing a rigid prop or brace.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat (present tense), prathama-puruṣa (third person), eka-vacana (singular), parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The dam obstructs the flow of water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṅ (past tense), prathama-puruṣa (third person), eka-vacana (singular), parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The warrior supported the falling pillar with a brace.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: skumbhu pratibandhe. stambhāditvāt śnā-pratyaye krite 'stambhustumbhu...' ityādinā sa-kārasya vikalpena lopo vaśābhyāsasya ca vidhānaṃ bhavati. skubhnāti, skumbhnāti. pratibandho nāma gati-rodhaḥ sthagirīkaraṇaṃ vā.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: skumbhu pratibandhe. stambhādigaṇe paṭhitaḥ. skubhnāti, skumbhnāti. pratiṣedhe vārodhe cāyaṃ vartate.

meanings.English: to obstruct, to arrest, to support, to prop up

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mṝ' belongs to the 9th conjugation class (Kryādi-gaṇa) and takes the special class sign 'nā' (śnā). It fundamentally means 'to injure', 'to harm', or 'to crush'. In standard usage it operates in the active voice (Parasmaipada) to show destruction or harming of an object.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present tense (laṭ), Third person singular, Active voice (Kartari)
scenarios.example_english: The warrior injures the enemy in battle.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Causative affix (ṇic), Present tense (laṭ), Third person singular
scenarios.meaning: Causes to be killed or slays
scenarios.example_english: The king causes the wicked one to be executed by punishment.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: mṝ hiṃsāyām. Kryādiḥ parasmaipadī aniṭ. Śnā-pratyaye kṛte 'mṛṇāti' iti rūpam sidhyati. Liṭi 'mamāra', 'mamratuḥ', 'mamruḥ'. Luṅi 'amārīt'. Hiṃsanaṃ pīḍanaṃ ca asyārthaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: mṝ hiṃsāyām. Mṛṇāti, mamāra, maritā. Hiṃsāpiḍāvadhādiṣu artheṣu vartate.

meanings.English: to harm, to injure, to kill, to destroy

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'yu' belongs to the 9th conjugation (kryādi gaṇa) and uniquely means both 'to unite/mix' (miśraṇa) and 'to separate/disjoin' (amiśraṇa). In the present tense, it takes the marker 'nā/nī' yielding forms like 'yunāti'. The exact sense of joining or separating is determined by context or upasargas (prefixes) like 'sam-' (together) or 'vi-' (apart).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana (active voice in Kryadi gana)
scenarios.example_english: The cook mixes honey with milk.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: nic pratyaya (causative), lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: causes to blend / causes to part
scenarios.example_english: The teacher causes the student to separate from faults.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ. kryādiḥ parasmaipadanirdeśāt parasmaipadī aniṭ. miśrībhāve viśleṣe ca vartate. śnā-pratyaye kṛte yunāti yunītaḥ yunanti iti rūpāṇi bhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ. ekīkaraṇe pṛthakkaraṇe ca vartate. virodhe'pi ubhayārtheṣu prayogo dṛśyate. yunāti jalam dugdhena.

meanings.English: to mix, blend, unite; to separate, disjoin, isolate
meanings.Hindi: milānā, joṛnā; alag karnā, pṛthak karnā
meanings.Bengali: meshano, jukto kora; prithak kora, bichhinnho kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kuṣ' belongs to the 9th class (kryādi gaṇa) and takes the special class sign 'nā' (śnā). It means to pull out, extract, or tear apart. In everyday Sanskrit, it appears in Parasmaipada as 'kuṣṇāti' (he/she pulls out or extracts). When converted to causative (ṇijanta), it becomes 'koṣayati' meaning 'causes to pull out or extract'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), laṭ lakāra (present tense), prathama puruṣa ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The doctor extracts the splinter.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇijanta (causative), kartari prayoga, laṭ lakāra ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The man makes his brother extract the thorn.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti treats 'kuṣa niṣkarṣe' under kryādi. It undergoes the śnā-pratyaya replacement, forming 'kuṣṇāti' through the application of ṇatva by 'aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye api'. The anit nature ensures forms like 'kuṣita' or 'koṣṭā' in specific kṛt derivations with standard sūtra exceptions, emphasizing the core sense of pulling out, dislodging, or separating forcefully.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kuṣa niṣkarṣe' with the semantic gloss of 'ākarṣaṇa' (drawing out or separating). It forms 'kuṣṇāti', 'kukoṣa', and 'koṣitā/koṣṭā'. He highlights its distinction from roots of similar phonetic shapes across other gaṇas by pointing out the unchangeable dental/retroflex conditioning and the active extraction action.

meanings.English: to extract, to pull out, to tear apart
meanings.Bengali: tule phelā, bāhir karā, khule neoyā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vrī' belongs to the 9th class (kryādi gaṇa) and means to choose, select, or cover. Because of the marker 'ñ', it is conjugated in both Parasmaipada (vrīṇāti) and Ātmanepada (vrīṇīte). Use Parasmaipada when the act of selecting or covering is directed externally, and Ātmanepada when the benefit of the choice or action returns to the subject.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (Present Tense), Prathama Purusha (3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The king chooses a worthy minister.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Ātmanepada, Lat lakara (Present Tense), Prathama Purusha (3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The maiden chooses a suitable husband for herself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: vrīñ varaṇe. kryādiṣu ñitvād ubhayapadī. varaṇaṃ svīkāraḥ āvaraṇaṃ vā. vrīṇāti vrīṇīte. liṭi vavrāya vavryatuḥ vavratus ityādi. aniṭkaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: vrīñ varaṇe. śnā-pratyayaḥ. varaṇaṃ prārthanā-sambhakti-chādanādiṣu vartate. vrīṇāti, vrīṇīte.

meanings.English: to choose, select, screen, or cover

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣubh' belongs to the 9th class (Kryadi) and takes the affix 'nā' (śnā) between the root and verb ending, becoming 'kṣubhnā-'. It means 'to shake', 'to agitate', or 'to be disturbed'. In Parasmaipada, it is used when someone or something disturbs an external object, or when describing an active shaking motion. In Atmanepada, it emphasizes the agitation affecting oneself or taking place internally.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The fierce wind agitates the ocean.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she/it becomes agitated or trembles internally
scenarios.example_english: When fear arises, his heart is deeply perturbed.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that 'kṣubh sañcalane' in Kryadigaṇa takes the śnā vikaraṇa to form 'kṣubhnāti' and 'kṣubhnīte'. The ñ-it markers in this section sanction Ubhayapada. In transitive contexts it denotes provoking motion or disturbance, while in intransitive contexts it signifies inner turmoil or physical trembling.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini glosses 'sañcalanam' as 'kampanam kṣobhaśca' (vibration, trembling, and agitation). The dental na becomes retroflex na due to the preceding kṣa (kṣa-kāra nimitta) by the rule of ṇatva, yielding kṣubhnāti.

meanings.English: to agitate, to shake, to disturb, to tremble
meanings.Tamil: kalanakkattai undupannu, kalangach chey, thalumba sei

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'yū' belongs to the 9th class (kryādi-gaṇa) and means to harm, cut, separate, or injure. It takes the class sign 'nā' (śnā) in strong forms and 'nī' in weak forms before consonant-initial endings. When a causative affix (ṇic) is added, it forms 'yāvayati', meaning 'causes to harm' or 'causes to cut'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, laṭ lakāra (present tense, active voice, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The warrior harms the enemy with a sword.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇic pratyaya (causative), kartari prayoga, laṭ lakāra
scenarios.example_english: The king causes the corrupt person to be afflicted with punishment.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: yū hiṃsāyām kryādiḥ parasmaibhāṣā aniṭ. śnā-pratyayaḥ. yunāti yunītaḥ yunanti. ṇici vṛddhau yāvayati. aniṭtvan-niyamāt ktvāyāṃ yūtvā ityetat rūpaṃ bhavati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: yū hiṃsāyām. hiṃsanaṃ chidrānveṣaṇaṃ vā. dīrghāntaḥ. śnāpratyaye kṛte yunāti ityetat siddhyati.

meanings.English: to injure, harm, cut, or separate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root dṛbh belongs to the 9th class (kryādi-gaṇa) and expresses the action of stringing together, arranging, or composing (like threading flowers into a garland or composing poetic verses). In active voice, it takes the class sign śnā to form dṛbhnāti. When used in the causative (ṇijanta), it changes to darbhayati, meaning to cause someone to weave, string, or compose.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice, laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana with śnā vikaraṇa)
scenarios.example_english: The garland maker strings flowers together with a thread.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: ṇyanta (causative voice, laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: causes to string together / gets composed
scenarios.example_english: The teacher makes the student compose the book.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: dṛbhi sandarbhe - sandarbho granthanam. kryādiḥ parasmaibhāṣā. dṛbhnāti, dṛbhṇītaḥ, dṛbhnanti. aniṭ-lakṣaṇam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: dṛbhi sandarbhe granthane. dṛbhnāti. kta-pratyaye dṛbdhaḥ iti rūpam.

meanings.English: To string together, to weave, to connect, to compose

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cur' means to steal or take away unlawfully. Belonging to the tenth conjugation (Curadi Gana), it naturally takes the suffix 'nic' (forming coraya-). It can be used in both Parasmaipada (corayati) and Atmanepada (corayate) based on whether the action's result directly benefits the agent or is general, though both forms carry the core meaning of stealing.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada standard usage in Curadi class with svarita/general agent focus
scenarios.example_english: The thief steals money.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada usage denoting the fruit of action accruing to the subject
scenarios.example_english: The thief steals a jewel for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Cura steye. Asya curadayah svarthe nicam labhante. Adyantavat sutrena parasmaipadam atmanepadam cobhayam bhavati. Corayati, corayate. Steyam ca apratibaddhataya parasvasvikaranam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Cura steye. Curadirasya adiriti curadih. Svarthe nic. Corayati caurah. Parakiyadravyasya paroksham haranam steyamucyate.

meanings.English: to steal, to rob, to pilfer

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'cit' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi gana) and means to perceive, contemplate, or be conscious of something. By default, roots in this group take the suffix '-aya-' (svarthika nic). When used in Parasmaipada, it highlights the general action of perceiving or contemplating; in Atmanepada, it emphasizes reflecting or internalizing the cognition.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svartha-nic, Lat lakara (present tense), Prathama purusha, Ekavacana (Parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The sage perceives the ultimate truth.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svartha-nic, Lat lakara (present tense), Prathama purusha, Ekavacana (Atmanepada)
scenarios.meaning: He/she reflects internally or becomes conscious of
scenarios.example_english: The student reflects upon righteousness within himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhava clarifies 'cita sancetane' by glossing 'sancetana' as 'samjnana' (comprehensive perception/consciousness) and 'jnana' (knowledge). The affix nic is applied in the primary sense itself (svartha) without requiring a causative trigger, producing forms such as cetayati and cetayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin interprets 'sancetanam' as cognitive awareness, perception, and intentional remembering (smarana). He illustrates the alternation of guna in the root vowel yielding the base ceta- before the curadi affix.

meanings.English: to perceive, to be conscious of, to think, to comprehend
meanings.Hindi: chetana hona, janana, dhyan dena, sochna
meanings.Bengali: upalabdhi kara, chetana labha kara, chinta kara

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cint' belongs to the 10th group (Curādi gaṇa), which inherently takes the suffix 'ṇic' (-aya-) in all basic conjugations. It means 'to think', 'to reflect', or 'to ponder'. Because it is an Ubhayapada root, it can take Parasmaipada endings (cintayati) when the focus of thinking is general, or Ātmanepada endings (cintayate) when emphasizing subjective contemplation or self-directed mental action.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe ṇic + Parasmaipada (laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy is thinking about the answer to the question.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe ṇic + Ātmanepada (laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: Ponders inwardly / reflects deeply within oneself
scenarios.example_english: The sage reflects upon the ultimate truth within himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: cinti cintāyām. curādiṣu paṭhitaḥ. iditvān nityam numāgamaḥ. svārthe ṇici cintayati cintayate iti rūpe bhavataḥ. cintitaḥ, cintanīyam, cintā.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: cinti cintāyām. iditkāraṇāt num bhavati. cintayati. cintā vicāraṇetyarthaḥ.

meanings.English: to think, to contemplate, to reflect, to worry

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vicch' belongs to the 10th group (Curadigana) and means 'to separate, divide, or split'. Because all 10th-class roots take the affix '-aya-' (nic) inherently, it forms 'vicchayati' in Parasmaipada and 'vicchayate' in Atmanepada without needing an external causative trigger.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada (Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The worker splits the piece of wood.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada (Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: He/she divides or portions out for oneself.
scenarios.example_english: The brother divides the fruit for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: viccha prthagbhave. curadau nityam nicanubandhah. tena vicchayati vicchayate iti roopadvayam bhavati. prthagbhavo namarthanam vibhajah.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: viccha prthagbhave. adantacuraditvan nica yoge vicchayati. vibhajanarthakah ayam dhatuh.

meanings.English: to divide, separate, split, sever

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'man' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana). Because it is in the 10th class, it automatically takes the nic affix (forming the base 'manaya-') in both active (Parasmaipada) and middle (Atmanepada) voices. It denotes stopping, restraining, stiffening, or showing pride/obstinacy. Both endings can be used without altering the core meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Kartari Prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/She restrains, stops, or becomes obstinate
scenarios.example_english: The warrior halts/restrains the enemy.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Kartari Prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/She halts or holds back for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The man restrains his own agitation.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root mana is read in the Curadi gana with the meaning 'stambha' (stopping, impeding, or making rigid/proud). As an adantadhatu or curadi root, it receives the canonical svarthe nic suffix, yielding forms such as manayati and manayate in the present tense, and amimanat in the aorist.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'mana stambhe' signifies constraint, obstruction, and pride (stambho garvah pratibandhashca). It forms standard Curadi tenth-class paradigms across Parasmaipada and Atmanepada with the augment i (set).

meanings.English: to stop, to restrain, to impede, to make stiff or proud
meanings.Hindi: rokna, stambhita karna, aithna ya ghamanda karna
meanings.German: anhalten, hemmen, erstarren machen, stolz sein
meanings.French: arreter, entraver, rendre rigide, s enorgueillir

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bal' belongs to the 10th class (Curadigana), meaning it takes the mandatory affix 'nic' in its basic sense (svartha) to express living, animating, or strengthening. Because it takes 'nic', it can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (when the action is directed outward) and Atmanepada (when the effect is self-directed or reflexive).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadigana svartha-nic, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama purusha, ekavacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.meaning: He/she animates, nourishes, or infuses strength into another
scenarios.example_english: The medicine strengthens (vitalizes) the sick person.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadigana svartha-nic, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama purusha, ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The youth strengthens himself through exercise.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'bala pranane' as being in the Curadi group. Since it ends with the inherent short 'a' (adanta), the suffix 'nic' is applied in the root's inherent sense (svartha). The operational meaning 'pranana' indicates supporting life, animating, or bestowing vital breath (jivana-dharana / baladhana). Forms such as balayati and balayate are derived regularly with i-guna and ay-adesha.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini notes that 'bala' functions in the sense of 'pranana' (sustaining life or infusing vitality). It takes the svārthika ṇic pratyaya, yielding forms like balayati, abibalat, and balayamcakara, carrying the nuance of animating or energizing.

meanings.English: to live, to animate, to sustain life, to strengthen
meanings.Hindi: prana phunkana, jivit karana, balavan banana
meanings.Chinese: fuyu shengming, shixing sheng, shi qiangzhuang

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'nat' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi) and means to act, perform, dance, or represent dramatically. Because it belongs to the Curadi group, it automatically receives the suffix 'nic' (making it 'nataya-') and undergoes vowel lengthening (vriddhi) to form 'natayati' or 'natayate'. In Parasmaipada, it highlights the external performance or dramatic portrayal of a character, while in Atmanepada, it highlights the actor's internal emotive engagement or mimetic gesture.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana (Parasmaipada, svarthe nic)
scenarios.meaning: Acts, dramatizes, or performs a role
scenarios.example_english: The actor acts out the story of Rama on the stage.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana (Atmanepada, svarthe nic)
scenarios.example_english: The poet depicts the joy of his heart through expressive gestures.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti glosses 'nata nrttau' within the Curadi group. It takes the affix nic essentially by rule, giving the base 'nati' with vriddhi to 'nat'. The root signifies both rhythmic dance movement (nrtta) and dramatic theatrical acting (abhinaya), resulting in forms like natayati and natayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin interprets 'nata nrttau' as denoting physical rhythmic posturing (gatraksepa) as well as dramatic representation of rasa and bhava. The canonical forms are derived with inherent causal morphology in the sense of theatrical expression.

meanings.English: to act, to dance, to dramatize, to represent on stage
meanings.German: schauspielen, tanzen, auf der Buhne darstellen
meanings.French: jouer la comedie, danser, interpreter un role
meanings.Russian: igrat na stsene, tantsevat, ispolnyat rol

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mūtr' belongs to the Curadi (10th) class and means 'to urinate' or 'to discharge urine'. Because it belongs to the 10th class, it naturally incorporates the 'ṇi' (causative-like) suffix in its standard form without changing the core meaning (svārthe ṇic). It can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga, Parasmaipada, Present Tense / Lat)
scenarios.example_english: The calf urinates in the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Middle Voice (Kartari Prayoga, Atmanepada, Present Tense / Lat)
scenarios.example_english: The horse urinates on the path.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: mūtra prasrāve. curādigaṇe svārthe ṇic-pratyayaḥ. adantatvāt ṇau kṛte mūtrayati, mūtrayate. caṅi 'amūmūtrat' iti rūpaṃ bhavati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: mūtra prasrāve. prasravaṇaṃ mūtrotsargaḥ. curāditvānṇyantaḥ. mūtrayati.

meanings.English: to urinate, to discharge urine

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pat' (10th class / Curadigana) denotes having supremacy, majesty, or sovereign authority (aisvarya). Being in Curadigana, it obligatorily takes the 'nic' (aya) affix in basic non-causative conjugations. It can take either Parasmaipada or Atmanepada endings based on whether the fruit of the action is intended for another or for the subject itself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadigana nic-pratyaya (svarthe nic), Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense)
scenarios.meaning: Rules, governs, or exercises sovereign authority
scenarios.example_english: The king rules the kingdom righteously.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadigana nic-pratyaya (svarthe nic), Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense)
scenarios.meaning: Exercises majesty or lords over for one's own domain
scenarios.example_english: The master manages his own household.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'pata' is read in the Curadigana in the sense of 'aisvarya' (supremacy/dominion). By 'satyapapasabdayasloka...', and the general Curadi rule, it takes the svarthe nic affix obligatorily, yielding forms like patayati and patayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'pata aisvarye' as a root expressing supreme authority or lordship, distinguishing it from the Bhvadi root 'pat' (to fall). It forms its present base as pataya- in both padas.

meanings.English: to possess sovereign power, to rule, to lord over, to possess supremacy
meanings.Kannada: aisvarya honduvike, aaluvike maduvudu, prabhuttva calayisuvudu
meanings.Telugu: aisvaryam kaligi unduta, prabhutvam cheyuta, eluta
meanings.Hindi: aishvarya yukta hona, shasan karna, prabhutva jatana
meanings.Bengali: aishvarya labh kora, shashon kora, prabhuttvo kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'muth' belongs to the Curadi gana (10th class) and means to crush, rub, oppress, or grind. Because it is in the Curadi class, it obligatorily takes the suffix 'nic' (making the base mothaya-). It can take Parasmaipada endings when the fruit of the crushing action affects another entity, and Atmanepada endings when it affects oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada (Kartari prayoga, active voice)
scenarios.example_english: The warrior crushes the enemies.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada (Kartari prayoga, self-directed fruit)
scenarios.meaning: He crushes/rubs for his own purpose
scenarios.example_english: The physician grinds the medicine for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: mutha pramardane. curadipathito nic-pratyayantah. mothayati, amumothat. pramardanamiti mardanam himsa ca ucyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: mutha pramardane. mothayati. curaditvannic. pramardanam pechanam hinasti va.

meanings.English: to crush, to grind, to injure, to oppress
meanings.Chinese: nian sui, ya sui, zhen ya

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'laks' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi), meaning it naturally takes the affix 'nic' (giving the stem 'laksaya-'). It signifies noticing, seeing, or marking. In Parasmaipada, it emphasizes the general action of observing or aiming at an object, whereas in Atmanepada, it highlights internal contemplation or personal observation.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Svarthe Nic, Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The archer aims at or observes the target.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Svarthe Nic, Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The wise person notices a fault within oneself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya confirms that 'laksa' belongs to Curadigana in the sense of 'alocana' (perception, reflection, or distinguishing). It takes the svarta-nic affix obligatorily according to 'satyamapapasa...' and related Curadi sutras, producing the stem laksaya- in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'laksa alocane', indicating both sensory perception (seeing/marking) and mental reflection (examination). It undergoes regular guna/vriddhi preservation and yields forms like laksayati, alalaksat, and laksita.

meanings.English: to observe, perceive, mark, or aim

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varṇ' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi gana). It inherently takes the affix 'ṇic' and means to describe, explain in detail, praise, or depict. In active voice, it takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana (Parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: The poet describes the beauty of nature.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Karmani prayoga (passive voice), Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana (Atmanepada with yak)
scenarios.example_english: The valor of the king is praised by all.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'varṇa' is read in Curadi with the meaning of 'varṇana' (detailed depiction, description, and praise). Since it belongs to Curadi gana, the affix 'ṇic' is applied obligatorily in the sense of the base root itself (svartho nic), yielding forms like varṇayati and varṇayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'varṇa' in the sense of describing or expanding upon something (vistāra-praśaṃsādiṣu). The ṇic affix is added without changing the basic verbal sense, producing standard tenth-class conjugations.

meanings.English: to describe, to depict, to color, to praise

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pāl' belongs to the 10th group (Curādi gaṇa) and means 'to protect', 'to guard', or 'to govern'. Roots in this class inherently take the affix 'ṇic' (which appears as '-aya-') in their basic forms without changing to a causative meaning. In active usage (Parasmaipada), it describes protecting someone or something externally, while in Middle voice (Atmanepada), it highlights the action benefiting the subject or self-preservation.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic + Laṭ lakāra (Present Tense, Active/Parasmaipada, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The king protects the citizens righteously.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic + Laṭ lakāra (Present Tense, Middle/Atmanepada, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.meaning: Nurtures / Protects (for oneself / with personal involvement)
scenarios.example_english: Janaki nurtures the trees with affection.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'pāla rakṣaṇe' is categorized under the Curādi gaṇa in the sense of preservation and governance. It takes the affix ṇic in the basic sense (svārthe ṇic), forming stems in -aya- (pālayati, pālayate). Its perfect forms include the periphrastic pālayāñcakāra / pālayāmāsa, and the reduplicated aorist is apīpalat.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'pāla rakṣaṇe' as signifying trāṇa (guarding/protecting). It is classified as an adanta or ṇijanta base in practice, retaining the inherent vowel length and combining with augment iṭ (seṭ) across non-conjugational tenses.

meanings.English: To protect, guard, nourish, cherish, govern
meanings.Bengali: Palon kora, rokkha kora, joton kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mul' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means to establish firmly, plant, or take root. Because it is in the 10th class, it intrinsically receives the 'nic' affix (forming the base 'mulaya-') and can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings without changing its core meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The farmer plants (establishes the root of) the tree in the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The righteous person firmly establishes his mind in righteousness.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'mula pratisthayam' as the action of fixing or establishing roots firmly (sthirikarana or rohana). As a standard root of the Curadi class, it takes the svarthe nic pratyaya obligatorily, generating the verbal stem mulaya- across all lakaras.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'mula' signifies 'pratistha' (founding, rooting, or stable establishment). Forms like mulayati and amumulat are derived in accordance with regular Curadi conjugational rules.

meanings.English: to plant, to root, to establish firmly
meanings.Bengali: shikod gada, sthapon kora, ropon kora
meanings.Chinese: sheng gen, zhi li, gu ding

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'gun' belongs to the Curadi gana (10th class), which inherently adds the affix '-aya-' (nic) to express its primary verbal meaning of inviting, addressing, or summoning. In Parasmaipada (gunayati), it indicates addressing or inviting someone in general, whereas in Atmanepada (gunayate), it emphasizes that the call or invitation is directed toward oneself or for one's own interest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe-ṇic, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The teacher calls upon the disciple.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe-ṇic, Atmanepada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The king summons the minister to his own counsel.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: guṇa āmantraṇe. Curādiḥ ubhayapadī. Svarthe ṇic pratyayaḥ. guṇayati, guṇayate. āmantraṇam abhimukhyakaraṇam āhvānaṃ vā. Liṭi guṇayāñcakāra, guṇayāmāsa. Luṅi ajīguṇat, ajīguṇata.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: guṇa āmantraṇe. āmantraṇaṃ sambodhana-pūrvaka-niyojanaṃ sambhāṣaṇaṃ vā. guṇayati guṇayate iti curāditvān nityam eva ṇic.

meanings.English: to invite, to summon, to address, to advise

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lakṣ' belongs to the 10th group (Curādi gaṇa). In this gaṇa, verbs inherently take the affix 'ṇic' (-aya-), appearing as lakṣayati (Parasmaipada) or lakṣayate (Ātmanepada). It conveys the actions of observing, noticing, aiming at, or marking something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), Parasmaipada, laṭ lakāra (present tense)
scenarios.example_english: The boy observes the moon in the sky.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga (active voice), Ātmanepada, laṭ lakāra (present tense)
scenarios.example_english: The wise person perceives knowledge in all things.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti glosses 'lakṣa darśanāṅkanayoḥ' indicating two primary senses: darśana (seeing, perceiving, observing) and aṅkana (marking, designating, branding). As a Curadi root, it obligatorily takes the svaritenta ṇic affix by default, permitting both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada terminations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'lakṣa' conveys cognitive observation (alocana) as well as physical marking or distinguishing (cihnikarana). Derived forms like lakṣaṇa (characteristic mark) and lakṣya (target, object of perception) originate from this root.

meanings.English: to observe, to perceive, to mark, to aim

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'math' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi gana) and carries the meaning of churning, stirring, or vigorously agitating liquids. Because it is in the 10th group, it naturally attaches the 'aya' affix (nic) in active forms. It can be used in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The milkmaid churns the curd kept in the pot.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana (action directed to oneself)
scenarios.example_sanskrit: Krsnah svayam navanitam labdhum payah mathayate.
scenarios.example_english: Krishna churns the milk himself to obtain fresh butter.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: matha vilolane. curadibhyo nic ityantargata-nicanubandhah. mathayati, mathayate. vilolanam viloḍanam sañcalanam ca.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: matha vilolane. adanta-curadir ayam. dadhi-mathanadishu prayujyate. mathayati.

meanings.English: to churn, to agitate, to stir vigorously

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pu' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and signifies purifying, filtering, or cleansing. Because it takes the Curadi affix 'nic' inherently, it forms stems like 'pavaya-'. It is Ubhayapadi, meaning it can take either Parasmaipada endings (when the action's benefit is general) or Atmanepada endings (when the purifying action directly benefits the agent).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The sage purifies the water.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The devotee purifies his own mind.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'pun pavane' belongs to Curadi. The marker n indicates both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada affixes. Taking the mandatory nic affix in the Curadi group, vriddhi occurs on the vowel 'u' preceding an ac resulting in 'av', giving the base 'pavaya-'. Thus we obtain the present indicative forms pavayati and pavayate in the sense of sodhana (purification/cleansing).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Under Curadi, 'pun pavane' denotes sodhana (cleansing, sifting, filtering). As an anudattopadesha root with it-marker n, it is Ubhayapadi. By applying the standard Curadi nic formation, the vocalic lengthening and augment yield forms like pavayati, apipavat, and pavayancakara.

meanings.English: to purify, to cleanse, to filter, to refine

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhūp' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi), where it essentially means to heat, to fumigate, to incense, or to torment/afflict with heat. Because it is a 10th-class root, it takes the inherent 'ṇic' (aya) affix inherently even in its basic active meaning. In Parasmaipada, it means performing the act of heating or fumigating; in Atmanepada, it can express the same action with the fruit accruing to the self.

It means to tell, narrate, describe, or compose continuous speech. When used in active voice, it takes endings like 'kathayati' or 'kathayate' to mean telling a story or communicating information clearly to listeners.

It forms regular present stems through the incorporation of the class-specific nic suffix, leading to ubiquitous active forms in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varn' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi Gana). Roots in this class automatically take the suffix 'nic' (seen as '-aya-'), meaning the root naturally acts with causative or intensive force without requiring an external causer. When used in Parasmaipada (varnayati), the action of describing, painting, or praising is expressed generally. In Atmanepada (varnayate), the focus is often on the internal composition or when the fruit of the description/representation accrues to the speaker or painter.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'varna' is enumerated in Curadi with the meaning of 'varnane' (delineating, describing qualities, or coloring). By the rule 'curadibhyo nic', it takes an essential svārthe-ṇic affix across all four non-conjugational and conjugational tenses, forming 'varnayati' and 'varnayate'. As a Curadi dhatu, it has both Padas and is treated as Seṭ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'varna' signifies 'varnane'—the act of expression through words (guṇabhāṣaṇa or stuti) or graphic depiction through pigments (rūpāṅkana). The derivation results in regular forms taking guṇa and the standard Curadi augment '-aya-'.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tul' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi) and always takes the affix 'nic' to form its base. It conveys the action of weighing, lifting, balancing, or comparing two things. Because Curadi roots allow both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada terminations, active usage typically denotes weighing or comparing an object, while reflective usage focuses on the agent balancing something for oneself or being equivalent in weight.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rac' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes the suffix 'nic' essentially to mean 'to compose', 'to arrange', 'to construct', or 'to string together'. As an Ubhayapada root in this class, it can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (e.g., racayati) and Atmanepada (e.g., racayate) without changing the fundamental meaning, representing the creative arrangement of verses, objects, or ideas.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'stup' belongs to the Curadi class (10th conjugation) and conveys the idea of heaping up, accumulating, or raising something high into a pile or mound (like building a stupa or monument). Because it automatically receives the affix 'nic' (forming 'stupaya-'), it can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings depending on whether the result of the action is intended for another person or for oneself.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'stupa' denotes 'samucchraya' (loftiness, heightening, piling up). It is classified among the adanta or nic-taking curadi roots that represent physical aggregation and vertical accumulation.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tark' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi) and naturally takes the suffix 'nic' (forming tarkaya-). It means to think, infer, speculate, or deduce context. When used in Parasmaipada (tarkayati), the subject directs the reasoning outwards, while Atmanepada (tarkayate) often emphasizes mental calculation or reasoning oriented to one's own comprehension.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under the Curadi section that 'tarka' is employed in the sense of 'vitarka' (investigation/hypothesis) as well as syntactic deduction ('adhyahara'). It forms full Ubhayapada sets in all lakaras taking standard set augment.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root sprh belongs to the 10th group of verbs (Curadi gana) and signifies desiring, longing for, or yearning. In Paninian syntax, the desired object governed by this verb uniquely takes the 4th case (caturthi vibhakti / dative case) rather than the normal 2nd case (accusative), under the rule 'sprher ipsitah'. Because it belongs to Curadi gana, it takes the affix 'nic' in its primary active sense without needing a causative trigger.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'sprha ipsayam' as denoting the action of intensely wishing or desiring. Since it falls under the Curadi class, the affix nic is added inherently (svarthe nic). In syntax, Madhava highlights the karaka rule 'sprher ipsitah', establishing that the desired entity attains sampradana designation and therefore takes the fourth case.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'sprha' in the sense of 'ipsa' (longing, reaching out in desire). He notes the non-differentiation of basic meaning upon adding the Curadi nic affix, generating regular inflections such as 'sprhayati', 'asprhayat', and 'sprhayamasa'.

meanings.English: to desire, to long for, to wish, to covet

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tul' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and expresses the action of weighing, measuring, or comparing. Since it naturally takes the suffix 'nic' (making the base 'tolay/tolaya'), it can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada terminations. When used in active voice, it means to measure, weigh, or compare something.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'tula' signifies 'unmana' (vertical or balance-based measuring/weighing). Forms like 'tolayati' and 'tolayate' are derived by application of 'nic' as an intrinsic gana characteristic.

meanings.English: to weigh, to measure, to compare

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'stah' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi Gana) and inherently takes the affix 'Nic' without needing a causative context. dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rac' means to produce, arrange, compose, or make an effort to craft something. Being in the 10th group (Curadi gana), it inherently adds the affix '-aya-', forming 'racayati' in active voice (Parasmaipada) and 'racayate' in middle voice (Atmanepada).

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root par belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana). Because it takes the essential nic affix (-aya-) inherently, it forms verbs like parayati and parayate. It carries the primary meaning of bringing to completion, sustaining, protecting, or successfully accomplishing an undertaking. In active voice (Parasmaipada), the focus is purely on the act of fulfilling or protecting, whereas in middle voice (Atmanepada), the accomplishment is centered upon the subject.

The senses denote nurturing, sustaining (palana), and completing or filling to satisfaction (purana). In the reduplicated aorist (lun), it takes forms like apiparat.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'para' is listed under Curadi with the semantic range of protection (palana) and completion/nourishment (purana). vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmī analyzes 'puṭ' as denoting 'bhedana' (splitting, cleavage, fracturing). It is classified as an adanta or curādi root taking ṇic with regular guṇa strengthening to form poṭayati/poṭayate.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rup' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi), meaning it obligatorily takes the '-aya-' affix (Nic). In Parasmaipada (ropayati) the action is directed outwards, whereas in Atmanepada (ropayate) the emphasis rests on the subject or self-interest.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'rupa vimohane' that the root conveys the sense of causing delusion or extreme mental perplexity (vimohana). As an adanta root of the tenth gana, it operates primarily with nic-vrita stems resulting in ropana.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'chadi' in Curadi is defined as 'chadi samvarane'. vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'chadi samvarane', identifying its semantic scope as encompassing both physical shielding (covering objects) and conceptual concealment (hiding secrets or facts).

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kal' belongs to the 10th group of verbs (Curadi gana) and primarily means to count, reckon, or calculate. Because it belongs to Curadi gana, it takes the affix 'nic' (forming kalaya-), functioning in both active (Parasmaipada) and middle (Atmanepada) voices. In everyday Sanskrit, it expresses reckoning, understanding, or driving forward.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kala' is listed in Curadi gana under the sense of 'saṅkhyāna' (counting, enumeration).
