When vṛddhi is applied optionally or by standard Curadi patterns, forms like kālayati/kālayate or kalayati/kalayate are generated.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kala saṅkhyāne' among the standard reckoning roots of Curadi. The sense extends to enumeration, driving, and observing (saṅkhyāna-gati-grahaṇeṣu).

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lakṣ' means to notice, observe, perceive, or mark. Believing to the 10th Gana (Curadi), it takes the 'ṇic' affix obligatory in the standard present tense to form 'lakṣayati' or 'lakṣayate'. When used in Parasmaipada, it highlights the act of viewing or observing outwards. In Atmanepada, it highlights observing carefully for oneself or perceiving internally.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'taḍ' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means 'to strike', 'to beat', or 'to hit'. vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'taḍi āghāte' signifying violent contact or striking (prahāra). It forms 'tāḍayati' and 'tāḍayate' through the invariable addition of the Curadi svārthe-ṇic affix.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that the root 'tula' in Curadi is assigned the semantic sphere of 'unmana' (measuring weight or counterpoising). vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin states under Curadi that 'tula unmane' denotes accurate counter-weighing and calibration of physical or abstract entities. The operation of guna on the penultimate short vowel 'u' leads to 'tolayati', expressing the determination of quantity or worth.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'santv' (or 'santva') belongs to the Curadi class (10th conjugation) and means to console, comfort, soothe, or pacify someone gently. Because it belongs to the Curadi group, it inherently takes the affix 'nic' (forming santvaya-), and it can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (santvayati) and Atmanepada (santvayate) depending on whether the action is directed outwards or reflexive.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'santva santvane' under the Curadi group. It is an intrinsically nic-ending stem (svarthe nic), yielding the base santvaya-. Being in the Curadi class, it admits both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada affixes and operates transitively with an it-augment (set) in non-sarvadhatuka environments.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'santva santve' as the act of soothing, comforting, or pacifying with kind words (priyavacana). It forms canonical present forms like santvayati and santvayate, signifying reassurance and alleviation of sorrow.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root kṣal belongs to the Curadi class (10th conjugation) and primarily means to wash, cleanse, or purify. Because it is a Curadi root, it obligatorily takes the affix nic (-aya-), lengthening the vowel to form ksalayati in active usage. It can take Parasmaipada endings when acting for another, or Atmanepada endings (ksalayate) when the action directly affects the agent.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti states: 'ksala saucakarmani' - refers to cleansing, scouring, and purifying external objects or parts of the body. By Curadi svarthe nic and ata upadhayah vriddhi rule, the penultimate short 'a' is lengthened to long 'a', yielding 'ksalayati' and 'ksalayate'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'ksala sauce' implies the removal of dirt and impurities (malamocana). It is grouped among the non-cocurring mittva roots of Curadi, hence experiencing standard upadha-vriddhi in the stem formation.

meanings.English: to wash, cleanse, rinse, purify

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root rūp belongs to the 10th group (Curādi gaṇa), meaning it takes the infix -aya- (ṇic) right from the start. Its primary meaning is to give form, to depict, to act out, or to closely investigate. In active voice (Parasmaipada), it expresses creating a visual representation or examining a fact, and with prefixes like ni- (nirūpayati), it denotes determining or ascertaining reality clearly.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti records rūpa under the meaning 'rūpakriyāyām' (in the sense of formative action, aesthetic depiction, and perception). Being in Curādi gaṇa, it receives the non-causative inherent suffix ṇic (svārthe ṇic), yielding the bases rūpaya- leading to rūpayati and rūpayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin interprets the root rūpa as rūpakaraṇe (giving visible shape or figure) as well as nirūpaṇe (discerning and investigating). It undergoes standard Curādi affixation without Guṇa change because the vowel ū is lengthened naturally by nature of the base.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varṇ' belongs to the Curadi class (10th group of verbs) and carries the inherent suffix 'ṇic'. It means to describe, depict, praise, or illustrate in detail. In Parasmaipada it expresses describing something directly (varṇayati), while in Atmanepada it indicates performing the narration with reflexive benefit or self-involvement (varṇayate).

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'varṇa' is listed in Curadi under the sense of 'varṇane' (description, detailing qualities, and praise). As an adanta root of the tenth class, it takes the svārthika-ṇic affix obligatorily, forming the stem 'varṇaya-' which conjugates in both padas (varṇayati, varṇayate).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'varṇa varṇane' as detailing attributes, painting, or portraying verbal forms clearly. It is grouped among the non-causative intrinsic nic-bearing roots in Curadigaṇa.

meanings.English: to describe, to depict, to color, to narrate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root tantr belongs to the Curadi class (10th conjugation) and takes the mandatory suffix nic (ay), meaning to manage, support, regulate, or sustain family and household affairs. Being Ubhayapada in Curadi, it can take both Parasmaipada terminations (tantrayati) when the action is directed outwardly and Atmanepada terminations (tantrayate) when highlighting personal responsibility and involvement.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root tantra is cited in the Curadi gana under the semantic marker parikutumbadharane, signifying the maintenance and disciplined governance of household and family dependencies. Because it is an adanta Curadi root, the affix nic is compulsory by Paninian sutra 'curadibhyo nic', leading to the derived base tantray- with ubhayapada inflection.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes tantra in the sense of family sustenance and systemic management (kutumbadharana and vyavastha). The formation involves the ay-pratyaya throughout sarvadhatuka stems, yielding forms like tantrayati and tantrayate.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kath' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi gana) and takes the mandatory 'nic' (aya) affix inherently. It means to narrate, recite, or tell a connected story. Being an Ubhayapada root, it can take Parasmaipada endings when focusing on the action or recipient, and Atmanepada endings when the outcome or narration reflects directly upon the agent.

It takes the svarthe nic suffix unconditionally, giving forms such as kathayati and kathayate, with regular curadi nit-guna and idagama rules in non-sarvadhatuka forms.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'katha' signifies systematic storytelling or connected discourse (samyak vakyaracanatvam). The base retains its inherent nic-pratyaya throughout conjugation, forming kathayati, kathitavan, and kathitam.

meanings.English: to narrate, tell, recount, or describe in connected discourse

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vas' in the 10th class (Curadi gana) means to sever affection, alienate, or perfume/scent. Being in the Curadi gana, it intrinsically takes the affix 'nic' (-aya-) in all basic conjugations. Because it is Ubhayapadi, it takes Parasmaipada endings when the action is directed outwards and Atmanepada endings when expressing an internal or reflexive engagement.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini notes that 'vasa' in Curadigana expresses snehavicchedana (severing affection) and is characterized by the default addition of the aya-pratyaya with both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'ghaṭ' belonging to the Curādi class means to assemble, join, unite, or bring together into a single whole. Because it belongs to the tenth class, it inherently takes the affix 'ṇic' in standard forms. When conjugated in Parasmaipada, the emphasis is on performing the action of combining or fashioning for general or external purposes. When conjugated in Ātmanepada, it highlights the assembly, effort, or union benefiting or oriented toward the subject.

Due to the inherent nic-pratyaya of Curadi, forms exhibit standard guna or vriddhi modification where applicable, yielding ghaṭayati and ghaṭayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'ghaṭ' in this context signifies samavaya or samghata (unification, dense combination, or forming a group), distinguishing its Curadi causative-like morphological nature from its primary Bhvadi homophone.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhrn' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi gana) and carries the meaning of satisfying, pleasing, or gratifying someone. In the 10th class, the affix 'nic' (-aya-) is added inherently. As an Ubhayapadi root, it can take Parasmaipada endings when focusing simply on the act of satisfying someone else, or Atmanepada endings when the fulfillment or reciprocal feeling reflects on the agent.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'dhrna tarpane' that the root denotes tarpana (gratification/nourishment). It follows the Curadi class conjugation, taking the affix nic svabhavatah, functioning transitively in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'laks' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi-gana) and inherently carries the affix 'nic' (forming laksaya-), expressing the action of observing, noticing, or reflecting upon something. It can take either Parasmaipada endings (laksayati) or Atmanepada endings (laksayate) without a change in its fundamental meaning of perceiving or observing.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains that 'laks alocane' denotes visual or mental observation (caksusam jnanam manasam va). The root operates with standard Curadi gunated stem alternants yielding laksayati and laksayate.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'carc' means to study, repeat, deliberate, or discuss. Belonging to the 10th class (Curadi), it takes the 'nic' (aya) affix naturally, appearing as 'carcayati' in Parasmaipada and 'carcayate' in Atmanepada without changing its core meaning.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chad' belongs to the Curadi (10th) class and primarily signifies covering, concealing, or veiling something. Because it belongs to the 10th gana, it obligatorily takes the affix 'ṇic' even in its basic sense (svārthe ṇic), yielding the inflected forms 'chādayati' and 'chādayate'. In the active voice (Parasmaipada), the focus is on the act of covering an external object, whereas in Atmanepada, it often conveys that the action reflects upon the agent or serves an internal purpose.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under the Curadi section that 'chad' carries the sense of 'apavāraṇa' (to veil, screen, or hide from view). The operational ṇic affix marks its tenth-class status, yielding transitive operations with accusative objects representing the entity that is veiled or covered.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dri' belonging to the Curadi class fundamentally expresses fearing, scaring, or tearing apart. In active usage (Parasmaipada), it means to frighten someone or to split/rend something, while in Middle voice (Atmanepada), it highlights the action reflecting onto oneself or done for one's own sake.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini notes that 'dri' in the tenth class denotes fear (bhaya) and rending (vidarana). The marker anubandha 'n' indicates its Ubhayapada status in conjugation, taking both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada terminations routinely.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin glosses 'pīḍa bādhāyām' indicating affliction, torment, and physical compression. Forms like 'pīḍitaḥ' are noted for the past participle, meaning pressed, pained, or tormented.

meanings.English: to torment, afflict, harass, or press

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root laks belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana), meaning 'to perceive, observe, see, or mark/characterize'. Because it is in the Curadi group, it always takes the affix 'nic' (forming laksaya-). In active voice (Parasmaipada), it conveys the action directed outward (e.g. noticing a sign), whereas in middle voice (Atmanepada), it highlights an introspective perception or reflection affecting the subject.

scenarios.meaning: Observes, perceives, or marks outward phenomena

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara (present tense), Prathama-purusa (3rd person), Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.meaning: Perceives, senses within oneself, or characterizes for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The sage perceives inner peace within himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'laksa darsanankanayoh' as denoting both perception (darsana/alocana) and marking or distinguishing (ankana/cihnakarana). Being part of the Curadi group, it mandatorily receives the svarthanic affix, yielding the stem laksaya- with both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin states under the Curadi section that 'laksa' signifies direct sight, mental observation, and making an identifying mark. The presence of the formative 'i' (nic) leads to forms like laksayati and laksayate across various tenses and moods.

meanings.English: to perceive, to observe, to notice, to mark

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cuṭ' belongs to the 10th class (Curādigana) and signifies the action of cutting, severing, or slicing into pieces. In this class, the suffix 'ṇic' is attached directly in the primary sense without changing it to a causative meaning. In Parasmaipada (coṭayati), it expresses cutting something for a general purpose or another person, while in Ātmanepada (coṭayate), it emphasizes the action performed for one's own benefit.

scenarios.example_english: The farmer cuts the rope for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'cuṭ' is defined in the sense of 'chedana' (cutting, severing). Being in the Curādi-gaṇa, it takes the svārthe ṇic affix. Guṇa vowel strengthening of the penultimate short vowel 'u' produces the base 'coṭaya-', yielding forms like coṭayati and coṭayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin categorizes 'cuṭ' under chedane (dvidhākaraṇe / splitting into parts). It represents the physical severance of an object into distinct segments and undergoes standard Curādi morphological operations.

meanings.English: to cut, to sever, to split into pieces

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'stan' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi Gana) and means to make a sound, especially the divine sound of thunder or roaring. Because it is in the Curadi class, it naturally takes the affix 'nic' (making it stanaya-), and it can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings without changing its core meaning of thundering or roaring.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'stana' is read in the sense of 'deva-shabde' (divine or celestial sound such as thunder) within the Curadi group. Since it is adanta, the suffix nic applies inherently, yielding forms like stanayati and stanayate across tenses.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'stana devashabde' as referring specifically to celestial rumbling or thunder. It takes svarthe nic as part of the Curadi class and inflects in both Padas.

meanings.English: to thunder, rumble, make a deep roaring sound

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kath' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and inherently takes the 'nic' affix (-aya-) in all basic conjugations. It means to tell, narrate, or compose connected sentences into a story. In Parasmaipada, it means narrating something generally. In Atmanepada, it often signifies narrating for oneself or expressing one's own inner thoughts/experiences.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'katha' is listed under Curadi gana in the sense of 'vakyaprabandha' (connected, coherent sentence arrangement or narration). By being in Curadi gana, it obligatorily receives the 'nic' suffix via 'satyapapasarvadhrtkathanapatanarcibhyah nic' or the general Curadi rule, yielding forms like kathayati and kathayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'katha vakyaprabandhe' as denoting the orderly articulation of sentences forming a narrative structure. It is set and produces the base 'kathaya-' through the inherent nic suffix.

meanings.English: to tell, narrate, relate, describe

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'satr' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi) and takes the mandatory affix 'nic' (forming the stem 'satraya-'). It means to extend, spread out, or perform an expansive action or ritual. Being an Ubhayapadi root, it can take both Parasmaipada (satrayati) and Atmanepada (satrayate) endings.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'satra vistare' under the Curadi-gana. The root obligatorily takes 'nic' without changing the primary lexical meaning ('svarthagata-nic'). Being marked with anudatta-it or by general curadi-prakriya, it functions in Ubhayapada with forms such as satrayati and satrayate, derived in the sense of expansion and continuation.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'satra vistare' denotes 'vistara' (expansion, spreading, prolonging). The nominal formation 'satram' (a prolonged sacrificial session or almshouse) is directly related to this verbal semantic sphere.

meanings.English: to spread, extend, elaborate, perform a prolonged action or sacrifice

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣip' belonging to the Churadi group means to urge, send, or propel. Because it inherently takes the 'nic' suffix (forming 'kṣepaya-'), it can take both active (Parasmaipada) endings to indicate an action directed outward and middle (Atmanepada) endings when reflecting an action connected to the agent.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṣipa preraṇe' is listed under Curādigaṇa. It forms the base 'kṣepaya-' after taking the mandatory svārthe-ṇic affix and Guṇa of the vowel 'i'. Both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada terminations are applied yielding kṣepayati and kṣepayate in the sense of motivating, throwing, or impelling.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'kṣipa preraṇe' in Curādi as synonymous with stimulating, throwing, or sending forward. With ṇic, it displays the forms kṣepayati-te with guṇa application on the penultimate vowel 'i'.

meanings.English: to throw, to send, to instigate, to propel

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'vid' in the 10th group (Curadi Gana) inherently takes the 'nic' affix (forming 'vedaya-') and operates in three distinct meanings: perceiving/experiencing (cetana), communicating/informing (akhyana), and residing (nivasa). It can take active endings (vedayati) or middle endings (vedayate) with equivalent transitive function.

scenarios.example_english: The student informs the teacher of his situation.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'vida cetanakhayananivasesu' as a Curadi root possessing three specific senses: cetana (sentience or direct awareness), akhyana (announcing, teaching, or narrating), and nivasa (dwelling or residing). By the rule 'curadibhyo nic', it forms stems in -aya- (vedayati/vedayate).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'cetana' as samjna-upalabdhi (perceptive consciousness), 'akhyana' as jnapana/pratipadana (communicating/imparting knowledge), and 'nivasa' as vasti (dwelling). All forms are built with the inherent causative-type nic affix.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'par' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) taking the inherent affix 'nic' in the active sense. It conveys completing an action, sustaining continuity, undergoing life through hardship, or maintaining purity. When used in Parasmaipada (parayati) or Atmanepada (parayate), it expresses accomplishing, persevering through, or sustaining an undertaking.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that the root 'para' in the Curadi class has multiple semantic applications, including santati (continuity/lineage), sauca (purification/uprightness), and krcchrajivana (surviving under hardship). Since it is within the Curadi gana, it takes the affix nic obligatorily in svartha, yielding forms such as parayati and parayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini confirms that 'para' denotes continuity, endurance, and purification. It forms the present stem paraya- by adding nic and sap, functioning as an Ubhayapadi root with set character in the non-sarvadhatuka environments.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mārg' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gana) and means to seek, search, or look for something. Because it belongs to the 10th class, it takes the affix 'ṇic' automatically, forming 'mārgayati' (Parasmaipada) or 'mārgayate' (Ātmanepada) without needing an extra causative sense. Both forms mean searching or seeking.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mārga' is read in Curādigaṇa in the sense of 'mṛgaṇe' (investigating, searching, seeking). By rule 'curādibhyo ṇic', it obligatorily takes the affix ṇic, yielding the forms mārgayati and mārgayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'mārga mṛgaṇe' as the act of searching or tracking. The root undergoes regular 10th-gana operations resulting in standard Curādi verbal formations.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bhāj' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi-gaṇa) and naturally takes the suffix 'ṇic' to form its base 'bhājaya-', meaning to divide, distribute, or apportion. When conjugated in Parasmaipada, it highlights the action of distributing something to others, while in Ātmanepada, it often emphasizes distributing among oneself or for personal involvement.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'bhāji' in the Curādi-gaṇa is defined in the sense of 'pṛthagbhāva' (separation, partition, division). By the rule 'satyāpapāśarūpaveṇatūlaślokasenālomatvacavarmacūrṇacurādibhyo ṇic', it obligatorily receives the svārthe-ṇic affix. vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes 'bhāji pṛthagbhāve' as expressing division or classification. The root operates transitively in dividing whole entities into parts and follows standard Curādi conjugational rules.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣap' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi Gana) and primarily means to drive, send, urge, or dispatch (prerana), as well as to wear out, consume, or pass time (kṣapana). Because it takes the essential 'nic' (aya) affix inherently in Curadi, it can take either Parasmaipada or Atmanepada endings depending on whether the action's fruit is intended for another or oneself.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pari' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi Gana) and primarily expresses the action of encircling, going around, enclosing, or making something spherical/round. dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rūp' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gaṇa) and takes the mandatory 'ṇic' affix (forming the base 'rūpaya-'). scenarios.meaning: He or she celebrates / conducts a festivity
scenarios.example_english: The person celebrates the festival.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.meaning: He or she rejoices or holds a celebration for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The king celebrates in his own palace.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti identifies 'garda utsave' under the Curadi-gana. The canonical meaning 'utsava' denotes festivity, joy, and grand public or private celebration. By virtue of being in Curadi-gana, the stem takes the svarthika-nic affix, yielding the base 'gardaya', conjugated as gardayati and gardayate in the present tense.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'garda utsave' is an adanta curadi root expressing the act of making merry or holding a festival. It follows the standard pattern of tenth-class verbs taking both padas across the lakaras with set characteristics.

meanings.English: to celebrate, to rejoice, to hold a festival

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mantr' belongs to the Curadi class and is conjugated in Atmanepada with the suffix 'nic' inherent to its nature. It conveys the action of holding private counsel, consulting, taking counsel, or deliberating secretly. When a leader, minister, or student discusses or deliberates confidentially, this root is used.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara (Present indicative), Prathama purusa (3rd person), Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The king consults secretly with the minister.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lan lakara (Past tense), Prathama purusa (3rd person), Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The commander deliberated with the soldiers.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mantri' is given in the sense of 'guptabhasana' (confidential speech or deliberation). Being an idit (having an 'i' as an it marker), the root retains an internal nasal consonant (num-agama), forming 'mantr'. As a Curadi root, it receives the svārthe nic affix and takes Atmanepada affixes, yielding forms such as mantrayate and amamantrata.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'mantri guptabhasane' as denoting esoteric or confidential dialogue, giving rise to forms like mantrayate. It highlights the semantic boundary of speech held purposefully under confidentiality or statecraft council.

meanings.English: to consult secretly, to deliberate, to advise
meanings.Hindi: gupta alocana ya paramarsa karna, mantrana karna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mrg' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi Gana) and means 'to search', 'to seek', or 'to hunt'. In general usage, it takes the affix 'nic' (or 'ayak' in classical terminology for mrgayu/mrgayate) and can be used in both Parasmaipada (mrgayati) and Atmanepada (mrgayate) to denote searching for a desired object or seeking knowledge.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi standard Atmanepada present active (Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy searches for the path.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi Parasmaipada present active (Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The hunter searches for deer in the forest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'mrga anveshane' as an action of seeking, pursuing, or searching thoroughly. As part of the Curadi group, it takes the suffix nic obligatorily (svarthe nic), yielding the forms mrgayati and mrgayate depending on Pada assignment.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'mrga' denotes seeking (anveshana) or hunting. The verbal base undergoes guna or guna-like stability according to morphological constraints, yielding bases in curadi such as mrgayati or the reflexive-deponent usage mrgayate.

meanings.English: to search, seek, pursue, hunt

canonical_dhatvartha: smrtyam cintayam ca (in the sense of thinking, contemplating, or remembering)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cint' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana), which naturally takes the 'nic' (aya) affix in all standard conjugations without needing an external causative trigger. When conjugated in Parasmaipada, the act of thinking is general or directed outward. When conjugated in Atmanepada, the mental reflection is internalized or personally experienced by the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada (Kartari prayoga, standard Curadi ṇic)
scenarios.example_english: The sage ponders the absolute truth.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada (Kartari prayoga, self-directed mental reflection)
scenarios.meaning: Thinks over for oneself, reflects internally
scenarios.example_english: The boy reflects upon his own duty.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Citi smrtyam. Curadi ganastha ayamatmako dhathuh. Svabhavatah nicpratyayantam cintayati iti bhavati. Smaranam cintanam va arthah.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Citi smrtyam cintane ca. Nic bhavati nityam curaditvat. Cintayati cintayate iti rupa-dvayam.

meanings.English: to think, to contemplate, to reflect upon, to worry

canonical_dhatvartha: prerane (to drive, to direct, to throw, to send)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣap' belongs to the tenth class (Curadi Gana) where the suffix 'ṇic' (-ay-) is added intrinsically to express driving, pushing forward, throwing, or causing movement. In Parasmaipada, the action directs outward, whereas in Atmanepada, the action reflects upon or pertains to oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svartha-nic suffix -aya- with Parasmaipada prathama-purusha eka-vacana (Active voice)
scenarios.example_english: The king dispatches an arrow (or sends a message).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svartha-nic suffix -aya- with Atmanepada prathama-purusha eka-vacana (Middle/Reflexive voice)
scenarios.example_english: The army chief directs the army for his own campaign.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṣapa' is taught in the sense of 'prerana' (impelling, throwing, or directing). Being in Curadi Gana, it obligatorily takes the 'nic' pratyaya by 'curo rnic' (3.1.25). Forms like kshapayati and kshapayate are derived without viddhi of internal vowels due to specific phonological conditioning.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'kṣapa prerane' as an impelling verb. It indicates active driving, sending forward, or propelling an object, behaving like a transitive causative-style stem throughout all tenses.

meanings.English: to direct, to impel, to throw, to send

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mūtr' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and inherently takes the 'ṇic' (ay) suffix to denote the biological action of passing urine or discharging fluid. Because it belongs to Curadigana, it can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings depending on whether the action or the result relates purely to the agent or not.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Lat Lakara
scenarios.example_english: The sick child urinates at night.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Lat Lakara
scenarios.example_english: The horse relieves itself on the road.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mūtra' is listed in Curadi under the meaning 'prasrāvane' (excretion/urination). Being in Curadigana, it obligatorily takes the 'ṇic' affix without requiring a causative sense, resulting in forms such as mūtrayati and amūmūtrat.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'mūtra prasrāve' as an adanta root occurring in the Curadi class that signifies natural excretion or discharge, forming derivatives with standard nic-guna operations.

meanings.English: to urinate, to discharge urine

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tarj' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi) and means 'to scold, threaten, or menace'. Because it is in Curadi, it intrinsically takes the affix 'nic' (forming tarjaya-) in non-causative active usage, functioning in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada. When used in active voice, the subject performs the act of intimidating or rebuking someone.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara (present tense), Parasmaipada, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The father scolds the misbehaving son.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara (present tense), Atmanepada, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she threatens / intimidates (with benefit/orientation toward oneself)
scenarios.example_english: The enemy threatens the warrior.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'tarja' belongs to the Curadi group in the sense of 'bhartsana' (rebuke, threat, or intimidation). It receives the swarthe-nic pratyaya obligatorily, yielding 'tarjayati' and 'tarjayate', behaving as an ordinary transitive verb governing the accusative case.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'tarja bhartsane' as a standard tenth-class root indicating censure, chiding, or frightening with words and gestures. As with Curadi verbs, the augment i (it) applies in the non-conjugational tenses.

meanings.English: to threaten, scold, censure, or menace
meanings.Bengali: dhomok deoa, torjon kora, bhoy dekhano

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣal' means 'to wash', 'to clean', or 'to purify'. As a member of the 10th class (Curadi gana), it inherently receives the 'ṇic' (ay) affix in standard usage. When used in Parasmaipada, the action generally focuses on the act of cleaning external objects; in Atmanepada, it often implies an action done for one's own sake or benefit.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Curadi nic affix, Parasmaipada, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy washes both his hands before the meal.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Curadi nic affix, Atmanepada, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The homemaker washes the soup bowls for herself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kṣala śaucakarmaṇi. Curādir ubhayapadī set. śaucakarma prakṣālanam. ata eva ṇau vṛddhau kṣālayati kṣālayate iti rūpe bhavataḥ. kṣālitam, kṣālakaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṣala śauce. śaucaṃ nirmalīkaraṇam, mala-apanayanam. curādau nic-antatvāt kṣālayatīti rūpam. cakṣuḥ kṣālayati, vastraṃ kṣālayati.

meanings.English: to wash, to clean, to cleanse, to purify

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rūp' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gaṇa). By default, roots in this class take the affix 'ṇic' (appearing as '-ay-') even in basic usage. It means 'to form', 'to shape', 'to depict', or 'to act out / portray on stage'. Being Ubhayapada, it accepts both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe ṇic + Parasmaipada (laṭ, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: He/she forms, depicts, or acts out
scenarios.example_english: The actor portrays the character of Rama on stage.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe ṇic + Ātmanepada (laṭ, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: He/she visualizes or creates a form for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The sculptor visualizes the form of the statue in his mind.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'rūpa' is listed under Curādi with the meaning 'rūpakriyāyām' (in the sense of bringing forth form, shaping, perceiving, or dramatic depiction). It takes svārthe ṇic, leading to forms such as rūpayati and rūpayate, with the reduplicated aorist form arūrūpat.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'rūpa rūpakriyāyām' as indicating the process of giving distinct visual manifestation or enacting representation (rūpasyāvirbhāvanam abhinayanam vā). It is treated as an Ubhayapadi root across classical usages.

meanings.English: to form, to shape, to represent, to depict, to act on stage
meanings.Hindi: roop dena, aakaar banana, abhinay dwara darshana
meanings.Bengali: roop dewa, aakar dewa, abhinoy kora
meanings.Russian: formirovat, pridavat formu, izobrazhat na stsene

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varn' belongs to the 10th group (Curadi gana) and naturally takes the suffix '-aya-' (nic) in its base forms. It means to describe, depict, paint, or praise. It can take either Parasmaipada or Atmanepada endings without changing its core meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-affix in Kartari prayoga (Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The poet describes nature.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Karmani prayoga (Passive voice, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The city is described by the author.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'varna' is listed under Curadi gana in the sense of 'varnane' (delineation, recounting, praise, and representation of qualities). Because it belongs to Curadi, it takes the svarthe nic affix obligatorily, forming bases like varnaya-.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'varna varnane' as expressing qualities, painting, or detailing descriptions. Being part of the Curadi group, it conjugates in both Padas with the formative suffix nic and follows regular seṭ patterns.

meanings.English: to describe, to depict, to praise, to paint

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mrad' belongs to the Curadi (10th) class and primarily means to crush, rub, pound, or soften. Because it is in Curadi gana, it intrinsically takes the affix 'nic' (-aya-). It can take Parasmaipada endings when focusing simply on the action of crushing or pounding an object, and Atmanepada endings when the action's effect or benefit is directed back to the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The physician crushes the medicine.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Atmanepada, Lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The farmer grinds grain for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mrad' is glossed as 'mrada mardane', indicating the semantic field of crushing, softening, grinding, or rubbing. Taking svarthe nic necessarily as a member of Curadi-gana, it forms bases with 'mradaya-' yielding 'mradayati' and 'mradayate'. In the aorist (lun), it takes the can affix forming 'amamradat'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'mrad mardane' in Curadigana denoting pressing, crushing down, or softening. The root forms standard Curadi causative-like active and middle forms with no vowel reduction because of its specific prosodic structure in this gana.

meanings.English: to crush, to rub, to grind, to soften
meanings.Chinese: nian mo, rou cuo, ya sui

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'suc' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes the mandatory 'nic' (ay) suffix across all non-causative conjugations. It means to indicate, hint, point out, or reveal hidden information. Because it is an Ubhayapadi root, it can take either Parasmaipada or Atmanepada endings without changing its core meaning, although Atmanepada is traditionally preferred when the result of informing or hinting directly benefits the speaker.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: curadi nic-pratyaya + lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana (Parasmaipada)
scenarios.example_english: Smoke indicates the presence of fire.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: curadi nic-pratyaya + lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana (Atmanepada)
scenarios.example_english: The sign reveals the hidden secret.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'suca' is glossed under 'bhedanapasparpanayoh', meaning to divide, pierce, spy out, or reveal through a hint or signal. As a Curadi root, it requires the svarthe nic affix, forming the derived base 'sucaya-', conjugated in both padas (sucayati, sucayate).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'suca bhedane pasparpane ca', explaining 'apasparpana' as secret exploration, detecting, or indicating subtly (gudhadutakarma/sucana), yielding forms like sucayati, asucat/asucisat.

meanings.English: to indicate, hint, point out, reveal, or spy
meanings.Hindi: sucita karna, sanketa dena, bhed kholna
meanings.Bengali: shuchita kara, ingita deoya, prakasha kara

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root curn belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes the suffix nic obligatorily in non-vedic usage. It primarily means to crush, grind into fine powder, pulverize, or contract/abridge (sanksepa). In everyday Sanskrit, it takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings without changing its core meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara (present tense), Parasmaipada, prathama-purusa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The cook crushes the medicine on the grinding stone.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara (present tense), Atmanepada, prathama-purusa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The youth reduces the collected matter into a concise form.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root curna sanksepe is listed in the Curadi gana. By the rule curader nic, it takes the affix nic obligatorily in general usage, forming curnayati and curnayate. Sanksepa refers to pulverizing, breaking into pieces, or condensing/summarizing.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes curna sanksepe: 'sanksepas curnikaranam'. It signifies the action of breaking an object down into its smallest atomic or powdered parts, as well as reducing bulk into a concise state.

meanings.English: to crush, pulverize, grind to powder, reduce, or abridge
meanings.Bengali: curna kora, gundo kora, sonkhipto kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'guṇ' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gaṇa). Verbs in this class compulsorily take the affix 'ṇic' (-aya-), making their basic active form look like a causative. In Parasmaipada (guṇayati), it denotes calling, addressing, or multiplying for others, whereas in Ātmanepada (guṇayate), the action directly affects or benefits the subject.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic, Parasmaipada, Laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The royal messenger invites the scholars to the assembly.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic, Ātmanepada (kartrabhiprāya), Laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The patron invites the priests for his own sacrifice.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'guṇa' is stated in the sense of 'āmantraṇa' (calling, greeting, or inviting). By the rule 'satyāpapāśarūpaveṇātulanślokasenālomattvacavarmavarṇacūrṇacurādibhyo ṇic', the affix ṇic is added inherently. Because it is a Curādi root, it takes both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada endings under general rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'guṇa āmantraṇe' as addressing or inviting ('āmantraṇaṃ sambodhanam'). The root does not undergo guṇa of the internal vowel due to the nature of the short vowel followed by a conjunct or single retroflex consonant in standard morphological derivations (guṇayati, guṇayate).

meanings.English: to invite, to address, to multiply

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kut' (often cited as 'kuti') belongs to the 10th class (Curadi Gana) and means 'to cut', 'to divide', or 'to split'. Because it belongs to Curadi, it intrinsically takes the affix 'nic' (forming the base 'kotaya-' or 'kuntaya-') in both active (Parasmaipada) and middle (Atmanepada) voices. It is used transitively when an agent cuts, chops, or sections an object.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The woodcutter cuts the timber.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The artisan cuts the wood for his own work.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'kuti chedane' in the Curadi class, highlighting the obligatory application of svarthe nic. The guna substitution yields the base 'kotaya-', conveying the sense of cutting or separating parts.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini glosses 'kuti' under 'chedane', stating that it shares morphological and semantic domains with roots signifying division, fracturing, and reducing objects into sections.

meanings.English: to cut, divide, split

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root puṭ belongs to the Curadi class, meaning it inherently takes the affix 'ṇic' even in its basic sense without needing a causative trigger. It means to fold, wrap, envelop, or connect together. Because it has a svarita accent marker from ṇic, it can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (active) and Atmanepada (middle/reflexive) forms without changing its core meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: Folds or wraps something for an external purpose
scenarios.example_english: The boy folds the letter.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: Folds or covers something for one's own self
scenarios.example_english: The mother folds the garment for herself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root puṭa is glossed in the context of saṃsarga (joining/connecting) and bhedana (dividing/separating). Since it belongs to the Curadi class, the svarthika ṇic suffix is added by default, yielding the base puṭi-. By virtue of ṇic carrying svarita intonation, it functions as an Ubhayapadi root resulting in forms like puṭayati and puṭayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes puṭa in the sense of saṃsarga (contact, enveloping, or folding into a hollow/cup-shape). It undergoes standard Guna modification of the penultimate short vowel 'u' before the ṇic suffix, forming the stem poṭayi- or retaining the unlengthened base depending on canonical adanta or mittva conventions.

meanings.English: to fold, envelop, wrap, intertwine, or divide
meanings.Hindi: lapetna, modna, samapta karna ya jodna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'gun' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and primarily conveys the sense of inviting, addressing, or enumerating qualities. Because it belongs to Curadi gana, it obligatorily receives the 'nic' suffix (forming gunaya-). In Parasmaipada, it means inviting or counting externally, whereas in Atmanepada, it can express the same action with the fruit accruing to oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she invites, addresses, or enumerates qualities.
scenarios.example_english: The teacher invites/addresses the disciples.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Atmanepada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she reflects upon or invites for oneself.
scenarios.example_english: The scholar ponders upon and enumerates good virtues.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti categorizes 'guna' under Curadi gana in the sense of 'amantrana' (inviting or addressing). By virtue of being in Curadi gana, it takes the affix 'nic' universally, forming the present stem 'gunaya-'. Being an adanta root within Curadi, it follows standard ubhayapada inflectional rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin interprets 'guna amantrane' as engaging in addressing, calling upon, or describing attributes. It undergoes complete pratyayanta derivation yielding 'gunayati' and 'gunayate' across active and reflexive domains.

meanings.English: To invite, address, enumerate, or advise
meanings.Hindi: Nimantran dena, bulana, gunon ka varnan karna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chad' belongs to the Curadi (10th) class and inherently takes the 'Nic' (ay) affix to mean 'to cover', 'to conceal', or 'to hide'. Being an Ubhayapadi root, it can take either Parasmaipada endings (when the action is directed outwards) or Atmanepada endings (when the action directly affects the subject or their own domain).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi Nic-pratyaya, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The cloud covers the sun.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi Nic-pratyaya, Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy covers his face with a cloth.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'chada samvarane' under the Curadi class, highlighting the svarthe-nic application ('chadayate', 'chadayati') to express covering, enclosing, or concealing an object completely.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'chada' signifies 'samvarana' (covering or shielding) and explains the retention and operation of the short and long vowel alternatives across specific derived nominals and verbal paradigms.

meanings.English: to cover, to conceal, to hide, to envelop

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'gaṇ' means to count, reckon, calculate, or consider. Belonging to the Curādi class, it inherently takes the affix 'ṇic' (making it 'gaṇi-') and conjugates in both voices. When used in Parasmaipada (gaṇayati) or Ātmanepada (gaṇayate), it expresses the act of counting objects or regarding someone/something in a specific way.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Active Voice (Kartari Prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy counts the books.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Middle Voice (Kartari Prayoga, Ātmanepada, Lat-lakara, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: He considers him as a true friend.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: gaṇa saṅkhyāne. curādiradantaḥ. saṅkhyānaṃ paricchedanam. ṇici gaṇayati gaṇayate. adantatvāt svārthe ṇic.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: gaṇa saṅkhyāne. gaṇayati. saṅkhyānaṃ parigaṇanā. adantāḥ curādayaḥ.

meanings.English: to count, to calculate, to reckon, to consider

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pīḍ' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi), which obligatorily takes the affix 'ṇic' (ay). It expresses distressing, afflicting, pressing, or tormenting. As an Ubhayapadī root, it takes Parasmaipada endings in general active statements, and Ātmanepada endings when the action directly affects oneself or in specific reflexive and passive contexts.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakāra, Prathama-puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: afflicts / oppresses / causes pain to another
scenarios.example_english: The disease afflicts the body.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic, Ātmanepada, Lat-lakāra, Prathama-puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The wicked person torments others for personal gain.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'pīḍṛ bādhāyām' is placed in the Curādi group. The ṛkāra is an it-marker indicating that the aorist (luṅ) takes the substitute can. By the general rule of the tenth class, it is conjugated with the affix ṇic in the intrinsic sense without altering the root's core meaning of causing distress or pressing.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'pīḍṛ bādhāyām' with the meaning of causing distress, harassment, or physical pressure. Being an ubiquitous tenth-class root, it retains guna and forms 'pīḍayati' and 'pīḍayate'.

meanings.English: to torment, to oppress, to afflict, to press, to harass
meanings.Hindi: satānā, pīṛit karnā, dukh denā, dabānā
meanings.Bengali: pīṛan karā, jālatana karā, kaṣṭa deoyā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'khad' belonging to the tenth conjugation (Curadi gana) primarily conveys the meaning of breaking, cleaving, splitting, or dividing something into pieces. Because it is a Curadi root, it naturally takes the affix 'nic' (forming the stem khadaya-). It can take endings of both Parasmaipada (active) and Atmanepada (middle), functioning transitively with an object.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-affix, Parasmaipada, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Lat-lakara
scenarios.example_english: The carpenter splits the timber.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-affix, Atmanepada, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Lat-lakara
scenarios.example_english: The farmer cleaves the boulder in the field.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'khada' is enumerated in Curadi with the semantic mark of bhedana (cleaving, splitting, dividing). Being inherently within the adanta-curadi or standard curadi class, it takes the svarthe nic suffix, resulting in forms like khadayati and khadayate. The presence of the short vowel 'a' leads to vriddhi or preservation depending on specific thematic treatment.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines 'khada' as conveying bhedana (breaking, tearing apart, fracturing). The root follows the standard Curadi derivation with intermediate it-agama in non-sarvadhatuka paradigms, yielding forms such as cakhadaya or khadayancakara.

meanings.English: to split, to break, to cleave, to divide

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root mūtr belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gaṇa). In this group, roots compulsorily take the affix 'ṇic' (aya) in their basic conjugational forms. It can be used in both Parasmaipada (mūtrayati) and Ātmanepada (mūtrayate) to mean discharging urine.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic affix with Parasmaipada prathama-puruṣa eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The child urinates after crying.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic affix with Ātmanepada prathama-puruṣa eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The animal urinates on the road.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: mūtra prasrāve. curādirantargataṇiṅantaḥ. mūtrayati, mūtrayate. ayaṃ svārthe ṇicpratyayāntaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: mūtra prasrāve. mūtrayatyuccāraṇam. curādau ṇicpratyayaḥ sidhyati.

meanings.English: to urinate, to discharge urine

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root tark belongs to the tenth conjugation (Curadi), meaning it obligatorily takes the affix nic (forming tarkaya-) in all general tenses. In classical usage, its core meaning of well-being (kalyana) and careful reasoning extends to examining, guessing, supposing, or wishing auspiciousness. It can take active endings (Parasmaipada) to convey the act of reasoning or blessing directly, or middle endings (Atmanepada) when the reflective benefit belongs to the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya with Parasmaipada lat-lakara (prathama-purusa ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: He/she reasons, examines, or wishes well
scenarios.example_english: The scholar analyzes the truth through logic.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya with Atmanepada lat-lakara (prathama-purusa ekavacana)
scenarios.meaning: He/she deliberates or ponders for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The student ponders the outcome within his own mind.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains root 'tarki' under the Curadi-gana with the primary meaning of 'kalyane' (auspiciousness, well-being, or blessing). Because of its idit status or Curadi class nature, it gets the nic suffix inherently, yielding forms like tarkayati and tarkayate, which also extend lexically to include critical thinking, conjecture, and philosophical reasoning.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'tarka' or 'tarki' is used in the sense of 'kalyane' (welfare and beneficial speculation). The derivation operates with the affix 'nic' by virtue of being in Curadi, forming 'tarkayati', connecting the root semantically to positive deliberation, examination, and benevolent intention.

meanings.English: to reason, reflect, guess, wish well, speculate
meanings.Bengali: tarka kara, cinta kara, mangala kamana kara
meanings.French: raisonner, conjecturer, supposer, souhaiter le bien

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'gan' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes an obligatory 'nic' (ay) suffix in its basic forms to express the act of counting, enumerating, or calculating. It can be used in both Parasmaipada (active focus) and Atmanepada (middle/self-reflexive focus) without changing its core meaning of enumeration.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga (active voice), Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy counts the fruits.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Karmani prayoga (passive voice), Atmanepada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The wealth is being counted by the accountant.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'gana sankhyane' under the Curadi group. Since it belongs to Curadi, the affix 'nic' applies in the sense of the root itself (svarthe nic). With the augment and vartana of nic, the base becomes 'ganaya', producing forms like ganayati and ganayate. The meaning is primarily enumerated quantification (sankhyana).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'gana sankhyane' that this root denotes counting and calculating objects systematically. It belongs to the adanta-prakarana of Curadi, requiring the nic suffix by default, and operates as an ubhayapadi root across all standard tenses.

meanings.English: To count, calculate, enumerate, reckon

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mad' in the 10th class (Curadi) means to satisfy, gladden, or delight someone. Because it belongs to Curadi gana, it naturally takes the causative-like suffix 'nic' (forming 'madaya-') and can take both active (Parasmaipada) and middle (Atmanepada) endings without changing its core meaning of causing joy or satisfaction.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (Present tense), Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The spring season immediately delights everyone.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Atmanepada, Lat lakara (Present tense), Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: Excellent music satisfies the connoisseurs.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya clarifies 'mada trptiyoge' as belonging to the Curadi class taking the affix nic intrinsically. It leads to the forms madayati and madayate in the sense of bringing about contentment, exhilaration, or full satisfaction (trpti-yojanam).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'mad' in Curadi is used in the sense of joining with satisfaction or causing exhilaration. Being a Curadi root, the affix nic is svarthe (inherent in the root meaning) or hetumannic.

meanings.English: to delight, to satisfy, to exhilarate, to gladden
meanings.Hindi: trpta karana, anandita karana, prasanna karana
meanings.Chinese: shi gaoxing, shi manyi, shi kuailuo

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varc' belongs to the Curadi class and means to shine, illuminate, or glow with brilliance. Because it is in the 10th class, it takes an inherent 'aya' (nic) suffix in its normal present forms. As an Ubhayapadi root, it can take Parasmaipada endings (varcayati) when focusing on the act of shining or illuminating an object, or Atmanepada endings (varcayate) when emphasizing the internal radiance or state of the subject.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya with Parasmaipada lat lakara prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The sun illuminates everything with its brilliance.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya with Atmanepada lat lakara prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The jewel glows radiantly by itself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'varca diptau' is taught in Curadi-gana. Taking the svarthe nic affix and pug-agama where applicable, it forms the base varcaya-. It is conjugated in both padas as varcayati and varcayate to signify radiant effulgence and shining.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'varca diptau' among roots signifying light and luster. The root forms varcayati/varcayate in the sense of prakasana (illumination) and tejas (glow).

meanings.English: to shine, to illuminate, to glow
meanings.Bengali: ujjvala haoya, alo deoya, dipita haoya

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'math' belonging to the Curadi class means to cause pain, harass, disturb, or agitate thoroughly. Because it belongs to the tenth class, it compulsorily takes the affix 'nic' even in its basic active meaning. It can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (e.g., mathayati) and Atmanepada (e.g., mathayate) without changing its core meaning of tormenting or churning/disturbing.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svārthe nic, Parasmaipada, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana, Lat-lakara
scenarios.example_english: The disease torments the body.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svārthe nic, Atmanepada, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana, Lat-lakara
scenarios.example_english: Anxiety troubles the mind.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes 'matha saṅkleśe' in the Curadi class, denoting the infliction of distress, anguish, or severe agitation. Being in the tenth gana, the affix nic is applied in svārtha, and by regular morphophonemic rules, it yields forms like mathayati and mathayate in the present tense.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin analyzes 'matha' within the Curadi inventory signifying affliction (saṅkleśa) and perturbation. It indicates inner or outer turmoil and follows standard set adanta Curadi conjugation across all lakaras.

meanings.English: to torment, to harass, to afflict, to agitate
meanings.Hindi: peedit karna, klesh dena, mathna ya vikkhubdh karna
meanings.Bengali: klesha deoya, piran kara, mathan kara

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'hṛṣ' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curādigaṇa), where the affix 'ṇic' is applied inherently, forming the verbal base 'harṣaya-'. While in the 4th conjugation (hṛṣyati) it means 'to be happy or excited', in the 10th conjugation it is transitive and means 'to gladden' or 'to cause joy to another'. It can take both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada endings.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi ṇic-pratyaya with Parasmaipada (Kartari prayoga, Laṭ, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The teacher gladdens the student with kind words.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi ṇic-pratyaya with Ātmanepada (Kartari prayoga, Laṭ, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The mother delights her own mind with the beauty of the child.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'hṛṣa' in Curādigaṇa is taught in the sense of 'harṣaṇa' (causing joy / producing happiness). By the rule 'curādibhyo ṇic' (Pānini 3.1.25), it obligatorily takes the affix ṇic. The vowel 'ṛ' undergoes Guṇa replacement to 'ar' before the affix, producing the base 'harṣaya-', which conjugates in both padas.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes that in Curādi, 'hṛṣa' is distinctly causative/transitive in meaning ('harṣaṇe' - the act of producing gladness or excitement in another), distinguishing it from Divādi 'hṛṣyati' which is intransitive ('tuṣṭau').

meanings.English: To gladden, to cause joy, to delight
meanings.Hindi: Harṣita karnā, prasanna karnā, khuśa karnā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pāl' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curādi gaṇa) and inherently carries the affix 'ṇic' (ay) in its basic forms without changing its basic meaning, signifying 'to protect', 'to preserve', or 'to rule'. Because it is an Ubhayapadī verb, it can take active Parasmaipada endings (pālayati) as well as middle Ātmanepada endings (pālayate).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic, Parasmaipada, Laṭ lakāra, Prathama puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: protects / guards / governs (for the sake of another/general action)
scenarios.example_english: The king protects the citizens righteously.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe-ṇic, Ātmanepada, Laṭ lakāra, Prathama puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: protects / maintains (reflecting back upon oneself or taking personal responsibility)
scenarios.example_english: The master sustains his own servants with affection.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'pāla' is listed under Curādi gaṇa in the sense of 'rakṣaṇa' (guarding, protecting, preserving). As an inherently ṇyanta (svārthe ṇic) base, it forms 'pālayati' and 'pālayate'. In perfect tense (liṭ), it takes the periphrastic form 'pālayāñcakāra' or 'pālayāmāsa'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes 'pāla rakṣaṇe' as a transitive root signifying the act of safeguarding, maintaining, or fostering. Derivations include nominal stems like 'pāla', 'pālaka', and 'pālana', denoting protectors and the act of maintenance.

meanings.English: to protect, to guard, to govern, to maintain, to rear
meanings.Bengali: rakṣā karā, pālan karā, poṣaṇ karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tap' in the 10th class (Curadi) means to exercise supreme lordship, power, or to display might and authority. Because it takes the essential 'nic' affix (forming 'tapaya-'), it can take either Parasmaipada or Atmanepada endings. In active usage, it signifies heating, ruling over with power, or exercising majesty.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi affix 'nic' with Parasmaipada prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: exercises power over / rules majestically / causes distress to enemies by power
scenarios.example_english: The king overpowers and subdues his enemies by his might.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi affix 'nic' with Atmanepada prathama-purusha eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: exercises authority / enjoys sovereignty for oneself
scenarios.example_english: The monarch exercises sovereignty through his own majesty.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Curadi root 'tapa' is taught in the sense of lordship, majesty, and exertion of strength ('aishvaryabalakarmasu'). Being an adanta root of Curadi gana, the affix 'nic' is inherently added by 'satya-pasha-rupashloka-tula-roca-kula-krtsna-vedibhyo nyak' and related Curadi sutras, leading to the formation of 'tapayati' and 'tapayate'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'tapa' in Curadi signifies exercising supreme authority ('aishvarye') as well as mighty physical or administrative action ('balakarmani'). Its forms exhibit the obligatory 'i' (nic) augment characteristic of the tenth conjugation.

meanings.English: to exercise sovereignty, to wield power, to dominate, to rule over
meanings.Kannada: prabhutva calayisu, aishvarya torisu, balaprayoga madu
meanings.Telugu: prabhutvamu celayincu, adhikaranni pradarshincu, balaprayogamu ceyu
meanings.Tamil: athikarathai seluthu, aatchi sei, thirambada aalu
meanings.Malayalam: adhipathyam sthapikkuka, aishvaryam kanikkuka, shakthi prayogikkuka
meanings.Hindi: aishvarya ya prabhutva dikhana, shakti ka prayoga karna, shasan karna
meanings.Bengali: probhutvo kora, aishvorjo prokkhas kora, shokti proyog kora
meanings.French: regner, exercer le pouvoir, dominer avec autorite
meanings.Chinese: shi zhan quan li, tong zhi, xian shi wei li

canonical_dhatvartha: citrīkaraṇe saṃskāre ca (in the sense of painting, adorning, variegated decorating, or causing wonder)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'citr' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi Gana) where it inherently takes the affix 'nic' (forming the stem 'citraya-'). In Parasmaipada, it highlights the action directed externally, such as painting a picture or decorating a surface. In Atmanepada, it denotes engaging in artistic creation or decoration where the fruit or process intimately reflects upon the agent. It can also signify making something remarkably varied or wondrous.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Kartari Prayoga (Active Voice, Parasmaipada, 3rd Person Singular, Present Tense)
scenarios.meaning: Paints, depicts, or decorates something beautifully
scenarios.example_english: The artist paints a beautiful picture on the wall.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Kartari Prayoga (Active Voice, Atmanepada, 3rd Person Singular, Present Tense)
scenarios.meaning: Decorates for oneself or wonders/acts in a multifaceted creative manner
scenarios.example_english: The girl decorates her home with various flowers.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that the root 'citri' operates in the Curadi class under the meaning 'citrīkaraṇe' (producing variegated colors, forms, or imagery). It inherently takes the 'ṇic' pratyaya without necessitating a separate causative trigger from outside, taking standard Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings (citrayati, citrayate) and admitting it-agama in non-conjugational formations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin indicates that 'citri' denotes making something 'citra' (diverse, multifaceted, adorned, or surprising). He notes the application across plastic arts, drawing, and figurative ornamentation, showing forms like citrayati, acicitat, and the past passive participle citrita.

meanings.English: to paint, decorate, depict, variegate, adorn, or surprise
meanings.Hindi: chitrana karna, tasvir banana, sajāna, alankrit karna
meanings.Bengali: chitra ankan kora, shojjito kora, alankrito kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varn' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means to describe, portray, praise, or color. Because it is in Curadi gana, it naturally takes the suffix 'nic' (forming varnaya-). When the action of describing is done for someone else or neutrally, it is used in Parasmaipada (varnayati); when done reflecting on oneself, it can be used in Atmanepada (varnayate).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara (present tense), Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The poet describes the beauty of nature.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat-lakara (present tense), Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The reflective person recounts intuitive knowledge within oneself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'varna' is classified under Curadi-gana with the semantic meaning 'varnane' (detailed description, depiction, or coloring). By the rule 'satya-pasha-rupa-vina-tula-shloka-sena-loma-tvaca-varma-varna-curna-curadibhyo nic', it takes the obligatory 'nic' affix in all tenses and moods without requiring causative meaning, forming bases like varnayati and varnayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'varna varnane' as expressing elaboration, articulation, depiction of qualities, and applying color or painting. The formation proceeds with the svarthe-nic marker to yield 'varnayati'.

meanings.English: to describe, depict, praise, or color

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cel' belongs to the Curadi class and means 'to contract', 'to shrink', or 'to cause to narrow'. Because it belongs to the 10th class, it naturally takes the affix 'nic' (forming celaya-). In Parasmaipada, it highlights an action directed outward, whereas in Atmanepada, it can express the action taking place for oneself.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe nic, Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The tortoise contracts its limbs.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe nic, Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: It shrinks or contracts within itself
scenarios.example_english: The cloth shrinks by being washed.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: cela sankocane - curadigana svarthe nic-pratyayah. celayati, celayate. sankoco nama sanksepena avasthanam avayavanam paraspara-nikatatvam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: cela sankocane. curadirmitvat parasmaipadam atmanepadam ca dharayati. celayati, acicelat.

meanings.English: to contract, shrink, compress

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root puth belongs to the Curadi class, meaning it inherently takes the affix nic (forming pothaya-) to express the action of striking, hurting, or crushing. It can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada without losing its core active meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi class with standard Parasmaipada inflection (nic + sap + ti)
scenarios.example_english: The warrior crushes the enemy with a mace.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi class with standard Atmanepada inflection (nic + sap + te)
scenarios.meaning: inflicts pain or crushes (with self-directed focus/interest)
scenarios.example_english: The formidable warrior strikes down the adversary.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root putha is enumerated in Curadi gana in the sense of violence, destruction, or causing distress (himsayam). Taking the obligatory svaarthe nic pratyaya, the vowel undergoes guna yielding pothayati and pothayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes putha himsarthah, emphasizing the application of force to subdue, strike, or crush an opponent in battle or harmful encounters.

meanings.English: to hurt, strike, crush, or destroy
meanings.Hindi: hinsa karna, marna, kootna ya nasht karna
meanings.Bengali: hingsha kora, aghat kora, dhongsho kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'drbh' means to string together, weave, arrange, or compose. Belonging to the 10th class (Curadi), it inherently takes the affix 'nic' (forming verbal stems ending in -aya). It can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (active voice) and Atmanepada (middle voice), expressing the act of composing or stringing items like flowers or verses together.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat lakara (present tense), Parasmaipada, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The poet composes verses.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Lat lakara (present tense), Atmanepada, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The garland maker strings flowers together for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'drbhi' belongs to the Curadi group in the sense of 'sandarbha' (stringing together, connecting, composing). Because it is in the Curadi class, the formative affix 'nic' is inherently added, undergoing guna to form 'darbhaya-'. It takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings under standard Curadi rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'drbhi sandarbhe' as denoting the systematic weaving, joining, or arranging of words or objects into a structured whole, yielding the verbal base 'darbhayati' / 'darbhayate'.

meanings.English: to string together, compose, weave, arrange

canonical_dhatvartha: badhayam (in the sense of tormenting, oppressing, or pressing)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pid' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi Gana) and inherently takes the affix 'nic' (forming 'piday-'). It expresses distressing, inflicting pain, bothering, or physical squeezing/pressing. In Parasmaipada, it indicates standard action directed toward an object, whereas in Atmanepada it can convey action reflecting on the agent or self-involvement.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'pida badhayam' belongs to the Curadi group. Taking the mandatory svarthanic pratyaya, it yields 'pidayati' in Parasmaipada and 'pidayate' in Atmanepada. Reduplicated aorist (lun) yields 'apipidat' with shortening of the radical vowel according to grammatical rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'pida badhayam' as denoting afflictive torment or mechanical pressing. Forms include 'pidayati', 'pidayam cakara' in lit, and derived nouns such as 'pida' (suffering, oppression).

meanings.English: to torment, oppress, hurt, or press

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'carth' belongs to the Curadi class (10th conjugation) and carries the meaning of begging, asking, or requesting. Because it belongs to the Curadi class, it inherently takes the affix 'nic' without altering its primary meaning (svarthe nic). In modern pedagogical practice, it can take Parasmaipada forms (such as carthayati) when the action is performed generally, and Atmanepada forms (such as carthayate) when the fruit or intent of the request specifically benefits the speaker.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svartha nic, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara, prathama purusha, ekavacana

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti identifies 'carthi yacanayam' under the Curadi group. Since it includes an idit marker (indicatory letter 'i'), it takes a penultimate nasal in its base formation. It takes svabhavika nic (svartha nic) forming the verbal base carthaya-, yielding carthayati and carthayate in active usage representing the act of petitioning, begging, or asking for help.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'carthi yacanayam' in the 10th gana as expressing solicitation or begging (yacana). It undergoes nic-pratyaya obligatorily by rule, forming carthayati, and follows standard Curadi conjugational paradigms for set roots taking full guṇa/affix application.

meanings.English: to beg, to ask for, to solicit, to request

canonical_dhatvartha: calane (to shake, to move, to waver, to agitate)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'hval' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi Gana) and takes the mandatory affix 'nic' (-aya-). It expresses shaking, moving, or causing to waver. In the Parasmaipada voice, it is used when the motion is directed externally or neutrally, while in the Atmanepada voice, it signifies shaking or agitation affecting oneself.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'hvala calane' that the root denotes physical movement, shaking, or staggering (calana). In the Curadi class, it produces forms such as 'hvalayati' and 'hvalayate', behaving analogously to roots of agitation and motion.

meanings.English: to shake, to move, to waver, to cause to stagger

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kal' means to count, reckon, or enumerate. Falling under the 10th class (Curadi), it obligatorily takes the 'nic' suffix (aya) in normal active forms without altering its base meaning, functioning in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada. When used in Parasmaipada or Atmanepada, it denotes computing or assessing something.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kala sankhyane. sankhyanam gananam. kalayati, kalayate. ayam adantah curadirapi ganane vartate.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The Curadi root kṣep expresses the action of sending, throwing, or impelling. Because it belongs to the 10th class, it obligatorily takes the affix 'ṇic' (making the base kṣepaya-) in ordinary active usage. It can take either Parasmaipada endings (kṣepayati) or Atmanepada endings (kṣepayate) without changing its core meaning of sending or impelling.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kath' means to tell, recount, or narrate a connected story or sentences. Because it belongs to the 10th group (Curadi-gana), it inherently takes the affix 'nic' (-ay-), resulting in the base 'kathaya-'. It can take endings in both Parasmaipada (kathayati) and Atmanepada (kathayate) with the same basic meaning of narrating or describing.
