The semantic scope 'vākyaprabandha' specifies speech consisting of syntactically and logically connected sentences rather than isolated words. It forms kathayati and kathayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'katha vākyaprabandhe' as denoting coherent exposition or continuous storytelling. Because it is in the Curadi class, the formative suffix 'nic' is always present, yielding the verbal stem kathaya- across all tenses.

meanings.English: to tell, narrate, recount, relate a story

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mārg' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi), meaning it inherently takes the affix 'ṇic' (-aya-) in its standard non-causative form to mean 'to search', 'to seek', or 'to track'. Because it is Ubhayapadī, it can be conjugated in either Parasmaipada (active endings like -ti) or Ātmanepada (middle endings like -te) without changing its essential meaning of seeking or inquiring.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varn' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi), which naturally takes the 'nic' suffix (forming 'varnay-'). It means to describe, portray, praise, or paint. dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varn' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi) and means to describe, depict, praise, or paint. vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: bhūṣa alaṅkāre. curādirantargatanik. bhūṣayati, bhūṣayate. alaṅkaraṇam vibhūṣaṇam. seṭ, ubhayapadī.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: bhūṣa alaṅkāre. svārthe ṇic. alaṅkāraḥ śobhākaraṇam. bhūṣayati, bhūṣayate. vibhūṣitaḥ, bhūṣaṇam ityādayaḥ prayogāḥ.

meanings.English: to decorate, adorn, ornament, embellish

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'jharca' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and inherently takes the 'nic' affix (forming jharci/jharcay-) in the sense of studying, reciting, or repetitive learning. It can be used in Parasmaipada or Atmanepada without shifting the basic meaning of focused recitation and learning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Curadi svarthe nic, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she studies or recites text repetitively.
scenarios.example_english: The student recites and studies the Vedic mantra.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Curadi svarthe nic, Atmanepada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she engages in deep study for personal mastery.
scenarios.example_english: The pupil studies the treatise intently by himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti places 'jharca adhyayane' within the Curadi group of roots expressing study and recitation. As a Curadi root, the affix nic is applied svarthe (in the intrinsic sense of the root) by rule 'satyapapasa...', forming the base 'jharcaya-'. Being marked with anudatta or svarita characteristics, it yields forms in Parasmaipada and Atmanepada with standard set augment (it).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'jharca adhyayane' alongside allied repetitive-phoneme roots of study (carca, curca, churca). The primary semantic scope is continuous recitation, critical repetition, or deep systematic study of traditional shastric texts.

meanings.English: to study, to recite repeatedly, to learn diligently
meanings.Hindi: adhyayan karna, baar-baar padhna, abhyas karna
meanings.Bengali: adhyayona kora, bar bar path kora, abhyasa kora
meanings.French: etudier, reciter de maniere repetee, apprendre assidument
meanings.Russian: izuchat, povtoryat pri chtenii, userdno uchit

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dam' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means to tame, subdue, calm down, or control. Because it inherently takes the 'nic' affix (forming 'damaya'), it can be used in both Parasmaipada (active voice towards an external object) and Atmanepada (middle voice where the action reflects inward or upon oneself).

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Parasmaipada, Prathama-purusha, Eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The king subdues the enemies.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya, Atmanepada, Prathama-purusha, Eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: Tames, restrains for oneself, or exercises self-control
scenarios.example_english: The sage restrains his own mind.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'damu upashame' in the Curadi class. It takes the inherent nic pratyaya to express calming down, subduing, or taming. The root retains the short 'a' due to mit-samjna rules or forms 'damayati/damayate' with penultimate vowel retention under specific conditions, operating as an Ubhayapada verb in the sense of upashama (cessation/pacification).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini explains 'damu upashame' as denoting the pacification of sensory agitations, anger, or external foes. It operates in the tenth class with both active and middle endings without change in core root significance.

meanings.English: to tame, subdue, control, or pacify
meanings.Hindi: daman karna, vash me karna, shant karna
meanings.Bengali: domon kora, shanto kora, boshibhuto kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varṣ' belongs to the 10th group (Curadi Gana) and means 'to urge', 'to impel', or 'to motivate'. Because it is in the 10th class, it always takes the affix 'ṇic' (making 'varṣaya-'). It can be used in Parasmaipada when the action affects someone else, and in Atmanepada when the effect returns to the subject.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi-ṇic (Parasmaipada, Kartari prayoga, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: He/she urges, impels, or motivates another
scenarios.example_english: The teacher urges the student toward knowledge.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi-ṇic (Atmanepada, Kartari prayoga, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.meaning: He/she impels or urges for one's own purpose
scenarios.example_english: The master directs the servant in work for his own benefit.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'varṣa preraṇe' under the Curadi class. By the general rule for 10th-class roots, the affix ṇic is added inherently, yielding the base varṣi- which inflects as varṣayati and varṣayate. Its primary lexical scope here is motivation or directing effort (preraṇa).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'varṣa preraṇe' that this root denotes impelling or urging action. It is distinct in this class from the Bhvadi root vṛṣu (sektā), taking obligatory curadi-ṇic morphology to convey motivating or impelling.

meanings.English: to impel, to urge, to motivate, to direct

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'laks' belongs to the Curadi class and takes the suffix 'nic' by default in svarta (inherent sense). It means to look at, observe, notice, or aim at something. When used in Parasmaipada (laksayati), it denotes the active act of observing or perceiving an object. In Atmanepada (laksayate), it highlights self-oriented observation or reflection.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svārthe ṇic, Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat lakāra, Prathama puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy observes the stars in the sky.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Karmaṇi prayoga (Passive), Lat lakāra, Prathama puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: Is observed / is seen / is noticed
scenarios.example_english: A mountain is observed in the distance.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'laksa alocane' as an adanta root in the Curadi class. By default, it takes the affix 'nic' in the root's inherent sense (svartha). It carries the sense of alocana (careful perception, viewing, or marking), yielding forms such as laksayati and laksayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under Curadi that 'laksa' signifies both alocana (intellectual or visual inspection) and ankana (marking/characterizing). Due to the inherent nic-pratyaya of the tenth gana, it derives standard forms like laksayati.

meanings.English: to observe, perceive, notice, mark, aim at

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root pāl belongs to the tenth class (curādigaṇa) and fundamentally means to protect, guard, foster, or govern. Because it belongs to curādigaṇa, it obligatorily takes the affix ṇic (appearing as -ay-), forming the present stem pālay-. It can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (pālayati) and Ātmanepada (pālayate). When used in Parasmaipada, the focus of the action of protecting or ruling is directed outward toward the object, whereas Ātmanepada indicates the protection or maintenance undertaken with direct relevance or interest to the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, parasmaipada, laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The king protects his subjects with righteousness.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: kartari prayoga, ātmanepada, laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she maintains or fosters for oneself / observes a vow
scenarios.example_english: The sage faithfully observes and maintains his vow.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root pāla is entered under curādigaṇa with the semantic definition rakṣaṇe (in the sense of protecting or guarding). It takes the svārthika ṇic pratyaya obligatorily by rule curādibhyo ṇic. Because it is a non-anubandha root of curādi, it operates as ubhayapadi, yielding the present active forms pālayati and pālayate, and the perfect forms pālayāñcakāra and pālayāmāsa.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes pāla in the sense of rakṣaṇa (preservation and protection). As a curādi root, it exhibits universal affixation of ṇic in all universal conjugations, forming pālayati/pālayate. The root functions transitively (sakarmaka) governing the object protected in the accusative case.

meanings.English: to protect, guard, maintain, rule, nurture
meanings.Bengali: rakṣā karā, pālan karā, paricaryā karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kīrt' belongs to the 10th group (Curādi gaṇa) and means to praise, glorify, mention, or recount. Because it is in the 10th gaṇa, it always takes the suffix 'ṇic' (which shows up as 'aya') in ordinary active usage, giving forms like 'kīrtayati' (he praises or recites). It can be used in Parasmaipada when describing general action or praising others, and in Ātmanepada ('kīrtayate') when the speaker/agent is intimately connected to the celebration or action.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Kartari prayoga (Active Voice), Parasmaipada, 3rd Person Singular
scenarios.example_english: The devotee praises the virtues of the Lord.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Karmaṇi prayoga (Passive Voice), Ātmanepada, 3rd Person Singular
scenarios.example_english: The fame of the hero is praised everywhere.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kīrta saṃsane' (also read as saṃśabdane) belongs to the Curādi class. It takes the obligatory affix ṇic by the standard rule for Curādi roots. In the aorist (luṅ), it forms the reduplicated stem 'acīkīrtat' following the normal phonological processes of ṇyanta stems.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines the root in the sense of uttering or describing qualities and virtues with praise (guṇasaṃkīrtana). The standard derived present-tense base is 'kīrtaya-', generating forms across both active and middle paradigms.

meanings.English: To praise, celebrate, mention, narrate, or recite
meanings.Hindi: Kīrtan karnā, praśaṃsā karnā, guṇagān karnā
meanings.Bengali: Kīrtan karā, praśaṃsā karā, vivaraṇa deoyā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lakṣ' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gaṇa) and inherently takes the 'ṇic' suffix (-aya-), forming the base 'lakṣaya-'. It means to observe, notice, behold, or aim at. Because it has a svarita accent marker in the gaṇa, it operates in both Parasmaipada (lakṣayati) and Ātmanepada (lakṣayate) without changing its core meaning.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe ṇic + Parasmaipada (laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy observes the stars in the sky.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi svārthe ṇic + Ātmanepada (laṭ, prathama-puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The sage perceives the ultimate truth within himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'lakṣa ālocane' is listed in Curādi gaṇa. Being a Curādi root, the affix ṇic is added obligatorily by rule 'satyāpapāśarūpa...curādibhyo ṇic' in the sense of the root itself (svārthe). By virtue of ṇit-pratyaya, it takes both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada endings.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'lakṣa ālocane' as expressing sight, observation, and mental perception. The form develops into 'lakṣayati' and 'lakṣayate' through the mandatory addition of the suffix ṇiñ/ṇic.

meanings.English: to observe, to perceive, to notice, to mark

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'par' belongs to the 10th verb class (Curadi gana) and inherently takes the 'nic' suffix (forming paraya-). It means reaching the other side, overcoming an obstacle, completing an action, or being able to manage a difficult task.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe nic, Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, Parasmaipada, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: Completes, overcomes, or reaches the end of an undertaking
scenarios.example_english: The student manages and solves the difficult question.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe nic, Kartari prayoga, Lat lakara, Atmanepada, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The courageous person overcomes the crisis.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: pāra tīrakarmaṇi. tīrakarma nāma tīragamanaṃ karmaṇaḥ samāptirvā. svārthe ṇic. pārayati, pārayate. ṇijantatvāt sarvatra rūpāṇi bhavanti.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: pāra tīrakarmaṇi. pāraṃ tīram, tasya karma pāraṇaṃ niṣpādanam. antagamanaṃ karmasampādanaṃ cetyarthaḥ.

meanings.English: to accomplish, to complete, to finish, to cross over, to overcome, to be able
meanings.Telugu: pūrti cēyu, samāptamu cēyu, dāṭu, sādhincu
meanings.Hindi: pūrā karnā, samāpta karnā, pār karnā, sāmarthya honā
meanings.Bengali: shēṣa karā, pūraṇa karā, pār karā, samāpta karā
meanings.French: accomplir, mener a terme, surmonter, traverser

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'śūl' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi), meaning it obligatorily takes the '-aya-' affix to express experiencing or causing acute pain, aching, or piercing discomfort (like a spear/śūla). In active usage, it denotes that an organ hurts or something causes pain to a person.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi ṇic-pratyaya in Parasmaipada, Lat-lakāra (Present tense, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy's stomach aches.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi ṇic-pratyaya in Ātmanepada, Lat-lakāra (Present tense, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The head throbs with pain due to the severe cold wind.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'śūla' is read in the Curādi-gaṇa with the meaning 'rujāyām' (in the sense of affliction or piercing pain). Being adanta in upadeśa, the svārthika ṇic-pratyaya is mandatorily attached, forming the present bases śūlayati and śūlayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin identifies 'śūla rujāyām' as conveying intense bodily anguish, piercing distress, or colic, semantically interconnected with the noun 'śūla' (spear/trident or acute pain).

meanings.English: To pain, to ache, to cause acute distress or colic
meanings.Bengali: Bēthanā dēoyā, bēdanā deoyā, kaṣṭa dēoyā
meanings.French: Faire mal, causer de la douleur, faire souffrir

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bhaṭ' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curādi-gaṇa) and means to hire, support, or maintain someone with wages or food. Because it belongs to Curādi, it compulsorily takes the affix 'ṇic' (-aya-) in all basic conjugations. It can take either Parasmaipada endings (bhaṭayati) or Ātmanepada endings (bhaṭayate) to denote maintaining or sustaining someone.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi ṇic-pratyaya, Parasmaipada, Laṭ lakāra (present tense), prathama-puruṣa (3rd person), ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The master hires and maintains the workers.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi ṇic-pratyaya, Ātmanepada, Laṭ lakāra (present tense), prathama-puruṣa (3rd person), ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: sustains / hires for one's own service
scenarios.example_english: The king employs and sustains soldiers for his service.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: bhaṭa bhṛtau - curādirubhayapadī seṭ. bhṛtiḥ nāma vetanādinā poṣaṇam ucyate. curādau svārthe ṇic. bhaṭayati, bhaṭayate. bibhaṭayiṣati, bibhaṭayiṣate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: bhaṭa bhṛtau - vetanadānena bharaṇe ityarthaḥ. ubhayato bhāṣā. bhaṭayati, bhaṭayate.

meanings.English: to hire, to pay wages, to maintain, to support
meanings.Hindi: vetan dena, bharaṇa-poṣaṇa karnā, naukar rakhnā
meanings.Bengali: betan deoa, poshon kora, bhoronposhon kora
meanings.German: in Dienst nehmen, entlohnen, verköstigen, unterhalten
meanings.Russian: nanimat na sluzhbu, soderzhat, vyplachivat zhalovane

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'pal' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi gana) and carries the meaning 'to protect, guard, or rule'. Because it belongs to Curadi gana, it obligatorily takes the affix 'nic' (forming the stem 'palaya-'). When conjugated in Parasmaipada (palayati), it denotes the active protection of others. In Atmanepada (palayate), it can express the protection undertaken for one's own domain or self-interest.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The king protects the citizens righteously.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat lakara, Prathama Purusha, Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The mother affectionately cares for and protects her own child.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya glosses 'pala rakshane' in Curadigana. It is classified as an adanta root taking the mandatory svarthanic pratyaya. The primary forms include the present active 'palayati', middle 'palayate', and the reduplicated aorist 'apipalat' and 'apipalata' in the primary sense of protection, defense, and administration.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin categorizes 'pala rakshane' under the Curadi class, highlighting its specific semantic value of shielding from harm, sustaining, and preserving living beings or kingdoms.

meanings.English: to protect, to guard, to nourish, to govern

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chad' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and carries the meaning of covering, concealing, or shielding. Because it naturally takes the suffix 'nic' (svarthe nic), it forms verbs like chadayanti/chadayate in both active and middle voices. In Parasmaipada, it highlights the general action of covering an object, whereas in Atmanepada, it emphasizes covering for one's own protection or internal benefit.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi class with Parasmaipada present active suffix
scenarios.meaning: They cover or conceal something externally
scenarios.example_english: Clouds cover the sun.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi class with Atmanepada present middle suffix
scenarios.example_english: The child covers his body with a cloth.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti explains 'chada samvarane' under the Curadi gana as taking the inherent causative-like affix 'nic' without altering its root sense of covering, veiling, or concealing. It notes the lengthening (vriddhi) of the penultimate vowel, producing forms such as chadayanti and acachadat.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini establishes that 'chada' denotes 'samvarana' (covering, enveloping, screening from view). It is characterized by inherent nic-pratyaya (svarthe nic) and accepts both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings across classical conjugation.

meanings.English: to cover, conceal, hide, clothe, shield

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chur' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means 'to cut', 'to sever', or 'to slice'. Because it is in the Curadi group, it inherently receives the affix 'nic' (giving the stem form 'churaya-') without needing an external causal trigger. It can take both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings depending on whether the action's fruit is intended generally or for the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Parasmaipada, Lat lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The farmer cuts the branch of the tree with an instrument.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kartari prayoga, Atmanepada (self-directed action), Lat lakara, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The cook slices the fruit for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'chura chedane' is listed in Curadi under the meaning of splitting or severing. It takes the affix 'nic' svarthe (in its own root sense). Due to being adanta-curadi or standard curadi, it forms 'churayati' and 'churayate'. The vowel 'u' remains short and does not undergo guna because it is followed by the conjunct or root-final conditions.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains 'chura chedane' as indicating the act of splitting into parts or severing ('chedanam dvidhakaranam'). It is distinguished from the root 'cur steye' by its specific semantic assignment to cutting and division.

meanings.English: to cut, to slice, to sever, to divide

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root cūrṇ belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gaṇa). In this class, the verb naturally receives the affix -aya- (ṇic). It primarily means to crush, powder, or reduce something into fine particles, and can also mean to abbreviate or summarize. When used in Parasmaipada (cūrṇayati), the action is directed outwardly, whereas in Ātmanepada (cūrṇayate), the outcome is directed towards the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi-pratyaya ṇic with Parasmaipada prathama-puruṣa eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The physician crushes the medicine into powder.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi-pratyaya ṇic with Ātmanepada prathama-puruṣa eka-vacana
scenarios.meaning: Crushes or grinds for one's own purpose
scenarios.example_english: The cook grinds the grain for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Under the entry 'cūrṇa saṅkṣepe', Madhava explains that the root is used in the sense of condensing, pulverizing, or reducing to smaller parts. By the general rule 'curādibhyo ṇic', it obligatorily takes the ṇiñ affix in svārthe (its own meaning), yielding the forms cūrṇayati and cūrṇayate across both voices.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'cūrṇa' implies peṣaṇa (grinding/crushing) as well as saṅkṣepa (reduction/condensation). As an adanta/curādi element, it is seṭ and ubiquitously maintains the causal-like affix -aya- across all conjugational tenses and derivatives such as cūrṇita.

meanings.English: To crush, to pulverize, to powder, to reduce
meanings.Bengali: Gũṛo karā, cūrṇa karā, piṣe phelā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root cit belongs to the Curadi class and signifies becoming conscious, perceiving, reflecting, or causing to realize. Because it belongs to the 10th class, it obligatorily takes the affix nic, forming present tense stems like cetayati or cetayate. In Parasmaipada, the subject brings awareness or perceives something externally; in Atmanepada, the awareness or internal cognitive process is experienced reflexively.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe-nic, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.meaning: He/she awakens, makes aware, or perceives consciously
scenarios.example_english: The teacher makes the student aware of righteousness.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi svarthe-nic, Lat lakara, Prathama purusha, Ekavacana, Atmanepada
scenarios.meaning: He/she reflects internally or experiences conscious awareness
scenarios.example_english: The sage internally contemplates the ultimate truth within the heart.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Citi sancetane. Sancetanam jnanam samjnanam ca. Curadau nic svarthe bhavati. Cetayati, cetayate. Gunah sarvadhatukardhadhatukayoh iti gunapratih.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Citi sancetane. Cetayati. Sancetanam bodhanam jnanam iti kshirasvami. Ubhayapadi ayam dhathuh nic-pratyayantasya prayogatvat.

meanings.English: to perceive, to awaken, to comprehend, to make conscious
meanings.Hindi: chetana lana, aavagat karana, jnana karana

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhan' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and carries the meaning of producing grain, yielding wealth, or generating prosperity. Being in the 10th class, it intrinsically takes the affix 'nic' (forming dhanayati/dhanayate). When used in Parasmaipada, the action generally produces wealth or fruits outwardly, while in Atmanepada, the fruit or benefit of the prosperity is retained by the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi-pratyaya (nic) + Parasmaipada lat lakara (kartari prayoga)
scenarios.example_english: The fertile field yields abundant grain.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi-pratyaya (nic) + Atmanepada lat lakara (kartrabhipraya phala)

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'pura purane' belongs to the Curadi group where the nic pratyaya is inherent (svartha). It operates transitively (sakarmaka) across both padas, signifying completeness or filling up.

meanings.English: to fill, to complete, to satisfy

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kath' means to narrate, tell, or recite a connected speech or story. Because it belongs to the 10th class (Curadi Gana), it obligatorily takes the 'nic' affix (aya), forming the base 'kathaya-'. It takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada endings depending on whether the action or narration is performed generally or specifically directed with self-interest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti clarifies that 'katha vakyaprabandhe' belongs to Curadi gana and takes the svabhavika nic affix. The term vakyaprabandha implies the continuous and coherent arrangement of sentences into a narrative or discourse.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'katha' denotes narrating sequentially with proper context and syntax (prabandha-rupam vachanam), yielding derived nominals like katha and kathanam.

meanings.English: to narrate, to tell, to recount, to compose speech

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root śūl belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi) and expresses experiencing or causing acute, sharp, spear-like bodily pain (colic or ache). Because it belongs to Curadi, it obligatorily takes the affix 'aya' (ṇic) in its base forms, yielding śūlayati in the Parasmaipada and śūlayate in the Atmanepada.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti records 'ṣūla rujāyām' under the Curadi class. The dental ṣ transforms into palatal ś by universal sandhi. It denotes sharp, lance-like distress or disease (rujā). Being a Curadi root, it receives the svārthika ṇic suffix, taking both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada terminations.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin interprets 'śūla rujāyām' as acute agonizing pain comparable to being pierced by a trident or spear (śūla). The vritti confirms its classification within the Curadi group with regular vocalic and suffixal operations.

meanings.English: To cause sharp pain, to ache acutely, to pierce or torment

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mūtr' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi) and means 'to urinate' or 'to discharge urine'. Because it belongs to Curādi, it takes an obligatory '-aya-' affix (svārthe ṇic) in the present tense, giving standard forms like 'mūtrayati' or 'mūtrayate'.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'mūtra' is read in the Curādigaṇa in the sense of 'prasrāve' (urination). It takes the svārthika ṇic pratyaya unconditionally, leading to forms such as mūtrayati and the reduplicated aorist amūmūtrat.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin categorizes 'mūtra prasrāve' among the Curādi verbs where ṇic is added inherently without conveying an external causal agent, yielding standard present bases like mūtrayati/te.

meanings.English: to urinate, to discharge urine

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bhaj' in the Curadi class means to divide, distribute, or apportion something among people. Because it is in Curadi, it always takes the suffix 'nic' (forming bhaji-), and since it is Ubhayapada, it can take either Parasmaipada endings (bhajayati) or Atmanepada endings (bhajayate) without changing its basic sense of sharing or dividing property, portions, or food.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'bhaja' in Curadi is defined as 'bhaja vibhage' (to divide or apportion). Being Curadi, it receives svarthe nic by default. Because of the ending in consonant 'j' with penultimate vriddhi/guna forms, it forms the base 'bhaji' and takes both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada inflections yielding 'bhajayati' and 'bhajayate'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'bhaja vibhage' as a Curadi root signifying partition, distribution, or distinct separation ('prthakkaranam'). It operates transitively with set characteristics.

meanings.English: to divide, apportion, distribute, share

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'sall' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi), meaning 'to go' or 'to move'. Because it belongs to Curadi, it automatically takes the nic affix (-aya-) even in its basic sense without changing to a causative. Being Ubhayapada, it can take Parasmaipada endings (sallayati) or Atmanepada endings (sallayate) to denote movement or progression.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes 'salla gatau', affirming that the root expresses locomotion and kinetic action with svabhavika nic addition under the Curadi group.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhūp' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curādi gaṇa) and takes the mandatory affix 'ṇic' (resulting in -aya-) in its standard active usage. It conveys the action of fumigating, incensing, heating, or causing distress through heat. In active voice, it can take both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada endings.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'gun' belongs to the Curadi class, meaning it inherently takes the affix 'nic' (forming gunaya-) without changing the base to a causative meaning. In active usage, it primarily means 'to invite', 'to consult', or 'to enumerate/multiply'. In Parasmaipada, the focus is on the action directed outward (e.g., calling or inviting guests), while in Atmanepada, it can express consultation or deliberation for oneself.

vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'guna' signifies amantrana (invitation/calling) as well as abhyasa/sankhyana (multiplication/reckoning). By addition of the affix nic, the root manifests as gunayati / gunayate.

meanings.English: to invite, consult, multiply, enumerate
meanings.Hindi: nimantrita karana, paramarsha lena, guna karana
meanings.Bengali: nimantrana kara, paramarsha kara, guna kara

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛt' (commonly seen as kīrt) belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi gana) and means to praise, celebrate, or mention. Because it inherently takes the causative-like suffix 'ṇic', the vowel 'ṛ' undergoes a special change to 'īr', forming the base 'kīrtaya-'. It can take Parasmaipada endings when mentioning or singing praises objectively, or Atmanepada endings when the action reflects directly upon the speaker.

scenarios.example_english: The devotee chants the name of Hari.

scenarios.example_english: The poet celebrates the fame of the hero for himself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kṛta saṃkīrtane' is listed in Curadi gana. By the rule 'ṛta iddhatoḥ' and elongation rules specific to this base, the root vowel 'ṛ' is replaced by 'īr', producing the stem 'kīrtaya-'. It denotes the thorough vocalization, glorification, or commemoration of qualities and deeds (saṃkīrtanam guṇādinām uccāraṇam).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes that 'kṛta saṃkīrtane' signifies public recitation, praising, or proclaiming virtues. The affix ṇic applies naturally as part of the Curadi class, yielding forms like kīrtayati and kīrtayate in active usage.

meanings.English: to praise, to chant, to mention, to celebrate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varn' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes the mandatory affix 'nic' to form its base 'varnaya-'. It means to describe, depict, explain, or color. Because it is used in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada, the action can be directed outward toward an audience or reflect the speaker's own perspective.

Being an adanta root in the Curadi group, it necessarily receives the svarartha nic affix, generating stems like varnayati and varnayate across all lakaras.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini notes that 'varna' operates in the sense of 'guna-abhidhana' (mentioning qualities or attributes) and 'rupa-nidarshana' (illustrating forms or details). It forms regular curadi causal-like conjugations without an inherent external instigator.

meanings.English: to describe, to depict, to paint, to color, to praise
meanings.Hindi: varnana karna, bakhan karna, chitrita karna

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'spṛh' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curadi Gana) and takes the affix 'nic' obligatorily, meaning 'to desire', 'to long for', or 'to covet'. When taking a complement in the active voice, the desired object traditionally takes either the accusative (dvitiya) or dative (caturthi) case as taught by the special rule 'sprher ipsitah'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya + lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The deer longs for fresh grass.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-pratyaya + lan-lakara (imperfect past tense), prathama-purusha, ekavacana

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that 'sprha ipsayam' is an adanta curadi dhatu which mandatorily takes the nic pratyaya by 'satyapapasarvadhurabhyo nyac' and general curadi rules. Under the special karaka sutra 'sprher ipsitah', the entity being desired receives the sampradana संज्ञा, thus taking the fourth case (caturthi vibhakti), though second case (dvitiya) is also observed in general usage.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin states in Kshiratarangini that 'sprha' denotes intense longing or wishing (kanksayam/ipsayam). The root operates predominantly in Parasmaipada in the Curadi class, yielding forms like sprhayati, sprhayatah, sprhayanti.

meanings.English: to desire, to long for, to wish, to covet
meanings.Bengali: kamana kora, ichha kora, spriha kora

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root pār belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and carries the core meaning of 'to finish, complete, reach the other shore, or accomplish'. Because it naturally takes the nic affix (forming pāraya-), it can be used in Parasmaipada (when the focus is on the action directed outward) or Atmanepada (when the outcome is centered on oneself). In everyday language, it expresses finishing a task or being capable of accomplishing an undertaking.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bhīs' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curādi) and expresses the act of frightening, terrifying, or causing fear. Because it takes the standard Curādi suffix 'ṇic' (resulting in -ay-), it forms present-tense stems in 'bhīsaya-'. In Parasmaipada (bhīsayati), it represents actively scaring someone else, while in Ātmanepada (bhīsayate), the action is reflexive or done with self-interest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti categorizes 'bhīsa' under Curādi in the sense of fear or frightening ('bhīsa bhaye'). It receives the svārthe-ṇic affix mandatorily in primary conjugation, becoming bhīsaya-, yielding bhīsayati and bhīsayate in standard usage.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in the Kshiratarangini that 'bhīsa' indicates inducing terror or causing intimidation, taking the standard adanta curādi ṇic-vikaraṇa with seṭ characteristics in the general tenses.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'varn' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes the affix 'nic' (aya) inherently. It means to describe, portray, paint, explain, or praise. It can take either Parasmaipada or Atmanepada endings without changing its core meaning.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'man' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means 'to honor', 'to respect', or 'to venerate'. Because it automatically takes the affix 'nic' (forming the base 'manaya-'), it can be conjugated in both Parasmaipada (active endings) and Atmanepada (middle endings) without changing its core meaning of showing honor to someone.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bharj' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi) and takes the inherent causative suffix '-aya-' (svarthe nic), meaning 'to arrange', 'to plan', 'to fashion', or 'to project/formulate'. Because it is Ubhayapada, it can take Parasmaipada endings (-ti) when the action is directed outwards or generally, and Atmanepada endings (-te) when the planning or outcome is intended for oneself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'bharja parikalpane' under the Curadi-gana. It notes that the root receives the mandatory thematic affix 'nic' in the primary sense itself without altering the basic verbal action. Being set and ending in a consonant cluster, it yields forms like bharjayati and bharjayate, signifying the systematic structuring, fashioning, or planning of an object.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses the root 'bharja' under the meaning 'parikalpana' (formulating, arranging, or designing). He explains that the verbal root operates in tandem with other roots of synonymous designation in this section (like carj) to describe conceptual formation and preparation, forming standard 10th-conjugation paradigms.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'tul' means to weigh, balance, or compare items. Beloging to the 10th class (Curadi Gana), it takes the affix 'nic' (forming base 'tolaya-' or 'tulaya-') and can be used in both Parasmaipada (active focus) and Atmanepada (self-directed or reflective action).

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti glosses 'tula unmāne' as measuring weight or value using a balance. Under the Curadi classification, it receives the svarthika-nic suffix, producing the base tolayati/tolayate, denoting acts of physical weighing or metaphorical comparison and equalization.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin interprets 'tula unmāne' as weighing (parimana) and lifting/balancing to find equivalence. He confirms the forms tolayati and indicates that in certain usages of measuring against a standard, comparative evaluation is denoted.

meanings.English: to weigh, measure, balance, compare

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'chad' means to cover, conceal, or veil. Belonging to the 10th conjugation (Curadi), it inherently takes the affix 'nic' (forming chādayati or chandayati). In Parasmaipada, it conveys covering or veiling an external object. In Atmanepada, it can express covering something for oneself or reflexively.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'chada' in the Curadi class is recorded in the sense of 'samvarana' (covering, concealing, enclosing). It operates with the inherent nic pratyaya throughout all lakaras, undergoing vriddhi of the radical vowel in non-mit contexts to yield forms like chādayati and chādayate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'chada samvarane' as the action of concealing, wrapping, or sheltering. The primary characteristic in the tenth class is its affixation with 'puk' or standard nic-vowel adjustments, distinguishing it as a transitive verb indicating covering.

meanings.English: to cover, conceal, veil, shelter

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'rup' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes the mandatory 'nic' (ay) affix, forming 'rupayati' in Parasmaipada and 'rupayate' in Atmanepada. It fundamentally means to form, sculpt, dramatize, portray, or carefully observe and examine. Parasmaipada is commonly used for standard actions like dramatic enactment or forming, while Atmanepada can be used when the fruit of the depiction or reflection directly affects the agent.

The meaning denotes the shaping, representation, aesthetic delineation, or theatrical manifestation of a form.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini remarks on 'rup' as indicating the act of bringing into a visual form, shaping, or discerning ('rupakriya'). It denotes the manifestation of physical or conceptual characteristics in art and perception.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cūrṇ' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi Gana) and inherently takes the 'ṇic' (aya) affix. It primarily means to crush, grind, pulverize, or condense into smaller parts. Being an Ubhayapadi verb in modern usage, it can take either Parasmaipada endings (cūrṇayati) when the action is directed outwards, or Atmanepada endings (cūrṇayate) when the consequence of the action is focused on the agent.

As an inherent Curadi root, it compulsorily assumes the suffix 'ṇic' in Sarvadhatuka forms, producing forms like cūrṇayati and acūcūrṇat in the aorist.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes in Kshiratarangini that 'cūrṇa' implies 'saṅkṣepa' (compression/pulverization), yielding derivatives denoting flour, powder, or minute dust particles, following the standard Curadi causative-like morphological conjugation.

meanings.English: to crush, pulverize, grind, or condense

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṛp' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means 'to show compassion', 'to pity', or 'to be merciful'. In the 10th class, the affix 'ṇic' (represented as -aya-) is mandatory. It can take either Parasmaipada endings (kṛpayati) or Atmanepada endings (kṛpayate) without altering its essential meaning of extending mercy or kindness towards someone.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti analyzes 'kṛpa kṛpāyām' under the Curadi class. Because it falls in the Curadi gana, the affix 'ṇic' is applied unconditionally (svārthe ṇic), yielding the base kṛpay-. It takes both parasmaipada and atmanepada endings under standard Curadi rules.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes under 'kṛpa kṛpāyām' that the root conveys the primary sense of compassion (dayā, anukampā) and tenderness. The verbal base undergoes guna optionally in secondary derivations but retains kṛpayati / kṛpayate in Curadi conjugation.

meanings.English: to pity, to show mercy, to be compassionate

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root bhid belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and means to split, break, or divide. Since it is in Curadi, it automatically takes the affix Nic, turning the root into bhedaya. It can be used in both Parasmaipada (bhedayati) and Atmanepada (bhedayate) to describe an action of breaking or causing division.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root bhida vidarane is listed in Curadi. It takes the affix Nic by default (svarte). Due to the puganta-laghupadha rule, the short vowel i undergoes guna to e, producing the base bhedaya. As an ubhayapadi root, it conjugates as bhedayati and bhedayate in the sense of vidarana (cleaving, splitting, or separating into parts).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin explains bhida as an action of separation or tearing apart (vidarana). Operating in the Curadi class, it forms bhedayati/te, signifying tearing open, shattering, or causing dissension among entities.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣip' in the Curadi-gana inherently carries the sense of impelling, inciting, directing, or casting. Because it belongs to Curadi-gana, it obligatorily takes the 'nic' suffix (forming 'kṣepi-') and can be used in both Parasmaipada and Atmanepada. In Parasmaipada, it highlights the simple action of driving or sending something forward, whereas in Atmanepada, it can indicate that the result or motivation of the impelling action reflects back upon the agent.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curadi nic-affix, Parasmaipada, Lat-lakara, Prathama-purusha, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: He/she impels, urges, or sends forward

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes 'kṣipa preraṇe' under Curadi-gana. The affix nic is applied obligatorily under the rule 'curādibhyo ṇic'. Guna substitution applies to the ik-vowel 'i' forming 'kṣep-', yielding 'kṣepayati' and 'kṣepayate' with the meaning of driving, urging, or dispatching.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin in Kshiratarangini clarifies 'kṣipa preraṇe' as denoting motivating, impelling, or urging onward, distinguishing it semantically from the Tudadi-gana 'kṣipa prerane' which primarily focuses on physical throwing, while the Curadi counterpart emphasizes instigation and directed movement.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lakṣ' belongs to the 10th conjugation (Curādi gaṇa) and primarily signifies observing, perceiving, or marking/characterizing. Because it is in the Curādi class, it inherently takes the affix 'ṇic' (appearing as 'ay') in standard present tense conjugation. It can take both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada endings without changing its core meaning of observing, noticing, or defining.

scenarios.example_english: The scholar perceives the subtle difference.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya Dhatuvritti notes that the root 'lakṣa' is taught in the sense of 'darśanāṅkanayoḥ' (seeing, noticing, and stamping or marking). Being part of the Curādi class, the affix ṇic is applied svārthe (in its own sense) mandatorily, forming the base lakṣi-, which conjugates in both padas (lakṣayati, lakṣayate).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin glosses 'lakṣa darśanāṅkayoḥ', stating that it denotes both visual/mental cognition (darśanam/ālocanam) and distinct physical or conceptual identification/marking (aṅkanam). The resulting derived nouns like lakṣaṇa (definition, mark) directly stem from this lexical root.

meanings.English: to observe, to perceive, to mark, to define

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kṣap' belongs to the 10th class (Curādi gaṇa) and takes the affix 'ṇic' inherently, forming 'kṣapayati' or 'kṣapayate'. It primarily conveys the sense of urging, impelling, casting, throwing, or dispatching an object or person. In Parasmaipada, the focus is typically on the external direct action, while in Ātmanepada, the action may reflect back or carry an intensive self-directed motivation.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The Madhaviya notes 'kṣapa preraṇe' under the Curādi gaṇa. The root takes the non-causative intrinsic ṇic affix by default, yielding the base kṣapaya-. Being in the Curādi class, both Parasmaipada and Ātmanepada endings are applicable (Ubhayapadatva). It denotes sending, impelling, throwing, or causing movement forward.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin interprets 'kṣapa preraṇe' as denoting impulsion, throwing, and propelling (preraṇam preritir vyāpāraḥ). The short vowel remains intact before ṇic as per canonical roots of this section, forming the active stem kṣapaya-.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'ksal' belongs to the Curadi group (10th class) and means 'to wash' or 'to cleanse'. dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'put' belongs to the 10th group (Curadi gana) and means to bring together, fold, connect, or embrace. dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root kṛp belongs to the Curadi 10th conjugation class and means to be capable, to enable, or to make fit. It takes the mandatory suffix Nic (ay) throughout its non-optional conjugation. Because it is Ubhayapada, it takes Parasmaipada endings (kṛpayati / karpayati) when expressing general capacity or enabling an action, and Atmanepada endings (kṛpayate / karpayate) when the result of the competence or capacity directly relates back to the agent.

Both guṇa-strengthened forms (karpayati) and non-strengthened forms (kṛpayati) are discussed by ancient authorities based on vṛddhi-guṇa rules for adanta bases.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin defines kṛpa as sāmarthye (fitness, capability, to be adequate). The root forms present stem variants such as kṛpayati and karpayati via svārthe Nic, functioning transitively when causing competence or intransitively when indicating inherent capability.

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'laks' belongs to the 10th class (Curadi gana) and takes the suffix 'nic' (forming -aya-) inherently.
