dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'sphāṭ' means to split open, crack, or burst something apart. Think of cracking open a tough nut shell or splitting a piece of wood into two halves.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṭ-lakāra, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The woodcutter splits the log.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṅ-lakāra, prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The farmer cracked the fruit open with a stone.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Recorded in the Cāndra tradition under sphoṭanārtha, this root acts as a causative/curādi variant corresponding to the act of causing to break or split.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes the overlap between sphuṭ and allied curādi forms such as sphāṭ in parallel grammatical treatises where vidāraṇa (tearing or cleaving) is the primary sense.

meanings.English: to split, to burst open, to cleave, to crack

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'svañj' expresses the action of holding someone closely in one's arms out of love or affection, meaning 'to embrace' or 'to hug'. In common usage, it frequently takes the prefix 'pari-', forming 'pariṣvajate'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana, Ātmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The mother affectionately embraces her son.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kta-pratyaya (Past Passive Participle), Puṃliṅga, Prathamā Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The child was embraced with love by the father.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: svaji pariṣvaṅge | ātmanepadī aniṭ idit | svajate, pariṣvajate | ikāro numartho na tu lopa-nivṛttyarthaḥ | pariṣvañjakaḥ | svaṅktā | asvaṅkta | svāṅkṣīṣṭa | pariṣvaktaḥ iti kti sañjādīnāṃ viśeṣavidhinā nakāralopaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: svaji pariṣvaṅge | sañjanapariṣvañjanayoḥ sāhacaryāt svajate | upasargasthānnimittāt sasya ṣatvam | pariṣvajate | kta-pratyaye nakāra-lopaḥ pariṣvaktaḥ.

meanings.English: to embrace, to hug, to clasp affectionately

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'huḍ' means to gather, heap up, or to sink/submerge. When people or objects are brought together into a single cluster or when an object is dipped under water, this root is used.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The farmer collects the grains together.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Luṅ (Aorist Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The aquatic creatures submerged into the water.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: huḍa saṃghāte nimajjane ca | candradhātau saṃghātārthe nimajjanārthe cāsya pāṭhaḥ prasiddhaḥ | huḍati, hoḍayati, huḍitaḥ ityādayaḥ prayogāḥ sidhyanti |
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: huḍa saṃghāte | 'huḍa nimajjane' iti keṣāñcit pāṭhāntaram | saṃghātaḥ samūhīkaraṇam, nimajjanaṃ jale 'ntardhānam |

meanings.English: to collect together, to heap, to sink or submerge
meanings.Hindi: ikaṭṭhā karnā, saṅgraha karnā, ḍūbnā yā ḍubonā
meanings.Bengali: ekaṭra karā, saṃgraha karā, nimajjita karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cuṇṭ' means to make something small, to curtail, or to diminish. It is used when an object is trimmed, lessened, or reduced in size or amount.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṭ-lakāra (present tense), prathama-puruṣa (3rd person), eka-vacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The worker trims the thread to shorten it.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṅ-lakāra (imperfect past tense), prathama-puruṣa (3rd person), eka-vacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The carpenter cut down the piece of wood to make it smaller.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: cuṭi alpatve. idittvān num. cuṇṭati. alpatvaṃ hrasvīkaraṇam alpa-parimāṇatāpādanaṃ vā.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: cuṭi alpatve. idit. cuṇṭati. alpaṃ karotītyarthaḥ.

meanings.English: to make small, to diminish, to curtail, to reduce

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'dhukk' means to enter, penetrate, or possess. Think of it as walking inside a room, stepping deeply into a forest, or entering a state of full mental absorption.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Indicative), Prathama-puruṣa, Eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The young man enters the house.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Imperfect Past), Prathama-puruṣa, Eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The brave hero courageously entered the fort.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Non-Pāṇinian verbal entry 'dhukka āveśe' primarily cited in Cāndra-dhātupāṭha. While standard Pāṇinian recensions prioritize roots like 'viś' for entry, comparative lists acknowledge this root in the sense of 'praveśana' (entering/absorbing).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes variations across non-Pāṇinian systems where 'dhukk' is recognized among verbal roots signifying internal motion, permeation, or possession (āveśa).

meanings.English: to enter, to penetrate, to absorb, to possess

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'lump' belongs to the Candra school of Sanskrit grammar and means to cut, break, rob, or omit. In everyday terms, it describes actions where something is severed, fragmented, or made to disappear.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṭ-lakāra (present indicative), prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy breaks the dry branch with his hand.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṅ-lakāra (past imperfect), prathama-puruṣa, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The thief plundered the wealth of the king.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: cāndradhātupāṭhe 'lupi~ chedane' iti idid-rūpeṇa paṭhyate. idittvāt num-āgame kṛte 'lumpati' iti rūpaṁ bhavati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kṣīrasvāmī tu tudādau 'lupḷ~ chedane' ity atra cāndramatam api udāharati yatra idittvena nityam num-āgamo vidhīyate.

meanings.English: to cut, break, plunder, or elide

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'vraś' means to cut, sever, or split something into parts. Think of it as using a sharp tool to cut wood or branch.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The woodcutter cuts the branch of the tree.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The man cut the rope.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: vraśa chedane - Cāndre dhātupāṭhe chedanārthe paṭhitaḥ, sakarmakaḥ, bhvādigaṇīyaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: vraśa chedanakriyāyām - vraśc-dhātoḥ tulyārthaḥ cāndradhātuvṛttāv api draṣṭavyaḥ.

meanings.English: to cut, to sever, to split

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'skal' is used to describe the action of stumbling, faltering, or slipping while walking or acting.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The foot slips on the road.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lan-lakara (imperfect past), prathama-purusha, eka-vacana
scenarios.example_english: The child stumbled while running.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Candradhatu-pathe 'skala skhalane' iti dirgha-talavyadi-patha-bhedo 'pi vartate, ayam akarmakah parasmaipadi.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: skala skhalana-calanayo iti candrah. khakara-rahita-rupam aupadeshikam anya-sampradayeshu pragrihyate.

meanings.English: to stumble, to slip, to falter, to deviate
meanings.Bengali: thokar khaoya, pichle jaoya, khonchot khaoya

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'khamp' is used when someone or something shakes, quivers, or trembles intensely due to fear or terror. In simple sentences, it shows a living being shivering with fright.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lat (Present Tense, 3rd Person Singular, Parasmaipada)
scenarios.meaning: He or she trembles (out of fear)
scenarios.example_english: Seeing the lion, the young deer trembles with fear.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Lan (Past Tense, 3rd Person Singular, Parasmaipada)
scenarios.meaning: He or she trembled (out of fear)
scenarios.example_sanskrit: Tam tamomayam margam vilokya sa akhampat.
scenarios.example_english: Looking at that pitch-dark path, he trembled.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Not specifically listed in the standard Paninian Madhaviya-dhatuvritti under this exact aupadeshika shape; recognized in the Candradhatupatha as 'khapi gati-kampanayoh / kampane bhayat' where the id-agama and nasalization (num) yield the present stem 'khampati'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes parallel variant forms under kamp-varga roots; Candragomin classifies 'khapi' independently under the first gana to express involuntary bodily movement born from sudden fear.

meanings.English: To tremble with fear, to shiver, to quake

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'ghuṇṭ' means to cover, wrap up, conceal, or protect something from being seen. Imagine wrapping a precious gift with decorative paper or covering a box with a cloth to hide its contents—this action of covering or enclosing is expressed by 'ghuṇṭayati' or 'ghuṇṭayate'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ-lakāra (Present Tense), Prathama-puruṣa (Third Person), Ekavacana (Singular), Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The boy covers his face with a cloth.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ-lakāra (Imperfect Past Tense), Prathama-puruṣa (Third Person), Ekavacana (Singular), Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The king covered the chest of secret wealth.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: ghuṭi āvaraṇe. iditvad num. ghuṇṭayati, ghuṇṭayate. ghuṇṭayati vastreṇa gupta-vastu.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: ghuṭi āvaraṇe 'pi pathyate. iditvena num-āgame ghuṇṭeti rūpam bhavati.

meanings.English: To cover, enclose, conceal, wrap, protect by hiding
meanings.Bengali: Dhākā deoyā, gopana karā, ābṛta karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'av' primarily means to protect, foster, or look after someone. It is also famous across Sanskrit grammars for expressing twenty distinct semantic nuances, including satisfying, moving, knowing, and helping.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṭ-lakāra (Present Indicative), prathama-puruṣa (Third Person), eka-vacana (Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The righteous king always protects the citizens.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: loṭ-lakāra (Imperative Mood), prathama-puruṣa (Third Person), eka-vacana (Singular)
scenarios.example_english: May the Supreme protect both of us together.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: ava rakṣaṇa-gati-kānti-prīti-tṛpty-avagama-praveśa-śravaṇa-svāmyartha-yācana-kriyecchā-dīpty-avāpty-āliṅgana-hiṃsādāna-bhāva-vṛddhiṣu. avati, āvīt, avitā.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: ava rakṣaṇādiṣu viṃśatyartheṣu. rakṣaṇaṃ pālanam. avatīti rājā prajām.

meanings.English: to protect, guard, foster, satisfy, desire, move, please
meanings.Hindi: rakṣā karanā, pālan-poṣaṇ karanā, santuṣṭa karanā
meanings.Bengali: rakṣā karā, pālan karā, tṛpta karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'il' describes the action of urging, sending, pushing, or impelling someone or something forward.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The wind pushes the clouds far away.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The mother sent the boy towards the school.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: ila preraṇe kṣepe ca. Kavikalpadrumānusāreṇa bhvādau parasmāipadī seṭ ca pathyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: ila preraṇārthe vartate. ilati, ailat, eliṣyati iti rūpāṇi bhavanti.

meanings.English: To send, to impel, to urge, to push forward

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kel' means to play, frolic, or amuse oneself. It works just like the familiar root 'krīḍ' or 'khel', describing engaging in games, playful movement, or lighthearted recreation.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy plays with his friends in the garden.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past Tense, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The deer frolicked freely in the forest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'kel' is catalogued in non-Paninian lists such as Vopadeva's Kavikalpadruma under 'kela krīḍāyām' as an un-aspirated counterpart to 'khela' or 'khelṛ', conjugated as kelati, kelitaḥ, etc.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes the phonetic overlap among the roots 'kel', 'khel', and 'cel' under the umbrella of playful movement ('calana-krīḍanārtheṣu').

meanings.English: to play, sport, frolic, amuse oneself
meanings.Bengali: khelā karā, krīṛā karā, ānanda karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'cill' means to become loose, weak, or relaxed. Imagine a tight knot that slowly loosens up over time or a string that loses its tension; this action of slackening or loosening is expressed by the root 'cill'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat (present tense, third person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The knot becomes loose over time.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: luṅ (aorist tense, third person singular)
scenarios.example_english: The thread became slack due to the wind.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: cilla śaithilye. cillati. acillīt. cillitā. śithilībhāve 'yam vartate iti kavikalpadrumānusāreṇa jñeyam.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: cilla śaithilye akarmakaḥ seṭ parasmaipadī. śithilo bhavati ity arthaḥ.

meanings.English: to become loose, to slacken, to relax
meanings.French: se détendre, se relâcher, devenir lâche

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'jhāṭ' means to cleanse, sweep, or wipe clean. It is used when an object or surface is swept, wiped, or cleared of dust and impurities.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present Tense (Laṭ), 3rd Person Singular, Active Voice
scenarios.example_english: The attendant sweeps the courtyard of the house.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Aorist Tense (Luṅ), 3rd Person Singular, Active Voice
scenarios.example_english: The boy swept the floor thoroughly.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Noted in comparative listings of post-Paninian lexicography as a secondary root denoting 'parimārjana' (cleansing/sweeping), preserving regional onomatopoeic usage systematized by Vopadeva.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Identified among sporadic cleaning-action roots (saṃśodhana-parimārjana) popularized in late classical and eastern vyākaraṇa traditions.

meanings.English: to clean, to wipe, to sweep away

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'daṃś' means 'to bite' or 'to sting'. It describes the action of teeth or a venomous creature clamping onto someone or something.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Indicative, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_sanskrit: Kṛṣṇasarpaḥ mārge gacchantaṃ narēna dṛṣṭaḥ san tam daśati.
scenarios.example_english: The black cobra, seen by the man walking on the path, bites him.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Kta (Past Passive Participle, Puṃliṅga, Prathamā Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The boy, stung by a scorpion, cries due to severe pain.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: dasi~ daṃśane. iditvat nityam num. śasi-vaśi-ghasīnām ca ityetāvatā anupadhāyā api nakāralopaḥ. daśati, daṅkṣyati, adaṅkṣīt, daṣṭaḥ.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: dasi~ daṃśane. kavikalpadrumādi-vopadevamate dasīti paṭhitaḥ. daśati iti rūpam bhavati. daṣṭam, daṣṭvā.

meanings.English: to bite, to sting, to seize with teeth

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'phel' means to throw, toss, or move swiftly. You can use it in everyday speech whenever someone throws a ball or casts an object away.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat (present indicative), kartari prayoga, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The boy throws the ball to play.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṅ (imperfect past), kartari prayoga, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: He threw the stone far away.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: phela gatau kṣepe ca. vopadevīye kavikalpadrumakāreṇa 'phela gatau kṣepe' iti paṭhitam. phelati, phelāñcakāra, aphelīt.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: phela gatau kṣepe ca. asya prayogaḥ kavikalpadrumādiṣu gatikṣepārtheṣu dṛśyate.

meanings.English: to throw, to cast, to propel, to move

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'bhuṅg' (bhugi) means to be crooked, to bend, or to move in a curved or zig-zag path. In Vopadeva's Kavikalpadruma system, the marker 'i' indicates the insertion of a nasal sound (num-āgama), forming present tense forms like 'bhuṅgati'.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa (Third Person), Ekavacana (Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The snake moves in a zig-zag path on the road.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Luṅ (Aorist Tense), Prathama Puruṣa (Third Person), Ekavacana (Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The river curved through the middle of the forest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Non-standard variant preserved primarily in eastern lexical schools (Vopadeva). Parallel to kuṭilagati roots like bhuja-bhujyate or vṛj-varjate, treated here as an idit root (bhugi) giving penultimate nasal bhuṅgati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Identified as a secondary idit root signifying kuṭilatva (crookedness or curvature), where the anubandha 'i' commands the penultimate nasal augment yielding bhuṅgati.

meanings.English: to be crooked, to bend, to curve, to move zig-zag
meanings.Hindi: ṭeḍhā honā, kuṭil gati karnā, muṛnā
meanings.Bengali: bān̐kā haoẏā, kuṭil gati karā, bām̐kā
meanings.German: sich krümmen, krumm sein, im Zickzack bewegen

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mall' means to hold, sustain, bind tightly, or embrace closely. It describes the physical action of grasping firmly or keeping objects held together.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense, Third Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The warrior firmly grasps the enemy with anger.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past Tense, Third Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The boy held his mother's hand.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Paninian recensions omit this independent entry; recorded in non-Paninian auxiliary lists such as Vopadeva's Kavikalpadruma in the sense of dhāraṇe (holding/sustaining).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Not treated in canonical Paninian Kṣīrataraṅgiṇī, but attested across comparative non-Paninian dhātupāṭha traditions under the meaning of holding or binding.

meanings.English: To hold, sustain, grasp firmly, clasp

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'lañj' means to scold, reproach, or reprimand someone. It is used when an elder, teacher, or authority figures blame or admonish someone for an improper action.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ-lakāra (Present Indicative, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The teacher scolds the careless student.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ-lakāra (Past Imperfect, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The father scolded the untruthful son at home.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: laji bhartsane. iditvān num. lañjati, lalañja. Vopadevīye Kavikalpadrumagranthe 'laji bhartsane' iti paṭhyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: laji bhartsane tarjane ca. idit kṛtanumko lañjati iti rūpaṃ sādhyate.

meanings.English: to scold, reproach, censure, or reprimand
meanings.Chinese: zé bèi, chì zé, xùn chì

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'valg' means to leap, gallop, or jump around energetically, just like a joyful deer or a galloping horse in a field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense, Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The horse gallops swiftly in the field.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past Tense, Prathama Puruṣa, Bahuvacana)
scenarios.example_english: The deer leaped joyfully in the forest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: valga gatikutsanayoḥ. valgatīti gatau plavane ca prayujyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: valga gatau. kutsitāyāṃ gatau ullāse vā valgatirbhavati.

meanings.English: To gallop, to leap, to jump, to spring exuberantly
meanings.Kannada: Jigiyuvudu, hāruvudu, kudurēya dāpukālu hāki oḍuvudu
meanings.Bengali: Lāphāno, kholāse dāpaṭāno, ghoṛāra mata chuṭe calā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'hāṭ' means to shine, glow, or emit bright light. It is used when something looks radiant, lustrous, or brilliant like gold or the morning sun.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present tense (laṭ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: In the morning, the sun shines brightly in the sky.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Aorist past tense (luṅ lakāra, prathama puruṣa, ekavacana)
scenarios.example_english: The golden gem shone brightly under the light of the lamp.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: In the standard Pāṇinian recensions, roots like 'bhrāj' and 'bhā' predominate for the sense of shining; however, comparative lexicons document non-Pāṇinian listings where 'hāṭ' is systematically preserved.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes variant regional roots expressive of dīpti (illumination). Vopadeva in his Kavikalpadruma explicitly distinguishes 'hāṭa dīptau' as a distinct Class 1 intransitive verbal base signifying gold-like brilliance.

meanings.English: to shine, to glow, to radiate light

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The verbal root 'khurj' means to worship, revere, or praise someone with deep respect, just like honoring a teacher or offering prayers to the divine.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Curādi laṭ-lakāra (Present Tense, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The student always honors the teacher.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: khurja pūjāyām - as cited in lexical collations and tradition texts such as Vopadeva's Kavikalpadruma, signifying the act of veneration and laudatory worship.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: khurja iti pūjāstutyartheṣu - recognized in supplementary non-Paninian grammatical recensions denoting worship and respectful adoration.

meanings.English: to worship, honor, revere, praise
meanings.Hindi: pūjā karanā, sammāna karanā, stuti karanā
meanings.Bengali: pūjā karā, sammāna karā, stuti karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'guñj' means to buzz, hum, or make a low indistinct murmuring sound, just like honeybees buzzing over blooming flowers in a garden.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa (3rd Person), Ekavacana (Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The bumblebee sweetly hums among the blossoms.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past Tense), Prathama Puruṣa (3rd Person), Bahuvacana (Plural)
scenarios.example_english: All the bees buzzed together in the forest.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: In standard traditional dhātupāṭha listings, guja/guji is read under avyakte śabde. Being idit (possessing an 'i' marker in the aupadeśika code), a penult nasal (num-āgama) is inserted, producing the stem guñj- (guñjati, guñjataḥ, guñjanti).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes guja avyakte śabde as producing inarticulate sonorous reverberations (dhvani-viśeṣa), particularly descriptive of the sweet low humming of bees and resonance of bowstrings.

meanings.English: To hum, buzz, murmur indistinctly
meanings.Kannada: Jhumkāra māḍu, gunugu, jhum eṅdu śabda māḍu
meanings.Bengali: Guñjana karā, gūñje oṭhā, bhuṅbhuṅ karā

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'jharjh' means to scold, rebuke, or speak harshly to someone in order to warn or reprove them.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṭ-lakāra (Present Indicative, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The mother scolds the mischievous boy.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: luṅ-lakāra (Aorist / Simple Past, 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The officer rebuked the mistaken servant with a warning of punishment.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: The root 'jharjh' with the semantic marker 'paribhāṣaṇe' is recognized predominantly in non-Paninian compilations such as Vopadeva's Kavikalpadruma to signify vocal reproach or intimidation ('tarjana'). Paninian standard recensions often assimilate such forms under related phonological stems like 'jharjh' or 'jharjhar'.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes instances of onomatopoeic and expressive roots denoting harsh sound and censure under allied phonetic clusters; 'jharjh paribhāṣaṇe' functions to convey harsh verbal chastisement.

meanings.English: to reprove, to scold, to threaten, to censure

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kamal' means to bloom, open up, shine, or become radiant and clear, just like a lotus blossom greeting the morning sun. It is specifically cataloged in the Katantra Dhātupāṭha to express the graceful blooming of flowers or the bright expansion of pleasant feelings.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense, Third Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: In the morning, the lotus in the lake blooms with delight.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Imperfect Past Tense, Third Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: With the sunrise, the forest blossom opened and bloomed.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: kamala vikāse iti kātantradhātupāṭhe gaṇitaḥ | ayam adantaḥ curādau vā draṣṭavyaḥ | kamalayati puṣpam |
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: kamala vikāse | kātantrānurodhena vikāśārthakaḥ | kamalayate kamalayati vā |

meanings.English: To bloom, expand, brighten, become clear or joyful

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'kusum' means to blossom, flower, or bloom. In simple terms, when plants or trees produce flowers in the spring, this verb is used to describe the act of blossoming.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat-lakara (present tense), prathama-purusa (3rd person), ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The lotus plant blossoms in the forest lake during springtime.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lan-lakara (past imperfect), prathama-purusa (3rd person), ekavacana (singular)
scenarios.example_english: The tree in the garden blossomed beautifully.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Non-Paninian Curadi enumeration. The root 'kusuma' is taken in the Katantra Dhatupatha with the sense of 'prasave' (yielding flowers or blossoms). Paninian tradition primarily treats 'kusuma' as a nominal stem (pratipadika) giving derived denominative forms (namadhatu kusumayati), whereas the Katantra registers it directly among root inventories in the Curadi class with the obligatory 'nic' (or equivalent Curadi suffix).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kshirasvamin notes parallel roots under curadi-gana as svabhavika roots or kandvadi/namadhatu overlaps. In Katantra and Haimacandra, kusuma denotes 'puspodbhede prasave ca' (unfolding of flowers or blossoming).

meanings.English: To blossom, to bloom, to bring forth flowers
meanings.French: Fleurir, s epanouir, produire des fleurs

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'taruṇ' means to be youthful, to act young, or to flourish with youthful vitality. It describes growing young or displaying the energy and beauty of youth.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa (Third Person), Ekavacana (Singular)
scenarios.meaning: He/she flourishes youthfully or acts young
scenarios.example_english: In spring, the tree flourishes youthfully with fresh leaves.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past Tense), Prathama Puruṣa (Third Person), Ekavacana (Singular)
scenarios.meaning: He/she became youthful or displayed youthfulness
scenarios.example_english: Through medicine, the elder became youthful again.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: In the Mādhavīya-dhātuvṛtti, this stem is treated predominantly as a nāmadhātu derived from the nominal base 'taruṇa', whereas non-Pāṇinian recensions like the Kātantra directly enumerate it within the curādi class in the meaning of displaying youth (yauvane).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin observes that secondary curādi formations such as taruṇa (yauvane) function to denote nominal state-transitions (bhavana-kriyā), preserved systematically in independent non-Pāṇinian verbal lists.

meanings.English: to be or become youthful, to act young, to rejuvenate
meanings.Hindi: taruṇa honā, yuvāvastā ko prāpta honā, yauvana dikhānā
meanings.French: être jeune, rajeunir, fleurir de jeunesse
meanings.Chinese: nianqing, huanfa qingchun, bian de nianqing

canonical_dhatvartha: udgame phenāyane ca (in rising, foaming, frothing)

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'phen' means to foam, froth, or bubble up. Think of ocean waves breaking into white foam on a beach or milk rising and frothing when boiled. In simple terms, it describes the action of forming froth or rising in bubbles.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present tense), Prathama Puruṣa (Third person), Ekavacana (Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The milk froths up due to the heat.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṅ (Past tense), Prathama Puruṣa (Third person), Ekavacana (Singular)
scenarios.example_english: The ocean wave foamed at the shore.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Kātantra-pāṭhe 'phena udgame' iti nirdiṣṭam. Pāṇinīya-mate tu phena-śabdāt 'phenāyate' iti kyaci prayogo bahulaḥ, kintu Kātantre dhāturūpeṇaiva paṭhyate.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kātantrādi-vaiyākaraṇaiḥ phena-dhātuḥ sākṣāt gaṇe gṛhītaḥ phenana-kriyāyām.

meanings.English: to foam, to froth, to bubble up

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'mukul' means to bud, contract, or close halfway like a flower bud. Imagine a lotus blossom closing its petals in the evening or eyes closing halfway in relaxation.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Present tense (lat, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.meaning: buds / closes into a bud / contracts
scenarios.example_english: In the evening, the lotus closes into a bud.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Past tense (lan, prathama-purusha, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The pair of eyes closed halfway due to sleep.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: mukul saṃkoce iti kavyaprayogeṣu tathā katantradivṛttiṣu namadhatutvena dhatutvena ca nirdiṣṭaḥ | mukulayati kusumam ityadi prayogaḥ |
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: mukul saṃkoce | mukulībhavati mukulayati vā saṃkucitakusumavat bhavatītyarthaḥ |

meanings.English: to bud, to close into a bud, to contract
meanings.Hindi: kali khilna ya band hona, sankucita hona, mudana
meanings.Bengali: kuri howa, sankucita howa, mudita howa
meanings.French: bourgeonner, se fermer en bouton, se contracter
meanings.Chinese: jie lei, ban bi he, shou suo

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'lavan' means to become salty, to release salt efflorescence, or to exhibit salinity. It is used when an object or soil displays a saline nature or mineral salt taste.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ-lakāra (Present Tense), Prathama-puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.example_english: The soil becomes saline due to waterlogging.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Luṅ-lakāra (Aorist / Past Tense), Prathama-puruṣa, Ekavacana
scenarios.meaning: became saline / acquired a salty taste
scenarios.example_english: That water turned salty because of the alkaline mixture.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: Non-Pāṇinian specific inclusion: In the Śākaṭāyana recension, 'lavaṇa kṣāre' is listed as an un-suffixed verbal base signifying the manifestation of salinity (kṣāratva-prakāśanam), whereas standard Pāṇinian grammar often derives such verbal senses via nāmadhātu affixes like Kyaṅ (lavaṇāyate).
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: Kṣīrasvāmin notes the variation in non-Pāṇinian lists where roots like 'lavaṇa' are enumerated directly under Bhvādi to express intrinsic saline taste or transformation without mandatory denominal derivation.

meanings.English: To become saline, to taste salty, or to release salt
meanings.French: Devenir salin, prendre un goût salé
meanings.Chinese: Biàn xián, fā chū yán fēn

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'madhur' means to make something sweet, pleasant, or melodious. It is used when describing sweetening food or making speech and sounds delightful to hear.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana, Parasmaipada
scenarios.example_english: The singer makes the song melodious with his voice.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: Laṭ (Present Tense), Prathama Puruṣa, Ekavacana, Ātmanepada
scenarios.example_english: The mother sweetens the milk for herself.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: madhura mādhurye curādiḥ. madhuram karoti iti madhurayati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: madhura mādhuryasaṁyoge. svādutvāpādane vartate.

meanings.English: to sweeten, to make sweet, to make melodious or pleasant
meanings.Chinese: shǐ tián, biàn tián, shǐ yuè'ěr

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'harit' (or 'harita') is used when something turns green, becomes verdant, or takes on a greenish-yellow color. Imagine dry grass turning lush green after the first shower of rain; this transformation is described by this verb.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat (present tense, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: During the rainy season, the earth turns green.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lan (imperfect past, 3rd person singular)
scenarios.example_english: In the forest, the tree became green.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: harita varne haritibhavanam ityarthah. sakatayanaprakriyanusarena sauvrana-kandvadipathe haritayater rupasiddhih.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: harita varnakhyane. haritam acarisyati haritayati va iti sakatayanadivisistapatha-samamnayena darsitah.

meanings.English: to turn green, to become verdant, to take on a greenish-yellow colour

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root karbur means to become variegated, spotted, or multicoloured, just like autumn leaves or a peacock feather turning into a pattern of many different shades.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: laṭ-lakāra (Present Indicative, Prathama-puruṣa / 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: In spring, the forest becomes variegated with diverse flowers.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: luṅ-lakāra (Aorist / Simple Past, Prathama-puruṣa / 3rd Person Singular)
scenarios.example_english: As the leaves fell, the ground became spotted with various shades.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: karbura citre. vicitrībhāve 'sya vṛttiḥ. ayaṃ dhātuḥ śākaṭāyanādisiddhaḥ parasmaipadī seṭ ca.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: karbura citre. nānāvarṇayoge vicitrīkaraṇe vā prayujyate. karburati.

meanings.English: to be variegated, to become multicoloured or spotted
meanings.Bengali: citrabicitra haoẏā, nānā raṅe raṅgina haoẏā
meanings.French: se bigarrer, devenir tacheté ou multicolore
meanings.Chinese: biande wucai banlan, bian cheng banbo

dhaturupanandini.simple_explanation: The root 'surabh' means to perfume, to make fragrant, or to fill an environment with a pleasant, sweet aroma. It is used when an object, flower, or incense makes its surroundings smell delightful.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lat (present indicative, prathama-purusa, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The jasmine flower perfumes the entire garden.

scenarios.grammar_trigger: lan (imperfect past, prathama-purusa, eka-vacana)
scenarios.example_english: The incense made the entire temple fragrant.

vritti_extracts.madhaviya_dhatuvritti: curādau 'surabhi gandhe' iti kevalam saugandhye prayujyate. nic-pratyaye surabhayatīti rūpam prasidhyati.
vritti_extracts.kshiratarangini: 'surabhi gandhe' iti curādikanda-gaṇayoḥ paṭhitaḥ. śākaṭāyana-siddhānte 'surabhiḥ sugandhīkaraṇe' iti gaṇyate.

meanings.English: to perfume, to make fragrant, to scent
